Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: referred by nephrology due to renal function alteration.

Current disease history: patient under follow-up at nephrology for renal insufficiency. Reports that routine laboratory tests revealed anemia. Brings previous biopsy reports.

Complementary examinations: renal biopsy showing amyloid deposits in the renal parenchyma. Hepatic biopsy also demonstrating amyloid deposition in the liver.

Management: outpatient follow-up.

Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "does not hear well" and very light skin.

Current disease history: family reports that the patient has always had difficulty hearing. Brings audiometry showing neurosensory hearing loss. Family members note since early childhood that the eyebrows are white and the eyelashes are also white. They also report that the skin and hair are significantly lighter than those of all other family members, with diffuse pigmentation over the body. Denies presence of involuntary eye movements.

Physical examination: generalized hypopigmentation. Iris color intense blue, same color in both eyes, without heterochromia. Absence of nystagmus.

Ophthalmoscopy: hypopigmented retina.

translation:
Identification: Female, 34 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of visual disorder.

Main complaint: "I cannot see almost anything."

Current illness history: Reports having had significant difficulty seeing at night and in poorly lit environments for many years. Also states that she has been losing peripheral vision, leading to frequent collisions with objects and people approaching from the sides. Currently, she can only distinguish between light and dark.

Physical examination: Ophthalmological examination reveals optic disc pallor, pigmentary retinopathy, and choriocapillary atrophy.

Complementary tests: Perimetry shows concentric constriction of peripheral fields. Electroretinogram is absent.

translation:
Identification: male, 45 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: long-standing muscle weakness.

Current illness history: patient reports difficulty climbing stairs, rising from a chair, and raising arms above the head. He also reports recurrent episodes of pneumonia throughout his life, requiring medical attention. He complains of coughing.

History: according to mother's report, was a "slippery" infant who would slide off when held by the armpits. Completed education regularly and works; no intellectual disability. Previous cardiac evaluation showed no ventricular dysfunction.

Physical examination: reduced muscle strength in shoulder and pelvic girdle muscles.

translation:
Identification: male, 45 years old.

Main complaint: referred to the cardiology genetics outpatient clinic due to electrocardiographic abnormalities.

Current illness history: patient reports that a ventricular tachycardia episode was documented in a previous Holter monitoring study. Denies syncope. Denies sensation of a racing or pounding heart. Denies prior episode of cardiac arrest.

History: no report of sudden death.

Physical examination: patient in good general condition, conscious and oriented.

Complementary tests: resting ECG shows ST segment elevation and incomplete right bundle branch block. QT interval without prolongation.

findings.text: generalized convulsive seizure during febrile illness

translation:
Identification: female patient brought by mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that her daughter started walking independently much later than other children. She also states that her daughter has never spoken any words. She describes a brief episode of generalized convulsive seizure during a febrile illness, lasting only a few minutes, without recurrence on the same day and without associated central nervous system infection.

Physical examination: patient shows evident intellectual disability on assessment.

Complementary tests: proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy of the brain showing reduced cerebral creatine peak. Urinary guanidinoacetic acid decreased. Plasma guanidinoacetic acid decreased. Serum creatinine within normal limits.

Identification: female, 48 years old, accompanied by her sister, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "seizures".

Current illness history: the sister reports that the patient has had epileptic seizures since early adulthood, with intermittent occurrence. She also states that she has always had difficulty learning in school, but is able to perform daily activities independently; previous neuropsychological assessment concluded with mild intellectual disability, without moderate or severe impairment. The family notes that her speech is "slurred," sometimes difficult to understand.

Physical examination: conscious and cooperative. Dysarthria present. Gait and coordination tests show no ataxia. No dystonia; no abnormal postures of trunk or limbs.

Complementary tests: cerebrospinal fluid brought by the family shows low glucose level.

findings.text: episodes of strong and rapid heart beating
reduced muscle strength on cervical flexion
TGO (AST) above upper limit of normality

absent: family history of previous loss of mental abilities
translation:
Identification: female, 25 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "racing heart".

Current illness history: Patient reports episodes in which she feels her heart beating strongly and rapidly, without a clear triggering factor. Family members deny any previous loss of mental abilities, such as memory or reasoning.

Physical examination: Reduced muscle strength on cervical flexion. Bilateral atrophy of the thenar muscles.

Complementary tests: CK elevated. DHL increased. TGO (AST) above the upper limit of normality.

findings.text: difficulty remembering names of people and objects
ability to describe but not recall word
inability to understand what is happening around

translation:
Identification: 56-year-old patient brought by a family member for evaluation in a neurology outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: progressive "forgetting".

Current illness history: Family reports that the patient has progressively begun to forget names, dates, and recent appointments, with gradual worsening. The patient also reports difficulty remembering the names of people and objects, being able to describe them but unable to recall the word. There are episodes during which the patient becomes disoriented, with disorganized thinking and inability to understand what is happening around. Currently, the patient requires assistance with bathing, dressing, and housekeeping. Family also describes episodes of generalized convulsive seizures since the beginning, with loss of consciousness, and rapid, involuntary jerks in the limbs.

History: Previous diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, referred for follow-up.

Physical examination: Patient with established dementia. Myoclonic movements are observed during the examination.

findings.text: delayed adaptation from dark to bright environment
delayed adaptation from bright to dark environment

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of visual complaints.

Main complaint: "discomfort with brightness."

Current illness history: Patient reports that strong light causes discomfort and even pain in the eyes, requiring the use of dark glasses or avoidance of highly illuminated environments. Also reports difficulty seeing moving objects, such as a ball being thrown or cars passing on the street. States that it takes a long time to adapt when transitioning from a dark to a bright environment or vice versa, remaining with poor vision for a period until adaptation occurs.

Physical examination: Reduced visual acuity bilaterally. Ocular movements without nystagmus.

findings.text: juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine
curved nails resembling a clock's glass

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: nosebleeds.

Current illness history: family history reports recurrent episodes of nosebleeds. Patient also reports episodes of seizures. Denies prior cerebrovascular accident.

History: prior colonoscopy and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed multiple juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine, as documented in the pathological anatomy report. No anemia detected in prior laboratory evaluations.

Physical examination: fingers with enlarged and rounded tips, with curved nails resembling a clock's glass. No telangiectasias observed in skin, lips, tongue, or mucous membranes.

Complementary tests: abdominal imaging revealed hepatic arteriovenous malformation.

findings.text: delay in holding up the head
lack of interaction or play compared to peers
head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex
decreased resistance to passive movement of the limbs
iso-electric pattern type I on ferritin electrophoresis

translation:
Identification: female patient brought by mother for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "delay in development".

Current disease history: mother reports that the child delayed in holding up the head, sitting, and babbling, and still does not interact or play like other children of the same age. She also reports episodes in which the child has a fixed gaze and experiences tremors in the arms and legs, lasting only a few minutes and resolving spontaneously.

Prenatal history: mother denies any reduction in fetal movements during pregnancy. No evidence of immune hydrops fetalis.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Child appears "floppy" during handling, with decreased resistance to passive movement of the limbs. Abdomen: hepatomegaly palpable.

Complementary tests: ferritin electrophoresis shows iso-electric pattern type I.

Identification: Female, 40 years old, attended genetic medicine consultation referred by orthopedics for evaluation.

Main complaint: Back pain.

Current disease history: Patient reports long-standing back pain that interferes with daily activities. States that she has always been the shortest in her family and notes that her trunk is shorter in relation to her arms and legs.

Physical examination: Disproportionate short stature, with a short trunk and limbs of normal length.

Complementary tests: X-rays of the spine brought by the patient show hemivertebrae and fusion of adjacent vertebral bodies.

Identification: female patient brought by mother for evaluation in medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for assessment of physical features.

Current illness history: mother noticed that one of her daughter's eyes "turns outward" occasionally, especially when the child is tired. She also reports that her daughter has always had sparse eyebrows with few hairs. Denies that the child has difficulty hearing; no complaint of conductive hearing loss.

Physical examination: rounded face. High forehead, without low frontal hair implantation. Sparse upper eyelashes. Iridial without bilateral coloboma. Nasal openings without anteversion. Smooth nasal floor, without deep nasal floor. Thin upper lip vermilion. Hands with broad thumbs, poorly developed thenar eminence, and reduced hypotenar eminence. Feet with low longitudinal plantar arch and long hallux.

findings.text: feeling of heart beating strongly and rapidly in the chest
feeling as if about to faint
short QT interval on resting ECG
mild reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction on echocardiogram

absent: prior episode of sudden cardiac arrest requiring resuscitation
paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in previous monitoring
translation:
Identification: male, 35 years old, referred to the cardiology genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "heart racing".

Current illness history: Patient reports episodes in which he feels his heart beating strongly and rapidly in the chest. He also describes episodes of feeling as if he is about to faint, with visual blurring and weakness, without actually losing consciousness. There is no prior record of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in previous monitoring.

History: No previous episode of sudden cardiac arrest requiring resuscitation.

Complementary tests: Resting ECG shows a short QT interval. Echocardiogram brought by the patient shows a mild reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction.

findings.text: severe infection requiring hospitalization due to cytomegalovirus
reduced lymphocyte transformation response to phytohemagglutinin
increased proportion of gamma-delta T lymphocytes

absent: severe infection requiring hospitalization due to cytomegalovirus
translation:
Identification: 1 year and 1 month old patient, brought by mother, referred to the pediatric immunology outpatient clinic for investigation.

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child has had multiple episodes of bronchiolitis, more frequent and more severe than in the siblings and other children in the daycare. She also reports a severe infection requiring hospitalization due to cytomegalovirus. The child has previously been diagnosed with autoimmune hemolytic anemia during hospital follow-up.

Physical examination: Enlarged liver and spleen on abdominal palpation.

Complementary tests: C3 complement level is elevated. Hemogram shows no eosinophilia and no lymphopenia. No evidence of autoimmune neutropenia. Immunophenotyping reveals an increased proportion of gamma-delta T lymphocytes. Lymphocyte transformation test shows a reduced response to phytohemagglutinin.

findings.text: spontaneous amputation of distal phalanges of some fingers
open wounds at the tips of toes and fingers
nail pulling and biting habit causing injury
reduced amplitude of sensory action potentials
demyelination without formation of onion bulbs at the basal lamina

translation:
Identification: male, 39 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of present illness: reports that for many years he has not felt pain when injured, perceiving injuries only upon seeing them. States that he has open wounds at the tips of his toes and fingers, with poor healing. States that he has lost parts of some fingers, which have detached spontaneously over time. His wife observes that he has an uncontrollable habit of pulling and biting his own nails, causing injury. Denies absence of sweating and denies excessive sweating.

Physical examination: hypoesthesia in hands and feet, predominantly distal. Deep reflexes globally hypoactive. Ulcers at the distal digits. Spontaneous amputation of distal phalanges of some fingers.

Complementary tests: Nerve conduction study (ENMG) showing reduced amplitude of sensory action potentials. Nerve sural biopsy revealing reduced number of myelinated fibers and demyelination, without formation of onion bulbs at the basal lamina.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD at birth

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, accompanied by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by her pediatrician for evaluation.

Main complaint: "difficulty learning."

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always had difficulty learning and performing daily activities compared to other children of the same age. Neuropsychological assessment using standardized tests revealed intellectual disability. She states that at birth, she was informed that the child's head was small; maternal records confirm a head circumference below -2 SD at birth.

Physical examination: microcephaly since birth, as documented in records. On profile inspection, the forehead is markedly tilted backward.

Management: return for follow-up.

findings.text: red, irritated eyes with a sensation of sand

translation:
Identification: male, 22 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: follow-up for an endocrine disorder and recurrent infections.

Current illness history: patient reports having recurrent fungal infections since childhood, which recur even after resolution. He has been followed by endocrinology for hypoparathyroidism. He also reports red, irritated eyes with a sensation of sand, evaluated by ophthalmology, which described keratoconjunctivitis. According to ophthalmological assessment, there is no cataract. In endocrinological follow-up, primary adrenal insufficiency was ruled out.

Physical examination: patient in good general condition, cooperative.

findings.text: thick greasy layer at birth resembling whitish varnish

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of skin and hair abnormalities.

Main complaint: scaly skin and fragile hair.

Current disease history: the family reports that at birth, the skin was covered by a thick, greasy layer, resembling a whitish varnish, which later shed. Since then, the skin has remained dry and scaly. The caregivers report frequent itching over the body. They note that the hair is thin, lacks shine, and breaks easily when combed. They also report that the patient is uncomfortable in bright light and closes their eyes in bright environments. There is no reported decrease in sweating.

Physical examination: generalized ichthyosis. Curly hair. Conical-shaped teeth. Unchanged nails. Ocular examination: corneal opacity; no inflammatory signs in the eyelids; absence of pterygium.

Complementary tests: trichoscopy with hair shaft microscopy showing tortuous hairs.

findings.text: no appearance of hands directly attached to the trunk

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of upper limb malformations and cardiac disease.

Main complaint: "arms are different and heart problem".

Current illness history: the family has noticed since birth that the upper arms are shorter. They bring a previously performed echocardiogram.

Physical examination: upper limbs present, with hands implanted in the forearm, no appearance of hands directly attached to the trunk; no absence of upper limb. Bilateral brachial segment shortened.

Complementary tests: radiograph of upper limbs shows absence of radius and ulna short; this is not merely a case of hypoplastic radius. Echocardiogram reveals atrioventricular canal (AVC) and common atrioventricular canal (CIA), with no patent foramen ovale and no total atrioventricular septal defect.

findings.text: frequent forgetfulness of names and appointments
inability to organize or plan daily tasks

translation:
Identification: male, 43 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: difficulty walking.

Current illness history: Patient attended by his wife, who reports that he has started walking in an uncoordinated and unstable manner. The wife notes that he frequently forgets names and appointments, and that he is no longer able to organize or plan daily tasks, leaving them unfinished. No involuntary urinary incontinence.

Physical examination: Slurred speech with poor word articulation. Supranuclear oculomotor paralysis, with preserved reflex eye movements. Nystagmus present. Muscle strength preserved in all four limbs. Spasticity in the lower limbs, with hyperreflexia of patellar and Achilles reflexes; upper limb reflexes normal, without hyperreflexia. Babinski sign present. Index-to-nose and heel-to-knee tests show dysmetria and movement breakdown. Gait altered.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI showing cerebellar atrophy. Somatosensory evoked potentials without abnormalities.

findings.text: shortening of the midsegments of the limbs (forearms and legs)
testes in the scrotal sac bilaterally

absent: absence of teeth in the dental arch
translation:
Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: the mother reports that the child has always been the shortest in his class, significantly shorter than the other children. She also notes that his head has always appeared large and that his forehead is prominently protruding. She further observes that the fingers of his hands and feet are short. She states that his gums are thick and project over the teeth.

History: previously diagnosed ventricular septal defect by cardiology.

Physical examination: short stature. Macrocephaly. Hypertelorism. Longitudinal palpebral fissures. Short nose with anteverted nares. Oral cavity with dental crowding; no absence of teeth in the dental arch. Shortening of the midsegments of the limbs (forearms and legs). Male genitalia with micropenis; testes in the scrotal sac bilaterally.

findings.text: feet turned inward and downward at birth
short fifth fingers curved toward fourth finger bilaterally

translation:
Identification: girl, 1 year and 7 months old, brought by mother, referred to pediatric genetics for evaluation.

Main complaint: recurrent urinary infections.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has already experienced several episodes of urinary infection. She also reports that the girl has difficulty and infrequent bowel movements, often going several days without defecating. Followed by pediatric urology with diagnosis of neurogenic bladder.

History: mother reports that the girl was born with feet turned inward and downward.

Physical examination: hands with short fifth fingers curved toward the fourth finger, bilaterally; short thumbs. Flat feet; short halluces.

Complementary tests: voiding cystourethrogram with vesicoureteral reflux. Lumbar-sacral spine MRI showing tethered spinal cord and filum terminale lipoma. Gynecological assessment with longitudinal vaginal septum and bicornuate uterus.

findings.text: worsening vision when reading and recognizing faces
reduced visual acuity in both eyes
retinal pigmentation in spiculated bone-like patterns in the mid-periphery

translation:
Identification: Female, 35 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for ophthalmological evaluation.

Main complaint: "I cannot see at night."

Current illness history: Patient reports significant difficulty seeing in dark or low-light environments, requiring assistance to walk at night. She also states that her visual field has been narrowing over the years, leading to bumping into objects beside her. She additionally notes that her vision has worsened when reading and recognizing faces.

Physical examination: Reduced visual acuity in both eyes. Fundoscopy: retinal pigmentation in spiculated bone-like patterns in the mid-periphery, with diffuse arteriolar and venular narrowing.

Complementary tests: Electroretinography shows present responses, not extinguished.

findings.text: one knee crossing the other at each step

absent: rigidity on passive range of motion
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought for evaluation in the neurology outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: difficulty walking.

Current illness history: family reports that he walks with his legs widely apart, with knees colliding and sometimes one knee crossing the other at each step. He also states that he was born with twisted feet, turned inward and downward. Family members deny any monotone speech or loss of intonation.

Physical examination: facial expression and mimicry preserved, without hypomimia. No rigidity on passive range of motion of the limbs. Movements performed at appropriate speed, without bradykinesia. No parkinsonian picture present. Deep tendon reflexes globally hyperactive. Babinski sign present. Congenital foot deformity observed.

findings.text: need for handrail support when climbing stairs
fatigue when standing for long periods
need to lean for support when standing
proximal predominance weakness in all four limbs
increased caliber variation of muscle fibers
increased internalized nuclei in muscle fibers

translation:
Identification: Female, 57 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of weakness.

Main complaint: "Difficulty climbing stairs."

Current illness history: Patient reports having significant difficulty climbing stairs, requiring support on the handrail. She also states that she cannot stand for long periods without becoming fatigued and needing to lean for support. Her daughter, who accompanies her, notes that she walks with a side-to-side pelvic rocking motion.

Physical examination: Proximal predominance weakness in all four limbs. Weakness of cervical flexor muscles. No facial muscle weakness. Deep tendon reflexes globally hypoactive.

Complementary tests: Serum creatine kinase elevated. Muscle biopsy: fibers with increased caliber variation, marginated vacuoles, increased internalized nuclei, and angular fibers.

findings.text: red, warm, and swollen skin treated as cellulitis
red lesions in the elbow and knee creases

translation:
Identification: girl, 6 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: recurrent infections.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has had infections since early childhood: frequent otitis with ear pain several times per year, along with colds, throat pain, and sinusitis that recur frequently. She also reports recurrent viral infections. The child has had several episodes of pneumonia throughout life. She reports having a mouth ulcer that recurs repeatedly, and blistering lesions on the lips that reappear multiple times. She had one episode of red, warm, and swollen skin, treated as cellulitis. No mastoiditis. No keratitis. No asthma attacks and no recurrent bronchitis.

History: allergy to cow's milk protein and egg allergy. No drug allergy. Since infancy, has had dry skin with intense itching and red lesions in the elbow and knee creases. Mother notes that the child has always been smaller than other children and grows slowly.

Physical examination: growth delay. High forehead.

findings.text: thick redness of the upper lip

absent: extra digit on the ulnar side of hands
extra digit on the lateral side of feet
no need for third-party assistance for daily activities
translation:
Identification: male patient, 34 years old, brought by his sister for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for etiological investigation.

Current disease history: the sister reports that he has always been frequently ill, with recurrent infections occurring several times per year. Followed up in ophthalmology, with report of rod-cone dystrophy. Presents severe intellectual disability, requiring third-party assistance for daily activities.

History: according to the family, the pregnancy progressed without increased amniotic fluid.

Physical examination: head circumference within the expected range for age and sex, without microcephaly and without macrocephaly. Low-set ears. Thick redness of the upper lip. Hands without extra digit on the ulnar side; feet without extra digit on the lateral side.

Complementary tests: brain MRI showing cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and molar tooth sign.

findings.text: white reflection in the pupil on photographs
white retrolental mass of pseudoglioma type

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "repeated fractures and vision problems."

Current illness history: Patient reports that since childhood he has had easy bone fractures, with multiple fractures throughout his life. He states that he has always had poor vision. His mother recalls that, when he was young, she noticed a white reflection in the pupil on photographs. Patient denies any school or learning difficulties, with adequate cognitive development.

Physical examination: Short stature. Spine with lateral deviation associated with increased dorsal curvature. Preserved muscle tone. Joints without excessive range of motion. Small-eyed appearance. Leukocoria. Reduced visual acuity.

Complementary tests: Ophthalmological evaluation with retinal detachment, a white retrolental mass of pseudoglioma type, and persistent hyaloid vasculature; transparent lens, without opacities. X-rays of the spine showing flattened vertebrae and vertebral compression fractures. Long bones of normal diameter, without tapering. Bone density measurement showing reduced bone mineral density.

findings.text: multiple fractures during childhood following minor traumas
prominent eyes projected forward from facial plane
deficient tubular modeling of long bones
bone density scan T-score between -1 and -2.5

translation:
Identification: boy, 12 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "breaks bones easily."

Current disease history: mother reports that the child has had multiple fractures during childhood, repeatedly, following minor traumas. She states that he took longer than his siblings to sit, crawl, and walk. Denies fractures identified at birth or on prenatal ultrasounds.

Physical examination: prominent eyes, projected forward from the facial plane. Occipital region flattened. Thorax narrow in lateral diameter. Bilateral flat feet, with longitudinal arch supported on the ground in orthostasis.

Complementary tests: bone density scan with T-score between -1 and - 2.5, not reaching the osteoporosis range. X-rays show widened diaphyses of long bones, with deficient tubular modeling. Spine shows no vertebral compression fractures.

Identification: girl, 10 years and 4 months, brought by mother, referred to the neuromuscular outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: weakness when climbing stairs and rising from the floor.

Current illness history: mother reports that the girl has always been "floppy" since infancy and only began walking properly after the other children in the family. Currently, she has difficulty rising from the floor, climbing stairs, and raising her arms above her head. She also noticed that her arms and legs are thin, "without muscle."

Physical examination: global hypotonia. Muscle weakness predominantly proximal, involving scapular and pelvic girdles. Diffuse amyotrophy. Contractures in elbows, knees, and ankles. Hypermobility of hand finger joints. Normal finger length. Normal palatal height. Normal neck length. No valgus deformity of the rear foot.

Complementary tests: serum creatine kinase within normal limits. Muscle biopsy: increased fiber diameter, increased number of fibers with central nuclei, foci of fiber necrosis, and increased endomysial connective tissue.

findings.text: hard projections on each side of the nose

translation:
Identification: male patient, 43 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "nose always blocked".

Current illness history: patient reports having had difficulty breathing through the nose since childhood. He brought a previous otolaryngological evaluation with nasofibroscopy, which revealed bilateral narrowing of the nasal passages. He also reports having noticed, over the years, hard projections on each side of the nose.

Physical examination: eyes well separated upon inspection, with increased interpupillary distance. On palpation, bilateral paranasal bony bulging, with a petrous consistency.

Complementary tests: cranial CT scan brought by the patient shows hyperostosis of the cranial vault.

findings.text: marry for years with unsuccessful conception
serum IGF-1 level below lower limit of normality
markedly reduced penile size for age

translation:
Identification: male, 36 years old, accompanied by sister.

Main complaint: referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Current disease history: Patient and sister report that he has been experiencing progressive hair loss for years, with areas of thinning on the scalp. The sister noticed that he has started closing his eyes forcefully several times a day, without being able to control it, as if his eyelids "locked up". Married for years, the couple has been trying to conceive without success. No hearing loss. No sudden muscle jerks. No tingling, numbness, or weakness in hands and feet.

History: intellectual disability since childhood, with daily activities requiring support. Under ongoing treatment for hypothyroidism. Previous diagnosis of hypogonadism. No history of diabetes.

Physical examination: diffuse alopecia on scalp. Blepharospasm observed during consultation. Penile size markedly reduced for age.

Complementary tests: spermogram showing absence of spermatozoa even after centrifugation. Serum IGF--1 level below the lower limit of normality.

findings.text: short upper limbs due to osteoskeletal underdevelopment
no granular layer visible in the epidermis

translation:
Identification: patient referred for evaluation in medical genetics; sex and age not specified.

History: during pregnancy, the mother reports that she felt the baby moving significantly less than expected.

Physical examination: cleft oral fissure. Eyes of reduced size (microphthalmia). Abnormal nasal shape. Thin skin. Absence of cranial bone ossification. Underdeveloped musculature. Short upper limbs due to osteoskeletal underdevelopment, as well as lower limbs. Omphalocele.

Complementary tests: cranial imaging shows intracranial cystic lesion. Both lungs have three lobes. Skin biopsy shows no granular layer visible in the epidermis. No kidney in the pelvis. No congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Echocardiogram shows no tetralogy of Fallot.

Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: assessment of osteoarticular alterations.

Current disease history: patient reports long-standing joint pain; previous imaging studies brought to the consultation show osteoarthritis and degenerative discopathy. Also, imaging reveals osteochondral fragmentation. Patient reports having been diagnosed in childhood with premature closure of cranial sutures.

History: denies hiatal hernia.

Physical examination: thorax with sunken sternum. Nose without increased projection of the tip. Spine without lateral deviation.

Complementary tests: aortography without aneurysm. Cerebral angiography without cerebral artery dilation.

findings.text: eyes not looking in the same direction
aneurysmal dilation of the aortic root

translation:
Identification: girl, 7 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatric cardiology for genetic evaluation.

Current illness history: mother reports that since infancy, the child has been "floppy", with a soft body when carried. She also notes that the girl's eyes "do not look in the same direction". She states that the child has never had difficulty seeing at a distance. The child is followed by a cardiologist for interatrial communication and persistent arterial duct.

Physical examination: eyes well separated, without eye deviation. Nasal bridge without flattening. Normal length of the nasal bridge. High palate; bifid uvula. Thorax with sternum depression. Long and slender fingers of the hands. Feet with inwardly deviated anterior foot; no congenital foot deformity. Global hypotonia on examination.

Complementary tests: echocardiogram showing aortic insufficiency and aneurysmal dilation of the aortic root. Angiography revealing tortuosity of the carotid arteries.

findings.text: muscle pains in legs and arms
lack of strength for daily activities
severe muscle pain after physical education
fainting with brief loss of consciousness
spontaneous recovery from loss of consciousness
generalized convulsive seizure with tremors in all four limbs
proximal muscle weakness in upper and lower limbs
muscle fiber atrophy in type 2 fibers

absent: no muscle pain after physical activity
translation:
Identification: female patient, 11 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: fatigue and muscle pains in legs and arms.

Current disease history: mother reports that the girl has been complaining of generalized body weakness and lack of strength for daily activities. She describes frequent muscle pains in the limbs, without specific localization, and that after playing or physical education, the child experiences severe muscle pain. She states that the child has already fainted several times, losing consciousness for a brief period and regaining normal consciousness spontaneously. There was also a previous episode of generalized convulsive seizure with tremors in all four limbs. There is a report of a previously reversed sudden unexpected death. Low blood glucose episodes have already been documented.

Physical examination: proximal muscle weakness in upper and lower limbs. Bilateral limitation of ankle dorsiflexion.

Complementary tests: ischemic exercise test of the forearm without lactate elevation. Muscle biopsy showing type 2 fiber atrophy, reduced muscular glycogen content, and fatty substitution of skeletal muscle.

findings.text: diminished vibration sensation in distal parts of limbs
slow pursuit eye movements without saccadic intrusions

absent: dysmetria in index-nose and heel-knee tests
normal vibration sensation in distal parts of limbs
translation:
Identification: female patient, 18 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "weakness in the legs and arms."

Current illness history: the patient reports experiencing progressive muscle weakness, with increasing difficulty performing daily activities. The mother, who is accompanying her, has noticed that her daughter's hands and legs have become thinner over time.

Physical examination: increased tone, with spasticity in the limbs. Patellar and Achilles reflexes are hyperactive bilaterally. Babinski sign is present. Vibration sensation is diminished in the distal parts of the limbs. Hypoalgesia on needle test. Slow pursuit eye movements without saccadic intrusions. Index-nose and heel-knee tests show no dysmetria.

findings.text: difficulty recognizing faces at a distance
horizontal corneal diameter at 13 mm or more
peripheral amber-halo adjacent to the limbus
clear corneal band separating peripheral amber-halo from limbus
polygonal mosaic opacities in the central corneal stroma

translation:
Identification: male patient, 72 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by ophthalmology for evaluation.

Main complaint: "difficulty seeing".

Current illness history: patient reports noticing progressive worsening of vision, with difficulty reading and recognizing faces at a distance.

Ophthalmological physical examination: reduced visual acuity. Horizontal corneal diameter increased, at 13 mm or more, with transparent cornea. Peripheral amber-halo adjacent to the limbus, separated from it by a clear corneal band, in both eyes. On biomicroscopy, deep anterior chamber and iridial transillumination defects. Polygonal mosaic opacities in the central corneal stroma.

Complementary tests: pachymetry showing decreased corneal thickness.

findings.text: reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes relative to CD3+ lymphocytes
diminished lymphocyte transformation response to phytohemagglutinin

translation:
Identification: female infant, 6 months of age, brought by mother, referred to pediatric immunology outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "canker that does not heal."

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has recurrent episodes of oral candidiasis and diaper candidiasis, which improve only to return shortly thereafter. She also states that her daughter "does not grow," becoming progressively smaller than other children of the same age since birth.

Physical examination: poor postnatal weight-height gain. Abdomen: enlarged liver palpable, approximately several centimeters below the right costal margin; enlarged spleen palpable below the left costal margin.

Complementary tests: serum immunoglobulins showing low IgG and low IgA for age; IgM without reduction. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping with reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes relative to CD3+ lymphocytes. Lymphocyte transformation test with diminished response to phytohemagglutinin.

findings.text: liquid bowel movements several times a day

translation:
Identification: Female, 56 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "I have been losing weight and have had loose intestines for a long time."

Current illness history: Patient reports progressive weight loss, noticing that her clothes are becoming increasingly loose. She also reports having liquid bowel movements several times a day, which have persisted for several months without improvement.

Complementary tests: Bring results of peripheral nerve biopsy showing amyloid deposits in the nerve.

Management: Outpatient follow-up.

findings.text: pink-to-whitish skin markings in lumbar region and thighs

translation:
Identification: male, 32 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

History of present illness: patient reports that he has always been the tallest in his class. He states that since childhood, he has been able to bend his joints beyond normal limits. He reports noticing skin markings, initially pink and later whitish, in the lumbar region and thighs. He states that he underwent inguinal hernia surgery.

Physical examination: tall stature. Palpebral fissures with downward slant; no hypertelorism. High palate. Mandible positioned posteriorly. Sternum deformity. Long and slender fingers of the hands. Skin without increased softness on palpation. Scoliosis observed during spinal examination. Flat feet bilaterally, without congenital foot deformity.

Complementary tests: echocardiogram showing mitral valve prolapse and aortic root aneurysm. MRI of the lumbar-sacral spine without dural ectasia and without Tarlov cysts.

findings.text: long periods arranging objects in a line
low valine in plasma amino acids
low leucine in plasma amino acids
low isoleucine in plasma amino acids

absent: seizure recurrence on the same day
translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: developmental delay and seizures.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has been delayed in reaching developmental milestones across all domains, consistently behind other children of the same age. She states that the boy sat and walked significantly later than expected. She notes that the child rarely looks at people's eyes, does not play with other children, spends long periods arranging objects in a line, and repeatedly performs the same hand movements. There was a brief, whole-body episode of shaking during a fever, lasting only a few minutes and not recurring on the same day. Subsequently, the child developed seizures without fever, characterized by loss of consciousness and whole-body shaking, which have occurred since the beginning.

Physical examination: head circumference appropriate for age, no microcephaly. Cognitive assessment reveals intellectual disability.

Complementary tests: EEG shows epileptiform activity interictally. Plasma amino acids show low valine, low leucine, and low isoleucine.

findings.text: rigid episodes with shaking of arms and legs
lack of energy to play or complete school tasks
increased citrulline in plasma amino acids

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics to genetic medicine outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "seizures and extreme fatigue".

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child has had episodes in which she became rigid, with shaking of arms and legs, and did not respond for several minutes. She also states that, during some periods, the child becomes very still, slow, and lacks energy to play or complete school tasks, although she says she wants to do so. The child also complains of abdominal pain on some days.

Complementary tests: Brought from prior hospitalization: elevated plasma ammonia. Plasma amino acids with increased citrulline.

findings.text: serum uric acid above reference value

translation:
Identification: male, 21 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: renal function alteration in follow-up.

Current disease history: patient attended accompanied by mother, bringing a nephrology report indicating chronic kidney disease in follow-up. Bringing recent laboratory tests.

Complementary exams: serum uric acid above reference value. Elevated serum creatinine. Renal ultrasound without renal cysts.

Identification: male, 16 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: "he is much shorter than his peers."

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always been the shortest in his class, with stature significantly below that of peers of the same age. She also notes that, since early childhood, his upper eyelids have drooped over the eyes. She states that he sat, walked, and spoke at the expected age, with no developmental delay. He is currently attending regular school level, without learning difficulties, and there is no intellectual disability.

Physical examination: short stature. Ptosis of the upper eyelids. Hypertelorism. Short nose with anteverted nares. High palate, without cleft palate. No cleft lip. Micrognathia. Genitalia: scrotal sac encompasses the base of the penis above, with implantation above it; testes palpable bilaterally, without cryptorchidism. Feet: forefeet turned inward, with adducted metatarsals.

findings.text: large head in relation to body size

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation. Sex and age not specified.

Main complaint: referral due to skeletal abnormalities.

Current disease history: the family reports that the patient requires assistance to breathe, with a respiratory insufficiency presentation. Family members also noted that the feet appear too small for the body.

Physical examination: head appears large in relation to body size, although the head circumference does not exceed two standard deviations. Forehead of normal height, without frontal bossing. Low nasal bridge and short nose. Ears with low implantation. Short hand palmar creases.

Complementary tests: skeletal radiographs show shortened long bones, cup-shaped metaphyses, and delayed epiphyseal ossification.

Identification: boy, 3 years old, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric cardiology.

Main complaint: "his heart stopped."

Current illness history: parents report that the child suddenly fell unconscious, without pulse, and required resuscitation by the emergency team. During evaluation, the monitor showed ventricular fibrillation, which was reversed with defibrillation. During hospitalization, episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia were documented.

Complementary tests: 12-lead ECG with prolonged QTc, T-wave alternans, and second-degree AV block 2:1.

Management: counseling to the family and coordinated follow-up with cardiology.

findings.text: variable platelet sizes on peripheral blood smear

translation:
Identification: female patient referred to the hematology/genetics outpatient clinic for investigation of abnormal hemogram.

Main complaint: "low platelet count on blood test".

Current illness history: Patient reports that routine tests have shown reduced platelet count. Denies nasal bleeding.

Complementary tests: Hemogram with thrombocytopenia. Increased platelet volume. Peripheral blood smear showing platelets of very variable sizes. Platelet aggregation with preserved ADP response. Normal clot retraction.

findings.text: cutaneous syndactyly of fingers on hands

absent: ears without low implantation and without posterior rotation
male genitalia with bilaterally scrotal testes
translation:
Identification: boy, 1 year and 6 months, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrician due to cranial, facial, and extremity abnormalities.

Current illness history: mother reports that since early infancy, she has noticed the child's head appears "tall and short", with a prominent forehead and eyes that are "stretched out". She also observes that some fingers on hands and feet are fused by skin, and that the big toe is broad.

History: gestation without excess amniotic fluid, according to mother.

Physical examination: brachycephaly. Prominent forehead with frontal bossing. Ocular proptosis. Hypertelorism. Low nasal bridge, anteverted nares. Hypoplasia of the midface. Thin upper lip with redness. High palate. Ears without low implantation and without posterior rotation. Distance between nipples without increase. Cutaneous syndactyly of fingers on hands and cutaneous syndactyly of pododactyls. Broad halluxes. Male genitalia with bilaterally scrotal testes.

findings.text: flattened vertebral bodies with anterior projections in the form of a tongue at several levels

absent: muscle tone abnormalities in any limb
translation:
Identification: male, 31 years, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of skeletal dysplasia.

Main complaint: "curved spine".

Current disease history: patient reports that the spine has been curved to the side and forward since childhood, with progressive worsening of the kyphoscoliosis. Denies foot deformities at birth. Denies history of hip dislocation.

Physical examination: muscle tone is preserved in all four limbs. Hands show complete range of motion at all joints, without contractures.

Complementary tests: skeletal radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies with anterior projections in the form of a tongue at several levels. Hypoplastic iliac bodies. Enlarged femoral trochanters. Widened metaphyses of long bones. Femoral heads with normal morphology, without dysplasia.

findings.text: sparse eyebrows at tips near temples
delayed bone age compared to chronological age

absent: abnormal facial features other than broad forehead, globular nasal tip, long labial frenum, fine redness of upper lip, metacarpal shortening
abnormal hand or wrist radiograph findings beyond delayed bone age
translation:
Identification: girl, 4 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrician for genetic evaluation due to facial features.

Main complaint: "her hair hardly grows at all."

Current illness history: mother reports that her daughter's hair grows very slowly and requires rare haircuts. She also notes that the eyebrows are quite sparse at the tips, near the temples. She states that the child keeps up with other children of the same age in walking, speaking, and playing, without developmental delay in neuropsychomotor skills. At school, the teacher does not observe learning difficulties; no intellectual disability is present.

Physical examination: broad forehead. Globular and voluminous nasal tip. Long labial frenum. Fine redness of the upper lip. Hands with metacarpal shortening on palpation.

Complementary tests: hand and wrist radiograph showing delayed bone age compared to chronological age.

findings.text: lack of interaction with other children
cleft between helix and lobule of ear
penis length exceeding 2 standard deviations for age

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics.

Main complaint: "different way of relating".

Current illness history: parents report that the child avoids eye contact, does not play with other children, speaks little, and almost does not interact, maintains very narrow interests, and persistently repeats movements and routines, becoming irritated when changes occur. Parents deny difficulties with sucking, chewing, or swallowing.

History: shortly after birth, required respiratory support due to neonatal distress. No omphalocele was present.

Physical examination: full and rounded cheeks. Micrognathia. Ear with a cleft between the helix and the lobule. Male genitalia with a penis length exceeding 2 standard deviations for age.

findings.text: seizures with rigidity and extended arms and legs
inability to sit even with support
head drops when placed in sitting position
dystonia in limbs and trunk with maintained abnormal postures
no cerebral atrophy on brain MRI

absent: seizures that begin on one side of the body
translation:
Identification: female infant, 11 months old, brought by mother, referred for neurological evaluation.

Main complaint: seizures and developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports episodes in which the child becomes rigid and extended arms and legs, with a stiff neck, lasting for a few seconds. Denies having seizures that begin on one side of the body. States that the daughter has not yet uttered any sounds with communicative intent, as expected for her age. Also notes that she is unable to sit, even with support, and that her head "drops" when placed in a sitting position. In general, she observes developmental delay in all milestones since the first months of life.

Physical examination: global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. Poor head control. Dystonia in limbs and trunk with maintained abnormal postures. No chorea. No athetosis. No opisthotonus.

Complementary tests: EEG shows hypsarrhythmia; in another recording, seizure-suppression pattern. Brain MRI shows no cerebral atrophy.

Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by ophthalmology.

Main complaint: ocular abnormalities.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child repeatedly inserts her fingers into her eyes and squeezes them several times a day. She also notices that the child's eyes tremble, swinging back and forth continuously without stopping.

Physical examination: bilateral rhythmic involuntary eye movements. On inspection and biomicroscopy, corneas with reduced curvature, without the usual protrusion relative to the sclera, without thinning or conical deformation. Fundoscopy: retinal pigment epithelium with a mottled appearance, with areas of different pigmentation; optic discs with a pink coloration, without pallor.

Complementary tests: cycloplegic refraction reveals hyperopia, without myopia.

findings.text: cleft in the roof of the mouth
hair implantation projecting from the tongue toward the ears directed toward the cheeks

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 17 years of age, brought by mother for genetic medicine evaluation.

Main complaint: Referred by otolaryngology for assessment of facial and auditory abnormalities.

Current illness history: Mother reports that the daughter was born with an opening in the roof of the mouth. She also states that the child has always had difficulty hearing, and audiometry revealed conductive hearing loss. She adds that the girl has never had eyelashes. No prior diagnosis of hydrocephalus is reported.

Physical examination: Facial features show malar hypoplasia and micrognathia. Oblique palpebral fissures directed downward. Inferior eyelid coloboma. Abnormal auricular morphology with external auditory canal atresia. Hair implantation projecting from the tongue toward the ears, directed toward the cheeks. Nasal openings patent, without choanal atresia.

Complementary tests: Cranial CT shows no coronal, lambdoid, or sagittal suture synostosis.

findings.text: progressive difficulty breathing due to respiratory muscle weakness

translation:
Identification: Female, 68 years old, referred to the neuromuscular outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "General body weakness and fatigue."

Current illness history: Patient reports a sensation of weakness and loss of strength that accompanies her daily activities, with increasing difficulty in performing routine tasks. Her daughter noticed that her mother has started walking with a side-to-side pelvic rocking motion. Patient reports having suffered several pneumonias over the past years. She has progressively developed difficulty breathing due to respiratory muscle weakness, reaching a state of respiratory insufficiency requiring hospitalization.

Past medical history: Previous diagnosis of myopathy, currently under follow-up.

Physical examination: Generalized muscle weakness, both proximal and distal. Weakness of cervical flexor muscles. Diffuse muscular atrophy. Global areflexia. Thoracic scoliosis. No ptosis of the eyelids. Extraocular motor function preserved, without ophthalmoplegia.

findings.text: lump in the neck in the thyroid region
serum calcitonin levels above reference value

translation:
Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: referred after diagnosis of thyroid tumor.

Current disease history: patient reports having noticed a lump in the neck, in the thyroid region. Laboratory testing showed serum calcitonin levels above the reference value. Histopathological examination of the lesion revealed medullary thyroid carcinoma. Denies episodes of sudden severe hypertension.

History: no history of hyperparathyroidism. No history of pheochromocytoma.

Physical examination: palpable nodule in the thyroid.

findings.text: repetition of words and phrases without intention to converse
hair growth in widow's peak pattern

translation:
Identification: male, 21 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for etiological investigation.

Current illness history: mother reports that he delayed in sitting, walking, and in all aspects of childhood development, remaining significantly behind other children. He began speaking very late and still has limited speech; he frequently repeats words and phrases he has just heard, without intention to engage in conversation. Since early childhood, he has avoided social contact, has very narrow interests, and performs repetitive movements. He becomes very nervous and tense in the presence of changes or new situations, with excessive fear. He requires assistance for nearly all daily activities and has severe intellectual disability.

History: in childhood, he had multiple ear infections, with recurrent middle ear infections.

Physical examination: short stature. Coarse facies. Hair growth in a widow's peak pattern. Bulbous nose. Small hands with short fingers. Prominent digital pads.

Complementary tests: urinary organic acids without abnormalities; plasma amino acids within normal limits; urinary mucopolysaccharide screening negative; urinary oligosaccharides absent; serum IGF-1 within normal range.

findings.text: frequent tripping due to foot weakness
difficulty maintaining upright head position when lying down
limited extraocular motility in multiple directions
cervical flexor and extensor muscle weakness
muscle strength grade 4 in scapular and pelvic girdles
distal muscle weakness in all four limbs
increased fibers with central nuclei in muscle biopsy

absent: difficulty with head position when lying down (no)
severe muscle weakness in scapular and pelvic girdles
normal cervical flexor and extensor muscle strength
normal distal muscle strength in all four limbs
increased fibers with central nuclei in muscle biopsy
translation:
Identification: female, 35 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for investigation of a neuromuscular disorder.

Main complaint: muscle weakness.

Current illness history: patient reports difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair, as well as difficulty holding objects with her hands and frequent tripping due to foot weakness. She states that she has trouble maintaining an upright head position when lying down. Family members have noted that her eyelids droop. She ambulates independently, without loss of gait.

Physical examination: blepharoptosis present. Limited extraocular motility in multiple directions. Facial muscle weakness, with difficulty closing her eyes forcefully and whistling. Cervical flexor and extensor muscle weakness. Muscle strength grade 4 in scapular and pelvic girdles, with distal muscle weakness in all four limbs. Deep tendon reflexes globally absent. Bilateral calcaneal tendon shortening. No lumbar hyperlordosis of the spine.

Complementary tests: serum creatine kinase (CK) elevated. Muscle biopsy shows increased fibers with central nuclei.

absent: right pulmonary vein drainage to the inferior vena cava
translation:
Identification: female infant, 8 months old, brought by mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by referral from pediatrics.

Main complaint: "she is developmentally delayed for her age."

Current illness history: mother reports that the child still does not maintain proper head control, nor interacts or babble like other children of the same age, with developmental delay in all domains. She believes the girl is "a floppy baby" in the arms. She also notes that one of the eyes occasionally "diverts" to the side. Denies that the upper eyelids are ptotic.

History: previous echocardiogram revealed ventricular septal defect and coarctation of the aorta; no aortic valve stenosis, no left ventricular hypoplasia, and no right pulmonary vein drainage to the inferior vena cava. Renal and urinary tract ultrasound showed renal pelvis and ureteral duplication.

Physical examination: appropriate length for age, no short stature. Axial and appendicular hypotonia. Arched, high-arched eyebrows. Elongated palpebral fissures, with lateral lower eyelid eversion. Bluish sclerae. Strabismus. Broad nasal base. Large ears. Prominent digital pads on the fingertips. Clinodactyly of the hand fingers.

findings.text: worsening visual clarity in both eyes
dark areas without endothelial cells on specular microscopy

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "seeing progressively worse."

Current disease history: patient reports progressive difficulty with vision, with worsening visual clarity in both eyes. Previously evaluated by an ophthalmologist, who recommended genetic follow-up.

Physical examination / ophthalmological assessment: reduced visual acuity. On biomicroscopy, bilateral corneal dystrophy. Presence of Descemet's membrane posterior facets, visualized as dark areas without endothelial cells on specular microscopy.

Identification: female patient, 16 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

Main complaint: "syncope".

Current illness history: the mother reports that the daughter has already experienced episodes in which she suddenly lost consciousness, fell, and regained full awareness spontaneously within a few seconds, without becoming confused afterward.

Complementary tests: resting electrocardiogram showing sinus bradycardia. Transthoracic echocardiogram revealing mitral valve prolapse and non-compacted left ventricular myocardium.

Management: joint follow-up with cardiology.

findings.text: loose, frequent stools for many months
multiple pneumonias since first year of life
repeated episodes of bacterial infections requiring antibiotic treatment
fungal skin lesions that recur after treatment
decreased proportion of memory B cells with class switching
reduced natural killer (NK) cell count below reference value
total T lymphocytes within normal range for age

absent: abnormal lymphocyte immunophenotyping showing increased memory B cells with class switching
normal proportion of memory B cells with class switching
translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years and 8 months old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for immunological investigation.

Main complaint: recurrent infections.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has had loose, frequent stools for many months without improvement. She states that the child has had multiple pneumonias since the first year of life, as well as repeated episodes of bacterial infections requiring antibiotic treatment. She also reports that the girl "catches viruses all the time," with successive viral episodes. Since infancy, the child has had oral thrush and fungal skin lesions that recur after treatment.

History: vaccinated with BCG at birth, with no local or regional reaction after vaccination.

Complementary tests: low IgA and low IgM. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping shows reduced total B lymphocytes, decreased proportion of memory B cells with class switching, and reduced natural killer (NK) cell count below the reference value. Total T lymphocytes (CD3+) within the normal range for age, without reduction or increase; no increase in B lymphocytes.

findings.text: normal number of megakaryocytes in bone marrow

translation:
Identification: girl, 6 years and 6 months old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrician for evaluation in hematology/genetics.

Main complaint: "red spots on the skin".

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child frequently has small red-brown spots on the skin that appear easily, even without significant trauma. No nasal bleeding.

Complementary tests: Complete blood count with thrombocytopenia. Decreased platelet volume. Bone marrow examination with normal number of megakaryocytes.

findings.text: hair breaks easily when pressed against pillow
scalp with rough elevated papules centered at follicular ostia
bead-like appearance of hair shafts under trichoscopy
regularly intercalated elliptical nodes separated by narrow segments under trichoscopy

translation:
Identification: boy, 2 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in dermatology/genetics.

Main complaint: "the hair is falling out."

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child's hair has been falling out progressively, leaving bald areas on the scalp. She also states that the hairs break easily when combing or when pressed against the pillow.

Physical examination: Scalp with rough, elevated papules centered at follicular ostia, with whitish corneal plugs. Under trichoscopy, the shafts show a bead-like appearance, with regularly intercalated elliptical nodes separated by narrow segments.

findings.text: yellowish skin in first days of life
acceptance of only small volumes during feeding
rhythmic shaking of both sides of the body

translation:
Identification: girl, 6 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics.

Current illness history: mother reports that, in the first days of life, the child had yellowish skin and had great difficulty breastfeeding, refusing the breast and accepting only small volumes. The child also frequently vomited after feedings. She reports episodes in which the girl became completely rigid and then exhibited rhythmic shaking of both sides of the body. She states that the girl spoke her first words late and still speaks significantly less than other children of the same age.

Physical examination: global hypotonia.

Complementary tests: serum galactose elevated. Erythrocytic galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase activity reduced.

Identification: female patient, 64 years old, accompanied by her sister.

Main complaint: referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: the sister reports that as a child, the patient was delayed in sitting, walking, and other milestones compared to other children, and that she began speaking words and phrases much later than expected. She states that her mood changes rapidly, shifting from crying to joy over minor reasons. She experiences episodes in which she shouts, curses, and at times hits people in the house. Occasionally, she bites her own hands and hits the wall. She needs to repeat certain actions, such as closing doors and organizing objects, multiple times, stating that "it has to be done." The family observes that she laughs loudly in inappropriate situations, including at funerals. It is also noted that her hands tremble when holding a cup. The sister reports that the patient is able to wait and control impulses without difficulty.

History: previous neuropsychological assessment revealed moderate intellectual disability, without severe intellectual disability. Urinary tract ultrasound showed no ureteral duplication and no renal pelvis duplication.

Physical examination: adequate head circumference, no microcephaly. Narrow palpebral fissures. Large ears. Long philtrum. High palate. Mandibular prognathism. Small hands. Hand tremor.

findings.text: height below -2 standard deviations for age and sex
shortening of the metacarpus on hand radiograph

translation:
Identification: girl, 1 year and 10 months, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: "She is very overweight and small for her age."

Current illness history: mother reports that the child gains weight excessively and that she notices the child is much shorter than other children of the same age. Previous multidisciplinary assessment with standardized tests revealed intellectual disability.

Physical examination: child is obese. Height below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Hands with digits of proportional length, without brachydactily. On palpation, absence of hardened nodules or calcifications in the subcutaneous tissue.

Complementary tests: hand radiograph shows shortening of the metacarpus. Serum calcium within normal limits. Serum phosphorus without abnormalities.

findings.text: ears with distorted folds and extra creases
reduced cerebellar volume on brain MRI

absent: generalized muscle rigidity with loss of consciousness
translation:
Identification: girl, 5 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child delayed in reaching milestones in all domains, both motor and speech and social interaction, with sitting and walking occurring later than in other children. She states that the child still walks with a wobbly gait and has difficulty maintaining balance. At school, the child has intellectual disability according to neuropsychological assessment. Diagnosed with cataract by ophthalmology. Mother denies difficulty swallowing. Denies episodes of generalized muscle rigidity with loss of consciousness.

History: no anal malformation at birth.

Physical examination: height appropriate for age. Flat facial profile. Ears with distorted folds and extra creases, appearing creased. Valgus knees. Tibias palpable bilaterally. Ataxic gait, with dysmetria on index-nose tests.

Complementary tests: brain MRI showing reduced cerebellar volume with preserved morphology. Radiographs showing delayed epiphyseal ossification.

findings.text: opening in the roof of the mouth
increased bone density of the skull vault

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "does not hear well," as reported by the accompanying family member.

Current disease history: the family reports that the patient was born with an opening in the roof of the mouth. The patient also states that many teeth have never emerged. Denies gingival enlargement or swelling over the teeth.

Physical examination: eyes are well separated from each other. Limbs show no shortening of the midsegments (forearms and legs) compared to the rest of the limbs. Fingers of hands and feet demonstrate full extension, without camptodactyly.

Complementary tests: audiometry reveals conductive hearing loss and neural-sensory hearing loss. Cranial radiograph shows increased bone density of the skull vault.

Identification: male patient brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "he is much shorter than his peers and has short fingers."

Current disease history: the mother reports that the child has always been the shortest in his class and that his hand fingers have been short since early childhood. She also notes that some toes are shorter than others and that the big toe is broad. She reports good academic performance and denies intellectual disability.

Physical examination: short stature. Hands with short fingers. Bilateral broad big toes.

Complementary tests: hand radiographs show short and broad metacarpals, as well as broad phalanges. Lower limb radiographs show short tibias and hypoplastic fibulas.

findings.text: failure to gain weight as expected
episodes of complete stiffness with rigid arms and neck
sudden startle reactions with brief arm tremors
episodes of intense body arching from neck to heels

translation:
Identification: girl, 5 years old, brought by parents, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Main complaint: developmental delay and seizures.

Current illness history: Parents report that the child has always taken longer to sit, speak, and interact, falling behind other children in all domains. Since early infancy, she has "not gained weight as expected" and has shown minimal growth since birth. The mother states that she frequently regurgitates after feedings and meals, with milk returning from the stomach. She has episodes in which she becomes completely stiff, with rigid arms and neck, and others of sudden startle reactions, with brief arm tremors. Denies episodes with stiffness followed by rhythmic generalized shaking. Parents also report episodes in which she arches her body intensely from the neck to the heels.

History: Gestation without amniotic fluid reduction.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Significant weight and height below expected values, with marked weight deficit. Global hypotonia. Eyebrows without marked arched appearance. Thorax without sternal protrusion. Fundus examination with bilateral papillary pallor. No cortical origin visual deficiency.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI with ventricular dilation and thin corpus callosum. Spectroscopy with lactate peak and reduced N-acetylmethionine. Interictal EEG abnormal.

findings.text: serum vitamin B12 level below lower limit of normality

translation:
Identification: female patient, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: laboratory test abnormalities.

Current disease history: patient brought previously ordered laboratory tests from general medicine, which prompted the referral. Reports being advised to seek specialized evaluation following test results.

Additional tests: hemogram and myelogram showing megaloblastic anemia. Serum vitamin B12 level below the lower limit of normality. Urine test showing increased proteinuria.

Management: case discussion in the multidisciplinary team; return with the tests brought.

corpus callosum thinning on brain MRI

absent: brain MRI with corpus callosum thinning
translation:
Identification: girl, 4 years and 7 months, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child walked alone later than expected and still speaks few words, with speech and language delay. She states that the girl is never still, runs around the house constantly, cannot concentrate on a game for more than a few minutes, and acts without thinking, picking up objects and crossing without waiting. She also reports that she has choking episodes and difficulty swallowing food. Since infancy, when crying, the mouth has drawn downward on one side only, while the other side remained still. The family has also noticed that she often holds her head tilted to look at things.

History: adequate head circumference at birth, no microcephaly at birth.

Physical examination: appropriate height for age and sex. Head circumference within normal limits, no acquired microcephaly. Eyes widely spaced, nasolabial fissures anteverted, high palate. Global hypotonia. Compensatory head posture.

Complementary tests: brain MRI with corpus callosum thinning.

findings.text: difficulty maintaining balance when changing position
push test with multiple backward steps requiring support

translation:
Identification: male patient, 40 years old, referred to the neurogenetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: imbalance and speech disturbance since childhood.

Current disease history: accompanied by his sister, who reports that he delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and learning during early childhood, falling behind other children in all aspects. Since early age, he has been wobbling and unsteady, a condition that, according to the family, has never worsened over the years. He reports frequent falls and difficulty maintaining balance when pushed or when changing position. His sister also observes that his speech is slurred and unclear.

Physical examination: non-progressive cerebellar ataxia, with broad-based gait. Push test with multiple backward steps requires support from the examiner. Dysarthria present. Nystagmus present. Limited extrinsic eye movement, with ophthalmoplegia.

Complementary tests: brain MRI shows reduced cerebellar volume with preserved morphology.

findings.text: rough, brown follicular papules on the outer surfaces of the arms and thighs

translation:
Identification: 3-year-3-month-old girl, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics for genetic medicine evaluation.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child took longer than other children to sit, crawl, and walk. She also notes that the child has always been the smallest in the class. She observes rough, bumpy nodules on the outer parts of the arms and thighs. Denies that the child easily turns blue. No complaints of difficulty seeing distant objects.

History: prenatal ultrasound revealed a single umbilical artery. Follow-up with cardiology for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and pulmonary stenosis. Hematology shows no history of juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.

Physical examination: short stature. High forehead. Hypertelorism, oblique palpebral fissures, and ptosis. Low-set ears with posterior rotation. Webbed neck. Thorax with sternal depression. Straight hair, not curly. Rough, brown follicular papules on the outer surfaces of the arms and thighs.

Complementary tests: ophthalmological evaluation shows no myopia and no keratoconus.

Identification: male patient, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics for evaluation of facial abnormalities.

Current disease history: parents report that the child takes longer than other children to sit, walk, speak, and interact, with developmental delay in all domains. They also note that he has always appeared to have his upper eyelids "drooping," covering part of the eyes.

Physical examination: eyes well separated, palpebral fissures with downward inclination, superior ptosis of the eyelids. Broad nasal base. Nose with a vertical median groove on the dorsum extending to the tip, dividing the nose into two halves. Median facial cleft. U-shaped redness of the upper lip, with the central portion significantly higher than the corners. Testes not palpable in the scrotal sac, located in the inguinal canal.
