findings.text: lack of response when called from a distance
need to speak loudly to be heard
palpable fusion of coronal sutures bilaterally

translation:
Identification: 4-year-old girl, accompanied by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: "She takes a long time to do everything."

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child delayed in holding her head up, sitting, walking, and speaking, always lagging behind other children in all areas. She also reports that the child does not respond when called from a distance and needs to speak loudly to be heard. Standardized psychological testing revealed intellectual disability. No seizures at any time.

History: no other relevant information.

Physical examination: child in good general condition, active. Cranial examination shows palpable fusion of the coronal sutures bilaterally, confirmed by imaging.

Complementary tests: cranial CT shows bilateral coronal craniosynostosis.

Identification: girl, 12 years old, brought by mother for first visit to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neurology.

Main complaint: "has been significantly delayed since early childhood."

Current disease history: mother reports that the girl had delayed milestones in sitting, walking, speaking, and playing compared to other children, with a global developmental delay described in early years. She recalls a prior hospitalization in the ICU during which the patient was in a coma. Previous hospitalization reports indicate low blood glucose, lactic acidosis, and a rhabdomyolysis episode. The mother also states that, over time, her legs have become stiff, making walking difficult.

Physical examination: spasticity in lower limbs.

Complementary tests: acylcarnitine profile provided by the family showing elevated tetradecenylcarnitine (C14:1).

Identification: Female patient, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: Accompanied by mother, who reports that since infancy the daughter has been "floppy," appearing lacking body firmness when picked up. She also states that, during early childhood, she delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting, falling behind other children in all developmental areas.

Physical examination: Globally decreased muscle tone. Flaccid abdomen, painless, liver not palpable below the costal margin, no hepatomegaly.

Complementary tests: Hepatic elastography for fibrosis. Lipid profile with elevated total cholesterol and increased LDL. Elevated alkaline phosphatase. Elevated GOT and GPT. Low serum ceruloplasmin. Isoelectric focusing of transferrin with type II pattern.

findings.text: feet stick to the floor when walking
lead-pipe rigidity on passive limb mobilization
neuronal loss in central nervous system

translation:
Identification: male, 49 years old, brought by spouse, referred to neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "forgetting and difficulty walking."

Current illness history: Spouse reports that the patient has been progressively losing memory, reasoning, and judgment, to the point where he can no longer work or maintain social life. Patient reports that he trembles when his hands are at rest in his lap, and the tremor improves when he uses his hands. He states that he has difficulty initiating any movement, and when attempting to walk, his feet "stick to the floor" for several seconds. He has had several falls at home. Some time ago, he stopped walking and currently does not ambulate. Reports that the parkinsonian syndrome improved well with levodopa. Denies urinary incontinence. Denies seeing or hearing things that do not exist. Family does not observe apathy or lack of motivation, and the patient does not have episodes of confusion.

Physical examination: Alert. Deep tendon reflexes globally hyperactive. Lead-pipe rigidity on passive mobilization of limbs. Akinesia. Fixed dystonic postures in limbs.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI shows no cortical cerebral atrophy. Previous cerebral biopsy histopathology: neuronal loss in the central nervous system, neurofibrillary tangles, and Lewy bodies.

findings.text: increased percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes

translation:
Identification: 11-year-old boy, brought by mother, referred to the pediatric immunology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: recurrent infections.

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child has recurrent throat, nasal, and sinus infections several times per year. No history of recurrent otitis. No history of recurrent pneumonia. No chronic diarrhea. No recurrent episodes of oral herpes.

Complementary tests: Thrombocytopenia with positive antiplatelet antibodies, consistent with primary immunodeficiency. Low serum IgA and low serum IgM. Immunophenotyping shows reduced absolute B lymphocyte count and increased percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes, without reduction in CD4+ cell proportion.

findings.text: reduced muscle strength in lower limbs
feet externally deviated in standing position

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 31 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "Slurred speech and weak legs."

Current illness history: Patient reports that people have difficulty understanding her because her speech has become slow and words are poorly articulated. She also reports leg weakness, with difficulty climbing stairs. Denies imbalance or lack of motor coordination.

Physical examination: Dysarthria. Spastic hypertonia in the lower limbs. Reduced muscle strength in the lower limbs. Hyperreflexia in both upper and lower limbs. Babinski sign present. Absence of Achilles clonus. Cerebellar tests normal, no ataxia. Feet externally deviated in standing position, with bilateral valgus foot posture; no cavus foot. No signs of peripheral neuropathy.

findings.text: partial agenesis of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: boy, 12 years old, brought by mother, referred to the genetic medicine outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: mother reports that he took a long time to speak and that, to date, he communicates with simpler sentences than those of other children of his age. She also states that since early childhood he has had difficulty hearing; previous audiometry revealed sensorineural hearing loss. Prior neuropsychological assessment concluded intellectual disability.

Physical examination: triangular facial shape, broad at the temples and tapering toward the chin. Deep-set eyes. Sparse eyebrows. Ears with posterior rotation. Feet with syndactyly between the 2nd and 3rd toes. Elbows extend beyond normal, with hyperextension. Hypermobility of the knees.

Complementary tests: cranial MRI brought by the family shows partial agenesis of the corpus callosum and arachnoid cyst.

findings.text: skin patches with alternating lighter and darker areas

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: skin changes and short stature.

Current disease history: the family reports that the patient has always been shorter than peers of the same age. They also note, for many years, patches on the skin with alternating lighter and darker areas, thin and wrinkled skin, and visible small blood vessels.

Physical examination: height below expected for age. Skin with poikilodermia.

Complementary tests: complete blood count showing neutropenia. Hormonal assessment revealing hypogonadism due to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Chest CT showing bronchiectasis and interstitial lung disease.

findings.text: small red dots on the skin
large purple macules on the legs

absent: neurological deficit other than cerebellar atrophy
translation:
Identification: male, 16 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by hematology.

Main complaint: "purple spots on the body".

Current disease history: The mother reports that the child frequently develops small red dots on the skin, mainly on the legs. She also states the presence of large purple macules, larger than a coin, appearing after minor trauma. No alteration in speech; no dysarthria present.

Physical examination: Ecchymoses in lower limbs and forearms. Speech without articulatory abnormalities.

Complementary tests: Complete blood count showing pancytopenia, with prominent thrombocytopenia. Bone marrow examination and bone marrow biopsy showing hypocellular marrow and reduced number of megakaryocytes. Brain MRI revealing cerebellar atrophy.

findings.text: sinus rhythm frequency below 50 bpm at rest

translation:
Identification: boy, 3 years old, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric cardiology.

Current illness history: parents report prior hospitalization in pediatric ICU due to a cardiac shock episode. They deny any episode of cardiac arrest. They bring cardiology reports and tests, described below.

Complementary tests: ECG showed sinus bradycardia, sinus rhythm frequency at rest below 50 bpm, and prolonged corrected QT interval. On another tracing, second-degree AV block was observed. Holter monitoring showed no ventricular fibrillation and no polymorphic ventricular tachycardia; no T-wave alternans was present. Echocardiogram revealed non-compacted left ventricular myocardopathy.

findings.text: ideomotor apraxia in the upper limbs

translation:
Identification: male, 57 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for investigation.

Current illness history: the wife reports that he started walking with a staggering gait, losing balance and bumping into objects. Over time, he ceased walking and currently moves using a wheelchair. The family also noticed that he became forgetful, with difficulty in reasoning and following conversations. No hearing loss reported.

Physical examination: nystagmus present. Fundoscopic examination shows bilateral papilledema. Spastic paraparesis. Ideomotor apraxia in the upper limbs.

Complementary tests: brain MRI shows cerebellar atrophy. Cerebrospinal fluid with elevated lactate.

Identification: male patient brought by mother for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: short stature and hair loss.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always been much shorter than other children of the same age. She states that his hair has always been thin and, over time, has started to fall out, leaving bald patches on the scalp. She also notes that one of his eyes "is crooked," deviating from the other when looking. She further reports that some teeth never developed, even after the expected age for tooth eruption.

Physical examination: severe short stature, below -4 standard deviations for age and sex. Small, short, and narrow face. Frontal bossing bilaterally. Prominent supraorbital ridges. Shallow orbits with protruding eyeballs. Thick eyelids, without inflammatory signs. Concave nasal dorsum. Thick superior lip redness.

findings.text: difficulty in rising from low chairs
weakness in the thighs and hips
prominent scapulae on the back when raising arms
bilateral scapular winging during upper limb elevation
proximal weakness in the lower limbs
fatty replacement of muscle groups on muscle MRI

translation:
Identification: Male, 37 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for assessment of a muscular disorder.

Main complaint: Weakness in the legs.

Current illness history: Patient reports progressive difficulty in climbing stairs and rising from low chairs, describing weakness in the thighs and hips. His wife notes that "the scapulae become prominent" on the back when he raises his arms. The patient continues to ambulate independently, without assistance, and has not lost the ability to walk.

Physical examination: Obvious muscular atrophy on inspection. Bilateral scapular winging during upper limb elevation. Proximal weakness in the lower limbs.

Complementary tests: Serum creatine kinase (CK) elevated. Muscle MRI showing fatty replacement of muscle groups. Spirometry with reduced VEF1/CVF ratio.

findings.text: incomplete finger extension in interphalangeal joints
increased distance between hallux and second pododactyl
reduced strength in distal lower limb muscles
preserved strength in proximal lower and distal upper limb muscles

translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "has difficulty walking and speaking".

Current illness history: mother reports that her daughter took longer than other children to sit, crawl, and walk. She notes that speech has always been slow, with words that are unclear and difficult to understand. She also observes that the girl is shorter than her peers of the same age. Denies recurrent respiratory infections, such as frequent pneumonias or bronchitis.

History: congenital flat feet, noted since birth.

Physical examination: height below expected for age and sex. Spine without scoliosis. Long and thin fingers of hands. Fingers of hands that do not fully extend, even passively, in the interphalangeal joints. Bilateral equinovarus feet, with increased distance between the hallux and the second pododactyl. Global decrease in muscle tone. Reduced strength in distal lower limb muscles; preserved strength in proximal lower limb muscles and in both proximal and distal upper limb muscles. Absent tendon reflexes globally. Dysarthria.

findings.text: excess skin folds that do not return to original position when pulled

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: mother reports that the child has minimal facial expression, with a blank gaze and mouth always slightly open. She also notes that his skin is loose, wrinkled, and has excess folds that do not return to their original position when pulled. She states that he has always been "floppy" when being carried.

History: previous echocardiogram revealed ventricular septal defect. Orthopedic evaluation diagnosed hip dislocation.

Physical examination: triangular face, with broad forehead and pointed chin. Hypertelorism. Broad nasal base; narrow nostrils in a fissure. Short palpebral fissures with minimal vertical opening (blepharoptosis). Lower eyelids turned inward, directed toward the globe. Low-set ears. Global hypotonia. Transparent lenses, no cataract. Bilateral testes in the scrotum, no cryptorchidism. No disproportional tall stature. Spine without kyphoscoliosis.

Complementary tests: echocardiogram showed no ascending aortic tubular aneurysm.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex
eyes well apart from each other
ears in concha form, projecting laterally, without fold of antihelix

translation:
Identification: Girl, 12 years and 4 months old, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: Assessment of facial abnormalities and short stature.

Current disease history: Mother reports that the girl was born with cleft lip on both sides and bilateral cleft palate, not limited to one side. She states that the girl has always been the shortest in her class. She reports that the girl has worn high-degree glasses since childhood to see distant objects. No conductive hearing loss was found on audiometry.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Height below the P3. Eyes well apart from each other. Broad nasal base and recessed nasal root. Small and retruded mandible. Ears in concha form, projecting laterally, without fold of antihelix. No frontal bossing. Thorax with sternal depression. Corneal opacity on ophthalmologic examination.

Complementary tests: Echocardiogram showed persistent left superior vena cava and no tricuspid valve.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex
short fingers on hands and feet

translation:
Identification: boy, 8 years and 3 months, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for short stature and school learning delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that he delayed in sitting, walking, and speaking, falling behind other children from infancy. Currently has intellectual disability with significant learning difficulties. Reports episodes of convulsive seizures. Also states that the child is chronically ill, with recurrent infections throughout the year. Has prior diagnosis of severe combined immunodeficiency; no isolated severe T-cell immunodeficiency.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Coarse facial appearance, broad nasal tip. No hypertelorism and no oblique palpebral fissures. Disproportionate short stature with short limbs and normal trunk; limb shortening due to minimal bone growth. Short fingers on hands and feet. Single transverse palmar crease. Thorax without pectus excavatum.

Complementary tests: radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies and proximal femoral epiphyses hypoplasia. Renal ultrasound shows no multiple cysts.

findings.text: urethral meatus at tip of glans

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years and  7 months, brought by mother, referred for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that, in early years, he was significantly delayed in all areas compared to other children, with global developmental delay. He sat and walked much later than expected. He began speaking very late and still has poor speech. Since infancy, he has had significant difficulty with breastfeeding and feeding. He does not like to interact with others, performs repetitive movements, and is always fixated on the same toys. He experiences seizures. The mother notes that he has poor hearing. At school, he is being evaluated by a psychological assessment, with a diagnosis of intellectual disability.

History: in the neonatal period, persistent arterial canal was identified. Duplication of the ureter was found on imaging studies. He has been followed up in ophthalmology for cortical visual deficiency.

Physical examination: low-set ears. No retrognathia and no micrognathia. Normal ocular alignment, without strabismus. Short thumbs bilaterally. Male genitalia with a penis of very small size for age; testes in the scrotal sac, without cryptorchidism; urethral meatus at the tip of the glans, without hypospadias.

findings.text: difficulty managing finances and household matters

translation:
Identification: female, 47 years old, referred to the neurogenetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: progressive loss of neurological functions.

Current disease history: the family reports that the patient has lost the ability to manage finances and household matters, has forgotten appointments, and is no longer able to follow conversations, resulting in significant social impairment. The husband noticed that speech has become slurred and difficult to understand. She no longer moves her legs, which have become rigid. She presents urinary incontinence and difficulty with bladder control, which the team attributes to neurological bladder dysfunction. Family members deny any episodes of aggression.

Physical examination: dementia-like presentation. Dysarthria. Spastic paraplegia. Ataxia in upper limbs. Supranuclear oculomotor paralysis; saccades with preserved velocity. No tremor. Absence of parkinsonian signs. No amyotrophy.

Complementary tests: brain MRI showing cerebellar atrophy and cerebral cortical atrophy. Nerve conduction study (ENMG) revealing axonal motor neuropathy.

findings.text: dark pigmented spots scattered over the skin
hypercrómica, flat, well-demarcated macules on trunk
chest computed tomography with interstitial pneumonitis

translation:
Identification: male infant, 3 months old, brought by mother, referred to medical genetics by pediatrics.

Current illness history: mother reports that the baby became jaundiced shortly after birth, and that jaundice persisted for many weeks. She states that the baby's skin has been turning red all over, with peeling occurring almost throughout the body. She also notes the presence of several dark pigmented spots scattered over the skin. She reports that the infant is not gaining weight or growing as expected. No persistent diarrhea.

History: fetal growth restriction was not observed during gestation.

Physical examination: infant with erythroderma. Hypercrómic, flat, well-demarcated macules on trunk. Prominent forehead. No hypertelorism. Enlarged liver on palpation.

Complementary tests: hypoalbuminemia. Elevated GGT. Decreased serum IgG; IgA and IgM within normal limits. Reduced natural killer cell count. Persistent CMV viremia. Chest computed tomography with interstitial pneumonitis.

findings.text: generalized swelling from eyelids to feet
head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex

translation:
Identification: girl, 1 year old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric nephrology.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has cyanotic lips and tips of fingers, especially when crying. She also notes that the child is "floppy," with a loose body posture. Several weeks ago, she noticed the child was swollen all over the body, from the eyelids to the feet. Denies decreased urine output; diapers remain wet as usual.

History: followed up by cardiology for tetralogy of Fallot. Echocardiogram shows ventricular septal defect; no common trunk, no persistent left superior vena cava, no partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage, and no right aortic arch. Subsequently referred to nephrology for renal insufficiency.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Axial and appendicular hypotonia.

Complementary tests: serum creatinine elevated.

findings.text: nail detachment starting at the tip
complete absence of hair follicles on the scalp
complete absence of hair follicles on the body

translation:
Identification: Female, 25 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: Nail changes and absence of hair.

Current illness history: Patient attended the consultation alone. Reports that the nails on her hands are detaching from the nail bed starting at the tip, becoming loose. She also states that her nails have always been irregular, brittle, and deformed.

History: No inguinal hernia. No unilateral cryptorchidism.

Physical examination: Ungueal dystrophy. Complete absence of hair follicles on the scalp and body. Oral cavity: teeth without abnormalities.

findings.text: delay in all areas of development
eyes tremble from side to side
brain MRI with cortical gyral pattern alteration
brain MRI with thin corpus callosum
brain MRI with enlarged cleft septum pell-ucidum

translation:
Identification: girl, 2 years and 3 months, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric neurology.

Main complaint: developmental delay and seizures.

Current illness history: parents report that the child has delays in all areas of development. She does not speak any words. She took a long time to hold her head up and sit, and to date she does not crawl or walk. She also has difficulty grasping small objects and using her hands. The mother noticed that her eyes "tremble" from side to side. She has had generalized seizures since the first year of life. In her medical record, head circumference growth has stopped, with flattening of the fontanelle curve.

Physical examination: coarse facial features. Deep-set eyes. Nystagmus. Palate without elevation. Well-marked labial fissure. Ears with normal implantation. Nose without shortening. No edema in the dorsal hands.

Complementary tests: fundoscopy with bilateral papillary pallor, suggestive of optic atrophy. Brain MRI: enlarged ventricles, delayed myelination, cortical gyral pattern alteration, thin corpus callosum, and enlarged cleft septum pellucidum.

findings.text: episodes of sudden and rapid shaking of arms and trunk
paralysis of all four limbs and trunk
increased methylmalonic acid in urinary organic acids

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neurodevelopmental pediatrics.

Main complaint: "delay in all areas and episodes of sudden shocks".

Current illness history: mother reports that since infancy, he delayed in holding his head up, sitting, speaking, and interacting, falling behind other children in all domains. She describes episodes of sudden and rapid shaking of arms and trunk, as if struck by a shock, occurring several times per week. Since early childhood, she has noticed that one eye "turns inward," deviating toward the nose. Currently, he does not speak, does not understand simple commands, and is completely dependent on caregivers.

History: followed up by neurodevelopmental pediatrics with diagnosis of encephalopathy.

Physical examination: does not communicate verbally; no significant interaction with examiner; profound intellectual disability. Paralysis of all four limbs and trunk, with no voluntary movement. Evidence of esotropia on ophthalmological examination.

Complementary tests: ophthalmological assessment showing hyperopia. Echocardiogram without structural cardiac abnormalities. Urinary organic acids with increased methylmalonic acid; urinary homocystine absent. Plasma methionine within normal limits.

findings.text: inability to determine baby's sex at birth
penile length below expected for age
scrotal sac divided by midline fissure

translation:
Identification: boy, 2 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatric urology for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: genital anomaly since birth.

Current illness history: mother reports that at birth, the medical team was unable to immediately determine the baby's sex based on genital appearance. She also states that since the first months of life, the child has rough skin with red plaques that itch severely, especially in the arm creases and behind the knees. She also noticed that the second and third toes are fused.

History: vaginal delivery without pelvic presentation.

Physical examination: low-set ears. Short nose. Penile length when stretched is below expected for age, urethral meatus in a ventral position, outside the glans tip. Scrotal sac divided by a midline fissure. Testes not palpable in the scrotum, located in the inguinal canal, both with reduced volume.

Complementary tests: low total cholesterol. Elevated serum 7-dehydrocholesterol. Elevated serum 8-dehydrochole-sterol. Serum testosterone within normal limits.

findings.text: urinary L-glycerate level above upper limit of normality

translation:
Identification: female infant, 11 months of age, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics to medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: renal stones.

Current disease history: mother reports that the child was investigated after the discovery of stones in the kidneys, whose analysis revealed calcium oxalate stones.

Physical examination: infant in good general condition, active and responsive.

Complementary tests: 24-hour urine showing increased urinary oxalate excretion. Urinary L-glycerate level above the upper limit of normality. Calcium excretion within normal range. Venous gas analysis without metabolic acidosis. Serum creatinine normal.

findings.text: lower eyelids covering part of pupils

absent: extra digits in hands and feet
neurological deficits other than Dandy-Walker malformation
developmental delay in motor skills beyond holding head up, sitting, and walking
translation:
Identification: male patient brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "He takes longer to perform tasks that other children do."

Current disease history: Parents report that their child delayed in holding his head up, sitting, and walking, and also speaks little and interacts less than expected for his age. The mother noticed that he sometimes breathes very rapidly, "gasping," even at rest. They deny episodes of apnea.

Physical examination: Lower eyelids drooping, covering part of the pupils. Palate of normal height. Upper lip erythema of normal thickness. Feet without fusion between the second and third toes. Absence of extra digits in hands and feet.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI brought by the family shows Dandy-Walker malformation and molar tooth sign.

findings.text: writhing hand and finger movements at rest
continuous athetoid movements in upper extremities
inability to perform voluntary eye movements in requested direction

translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in pediatric neurology outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "walks unsteadily and speaks in a slurred manner."

Current illness history: mother reports that the child wobbles when walking, falls frequently, and has difficulty grasping objects with precision. She also notes that his speech is slow and hard to understand, with words poorly articulated. She observes that he makes slow, writhing movements of his hands and fingers, which he cannot control, even when at rest.

Physical examination: ataxic gait with widened base; bilateral dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia. Obvious dysarthria during conversation. Continuous athetoid movements in upper extremities. Deep tendon reflexes globally diminished. On oculomotor assessment, unable to perform voluntary eye movements in the direction requested, although the oculocephalic reflex is preserved with complete conjugate eye movement.

Identification: Male infant, 2 months of age, brought by parents for first visit to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neonatology.

Current illness history: Parents report that the baby is "floppy," appears to slip when picked up from the parent's lap. They state that the infant does not maintain eye contact nor smile, and spends most of the time drowsy, poorly responsive to stimuli. They deny having experienced any convulsive episodes.

Physical examination: Head circumference appropriate for age, no microcephaly. Global hypotonia. Global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. Decreased level of consciousness, presenting with encephalopathy.

Complementary tests: Elevated serum lactate. Arterial gas analysis showing lactic acidosis. Plasma amino acids with elevated alanine; plasma glycine within normal limits. Brain MRI: dilatation of lateral ventricles and periventricular cysts; gyrification pattern without simplification. EEG: posterior baseline rhythm present.

findings.text: fingers become white with cold exposure
fingers become red with cold exposure
fingers turn red with cold exposure
reduced post-vaccination titers to tetanus toxoid
diminished response to polysaccharide pneumococcal vaccine
diminished response to conjugated pneumococcal vaccine

absent: complete absence of response to tetanus
translation:
Identification: Female patient, 21 years old, referred to the clinical immunology outpatient clinic for evaluation of laboratory abnormalities.

Current illness history: Reports that, with cold exposure, her fingers become white, then red, and subsequently turn red. Denies recurrent otitis. Denies recurrent sinusitis. Denies recurrent pharyngitis. Denies repeated episodes of giardiasis.

Complementary tests: Immunoglobulin levels: low IgG, low IgA, and low IgM. Vaccine response assessment: partial response to tetanus toxoid, with reduced post-vaccination titers, although not absent; no complete absence of response to tetanus. Diminished response to the polysaccharide pneumococcal vaccine and also to the conjugated pneumococcal vaccine.

findings.text: wakes up several times during the night
repeated hand swinging without purpose for prolonged periods

translation:
Identification: girl, 2 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrician for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: "delay in development".

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always been slower than other children in all areas. It took a long time to achieve independent sitting, and still does not walk without support. She does not speak any words, only emits sounds. The mother states that the daughter has never lost any previously acquired skills. Since early infancy, she has had difficulty feeding, taking a long time to eat, and accepting little food. She has poor sleep, wakes up several times during the night, and has irregular sleep schedules. She presents with focal onset epileptic seizures. The mother observes that the girl repeatedly performs the same hand movement, swinging her hands without purpose, for prolonged periods.

Physical examination: child is active, with global hypotonia.

Complementary tests: brain MRI shows hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and hypoplasia of the frontal lobes; adequate myelination for age. EEG is abnormal.

findings.text: failure to gain weight as expected
recurrent infections since first months of life
head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex
cerebral lactate peak on brain MRI spectroscopy

translation:
Identification: female infant, 10 months old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always had difficulty breastfeeding, becoming tired and dropping the breast, and has not been gaining weight as expected. She also states that the daughter "lives sick," with recurrent infections since the first months of life. She notes that the child does not respond well to sounds and is "floppy" when picked up. Developmental delay in all domains: still does not sit without support, does not babble, and shows minimal interaction.

History: full-term birth, small for gestational age. Previous echocardiogram revealed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, without pulmonary hypertension.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Length below the 3rd percentile. Prominent testes. Palpebral fissures of normal size; eyelashes without elongation; eyebrows without thickening. Axial and appendicular hypotonia. Audiological assessment with hearing loss.

Complementary tests: hyperlactatemia in serum measurements. Brain MRI spectroscopy with cerebral lactate peak.

findings.text: head involuntarily turns to one side
neck contractions that cannot be controlled
sudden and rapid tremors in the arms and legs
reduced homovanillic acid in cerebrospinal fluid

translation:
Identification: 51-year-old patient referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of a movement disorder.

Main complaint: "neck that pulls itself alone."

Current illness history: Patient reports that the head involuntarily turns to one side, with neck contractions that cannot be controlled. Also reports sudden and rapid tremors in the arms and legs. Psychiatrically, patient states feeling "down," with no hope or value, and difficulty escaping this state. Denies anxiety. No intrusive thoughts or repetitive behaviors.

History: Consumes large amounts of alcohol for many years, unable to reduce intake, experiences strong cravings to drink, and becomes ill when deprived of alcohol.

Physical examination: Cervical dystonia present. Myoclonus in the limbs. No axial dystonia. No dystonia in the lower limbs. No dystonia in the upper limbs.

Complementary tests: Cerebrospinal fluid shows reduced homovanillic acid and reduced 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid.

findings.text: eye pain when exposed to sunlight
tearing when exposed to bright light
need to hold objects very close
need to hold television very close
skin significantly lighter than family members
iridescence of different colors between right and left eyes

translation:
Identification: male patient brought by mother for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "very uncomfortable with brightness".

Current disease history: mother reports that the child experiences eye pain and tearing when exposed to sunlight or bright light, preferring dark environments. She also notes that he has poor vision and needs to hold objects and the television very close. She observed early on that his skin is significantly lighter than that of family members and that his hair is very light, almost colorless.

Physical examination: involuntary and rhythmic eye movements, with tremors, present continuously. Iridescence of different colors between the right and left eyes. White eyebrows. Diffuse hypopigmented skin.

Complementary tests: ophthalmological assessment with reduced visual acuity.

findings.text: inability to maintain proper trunk posture when sitting
hyperintense areas on T2 in cerebral white matter
hyperintense areas on T2 in spinal cord

translation:
Identification: girl, 2 years and 2 months, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics to neurology consultation.

Main complaint: "She stopped doing things she had already been doing."

findings.text: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex

no increase in bone mineral density

Identification: female patient brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Current disease history: mother reports that the daughter experiences episodes during which she becomes rigid and convulses, without responding, lasting a few minutes, and then spontaneously resolves. She also notes since childhood that there are some lighter patches on the trunk skin, in leaf-shaped forms.

elliptical red blood cells in cigar-shaped form

Main complaint: "Yellowish skin."

Current illness history: The mother noticed that her daughter's skin turns yellow and that the whites of her eyes also turn yellow.

Physical examination: Child is active. Spleen palpable below the right costal margin, enlarged. Liver palpable below the right costal margin, enlarged.

Identification: male, 21 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

findings.text: liquid stools several times a day

Physical examination: prominent forehead. Lip fissure and palatal cleft. Small fossa in front of the ear. Ears with normal implantation. Nasal passages patent, without choanal atresia. Anus patent, in normal position. Signs of hypovolemia on examination.

Ophthalmoscopy: coloboma of the cornea-retina.

Complementary tests: hyponatremia.

findings.text: delayed motor milestones in sitting and walking
seeking hidden foods shortly after meals

translation:
Identification: male, 14 years old, brought by mother, referred by school for genetic medical evaluation.

findings.text: discomfort and eye pain in bright light

frequent bumping into objects beside him

Identification: male, 19 years old, referred to medical genetics for ophthalmological evaluation.

Main complaint: "vision has been getting worse."

Current illness history: patient reports that he used to see better previously and that his vision has been progressively deteriorating. He describes discomfort and eye pain when exposed to bright light, preferring darker environments. He also reports significant difficulty seeing at night and in poorly lit areas. He notes that he frequently bumps into objects beside him, as he can only see clearly what is directly in front of him.

Complementary tests: perimetry shows constriction of the peripheral field. Electroretinography shows a cone-rod dystrophy pattern.

Complementary tests: Previous electroretinogram shows rod and cone dystrophy.

findings.text: delayed hand opening after forceful closure

Identification: male, 24 years, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation, accompanied by mother.

Main complaint: long-standing cough with sputum and warts.

Current illness history: patient reports a near-daily productive cough for years, worsening in winter, managed by pulmonology for chronic bronchitis. Mother reports that he has always had hearing difficulties, requiring repetition of spoken words. For years, he has had warts on hands and feet, which reappear after removal. No history of recurrent ear, throat, or facial sinus infections. No history of recurrent herpes zoster. No history of recurrent herpes labial.

History: academic difficulties since childhood; previous neuropsychological assessment revealed borderline IQ.

Physical examination: short stature. Head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Multiple verrucous lesions on the dorsal surfaces of hands and feet.

Complementary tests: thoracic CT with bronchiectasis. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping: reduced absolute count of B lymphocytes, reduced absolute count of natural killer (NK) cells, decreased percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes, and decreased proportion of naive CD4+ T cells. Serum IgA within normal limits. Serum IgM within normal limits.

Identification: female patient, 61 years of age, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

Current illness history: patient reports having been admitted urgently for ascending aortic dissection. In cardiac follow-up, she already knew about mitral valve leakage, according to explanation received from the team that has been managing her care.

Physical examination: on oropharyngeal examination, the uvula is divided into two parts at the tip. Mandible is of normal size, without micrognathia. Auricles show normal implantation, without low-implantation ears.

Complementary tests: the echocardiogram brought by the patient describes mitral insufficiency and aortic root aneurysm; tricuspid pulmonary valve, without bicuspidal pulmonary valve. Thoracic angiography shows no pulmonary artery aneurysm and no descending thoracic aortic aneurysm. Lumbar-sacral spine magnetic resonance reveals dural ectasia.

findings.text: no response to any external stimulus
cystic formations in the base nuclei

translation:
Identification  
Male patient, brought by family members for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by the intensive care team.

Current disease history  
Family reports that the patient stopped waking up and does not respond to anything, neither when called, touched, nor stimulated with pain.

Physical examination  
Patient in coma, no response to any external stimulus.

Complementary tests  
Cranial magnetic resonance imaging shows cystic formations in the base nuclei.  
Urine sulfite level is elevated.

Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "loose skin and difficulty walking," as reported by the family.

Current disease history: parents report that the skin has always been wrinkled, hanging, and lacking elasticity. They mention delayed milestones in sitting and walking. The mother notes that the voice is very thin and high-pitched, persistently. They also report that the closure of the "moleira" occurred significantly later than expected. There is no intellectual disability. There is no history of acute hepatic failure.

Physical examination: short stature. Mandibular retrusion. Thorax with sternal depression. Global hypotonia. Long fingers; no metacarpal shortening. Flat feet. Fundoscopic examination with bilateral optic papilla pallor.

Complementary tests: bone densitometry showing reduced bone mass. Peripheral blood smear with neutrophils having hyposegmented nuclei. Serum IgA without reduction. Natural killer cell count without decrease.

Identification: boy, 8 years old, referred by mother to pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for investigation of imbalance.

Main complaint: "falls frequently."

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child falls frequently, several times per week, since beginning to walk. She states that he took longer than his siblings to sit, crawl, and walk independently. She also notes that his hands "shake" without him being able to control them, especially when holding objects. She has also noticed that one of his eyes "is crooked" in relation to the other.

Physical examination: Strabismus on ophthalmological exam. Ataxic gait with widened base. Dismetria on index-nose and heel-knee tests. Tremor in upper limbs. Absent bilateral Achilles reflexes. Distal muscular hypotrophy in limbs.

Complementary tests: Elevated serum lactate. Elevated lactate in cerebrospinal fluid. Nerve conduction study (ENMG): axonal peripheral polyneuropathy. Brain MRI: cerebellar vermis atrophy.

findings.text: tall stature for age and sex

translation:
Identification: Female, 52 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: Patient reports that she has always been the tallest in her family and in school. She states that she was born with inwardly turned feet. Denies prior diagnosis of hip dysplasia.

Physical examination: Tall stature for age and sex. Elongated facial features. Cranium without increase in anteroposterior diameter. No hypertelorism. Dental arches without crowding. Skin with soft texture on palpation. Feet with equinovarus deformity. Absence of hallux valgus bilaterally.

findings.text: inability to bend the tip of the thumb

translation:
Identification: female patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by immunology for evaluation.

Main complaint: changes in hands and face.

Current disease history: mother noticed early on that her daughter's hands were thin and narrow, and that the base of the thumb area was underdeveloped. She also reports that the girl is unable to bend the tip of the thumb. No developmental delay in neuropsychomotor function.

Physical examination: upper lip with fine erythema. Eyes widely spaced, without epicanthal folds. Nasal alae underdeveloped. Small mandible. Hands with a single transverse palmar crease, distal phalanges of fingers elongated, and clinodactyly. No syndactyly. Enlarged clitoris.

Complementary tests: radiography of hands showing thumb hypoplasia and a short first metacarpal. Immunoglobulin levels with reduced IgA and IgM. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping with absence of circulating B lymphocytes.

findings.text: thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer
no structural abnormalities of the cerebellum

translation:
Identification: male, 60 years old, referred to the neuro-ophthalmology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "my vision has been getting weaker."

Current illness history: Patient reports progressive worsening of vision, with difficulty seeing both at a distance and up close. He also reports difficulty distinguishing colors, especially when choosing clothes. He has been followed for years by an ophthalmologist for glaucoma. No depression, persistent sadness, or suicidal ideation. Family members deny sudden, abrupt, and irregular involuntary movements of the body or face, as well as excessive motor agitation. No nystagmus since birth.

Physical examination: Reduced visual acuity bilaterally. Fundoscopic examination shows bilateral optic disc pallor. Neurological examination shows no chorea and no hyperkinesia.

Complementary tests: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) of the optic nerve reveals thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer. Brain MRI shows no structural abnormalities of the cerebellum.

Identification: male patient, brought by mother, referred to the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: mother reports that, during the first year of life, the child began to have episodes of sudden trunk and limb flexion, consistent with infantile spasms. Subsequently, multifocal epileptic seizures developed. She also reports that the child has difficulty feeding, takes a long time to latch onto the breast, and frequently chokes, having trouble swallowing. She states that the child took a long time to achieve sitting, significantly later than expected for his age.

History: at birth, there was a cord around the neck.

Physical examination: global hypotonia. No nystagmus present. Fundus of the eye shows no optic disc pallor, no optic disc coloboma, and no optic atrophy.

Complementary tests: EEG shows hypsarrhythmia. Vascular imaging shows no vascular dilation.

findings.text: opening in the lip and palate
abnormal postures with arms and trunk
minimal interaction or babbling for age

translation:
Identification: male infant, 7 months of age, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred by pediatrics for investigation of congenital malformations.

Current disease history: parents report that the infant was born with an opening in the lip and palate. They state that the baby still does not hold his head well nor roll over, and shows minimal interaction or babbling for his age. The mother notes that the infant occasionally assumes abnormal postures with arms and trunk, which take a long time to resolve.

Physical examination: coarse facies. Cleft lip and cleft palate. Broad palms. Hands with joint contractures, without central cleft or absence of rays. Broad feet.

Complementary tests: laboratory findings show low serum sodium and elevated urinary sodium excretion, indicating renal sodium loss. Renal ultrasound shows no renal multicystic dysplasia, no hydronephrosis, and no increased cortical echogenicity. Neuroimaging reveals ventricular dilation without obstruction to cerebrospinal fluid flow, i.e., communicating hydrocephalus, without obstructive hydrocephalus.

findings.text: tripping over objects in the evening
extra finger on the side of the little finger
fifth digit with radial deviation bilaterally

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 14 years of age, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "Cannot see properly in the dark."

Current illness history: Mother reports that the girl has significant difficulty seeing at night and in poorly lit environments, frequently tripping over objects in the evening. She also states that the girl has poor vision both at a distance and up close, even during the day. At school, she has always required additional support and has a slower learning pace than her peers; a previous neuropsychological assessment concluded mild intellectual disability.

History: Mother reports that the patient was born with an extra finger on the side of the little finger.

Physical examination: Hands with short fingers, disproportionate to the size of the hands. Fifth digit with radial deviation bilaterally. Presence of postaxial polydactily.

Complementary tests: Ophthalmological assessment with reduced visual acuity.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 40 years old, brought by her sister for evaluation in Medical Genetics.

Main complaint: Referred for etiological investigation.

Current disease history: The sister reports that, as a young child, the patient had delayed milestones in sitting, walking, and speaking, falling behind other children in all aspects. Since childhood, she has experienced seizures. She also reports that she has always walked with a waddling gait, with difficulty in balance and coordination of movements. She has intellectual disability and requires family members for daily activities.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Anteverted nares. No hypertelorism, no proptosis, and no frontal bossing. Thorax without pectus excavatum. Feet with hallux valgus; no syndactyly between the 2nd and 3rd toes. Ataxic gait.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI brought by the family shows parietal cortical atrophy.

findings.text: excessive skin growth after minor cuts and scars
thick, raised, and hardened scars extending beyond original wound boundaries
grown flesh on the eye advancing from the corner toward the colored part of the eye in the shape of a wing

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 75 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: Elevated skin lesions.

Current illness history: The patient reports that, after minor cuts and scars, the skin grows excessively, forming thick, raised, and hardened scars that extend beyond the original wound boundaries. She also describes a "grown flesh" on the eye, advancing from the corner toward the colored part of the eye, in the shape of a wing.

Physical examination: Height appropriate for age and sex. Nasal bridge without abnormalities. Nose with normal morphology. Hair without changes. Presence of a cutaneous fibroma. Ocular examination reveals a pterygium invading the cornea.

Complementary tests: X-rays show no signs of osteolysis.

findings.text: concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field
amyloid deposition in the superficial dermis

absent: involuntary movements of the head and neck
involuntary contractions of the face, jaw, or tongue
translation:
Identification: female, 64 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: Patient reports that the skin of her body has been becoming loose, wrinkled, and drooping, with loss of elasticity. She also states that her upper and lower eyelids have become flaccid and have developed bags. She complains of imbalance and lack of coordination in movements. She denies hypertension, denies chest pain with exertion, and denies palpitations or irregular heart rhythm. She does not exhibit abnormal posture or involuntary movements of the head and neck, nor does she have involuntary contractions of the face, jaw, or tongue.

Physical examination: Gait and coordination tests show ataxia. Ophthalmological examination reveals cataracts and trellis corneal dystrophy. Fundoscopic examination shows optic neuropathy.

Complementary tests: Perimetry shows concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field. Skin biopsy demonstrates amyloid deposition in the superficial dermis. Cranial CT shows cerebral calcifications.

findings.text: short stature for age and sex
head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex

translation:
Identification: female, 22 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation; accompanied by mother.

Current disease history: mother reports that, in childhood, the daughter had delayed milestones in sitting, walking, speaking, and learning compared to other children. She also states that she was always the shortest in her class. Reports documented sensorineural hearing loss previously evaluated by audiological assessment. Follows endocrinology for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Denies hair loss. Does not have high-grade myopia.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Short stature for age and sex. Spinal curvature observed on visual inspection and Adams' test.

Complementary tests: reduced FSH and LH, without hypogonadism due to hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. Low TSH. Serum GH below reference values. No diagnosis of hypopituitarism.

findings.text: reduced absolute count of CD3+ T lymphocytes
percentage of CD4+ T cells within the CD3+ compartment below the reference range for age
reduced percentage of CD8+ T cells
low absolute count of B lymphocytes (CD19+)
reduced absolute number of natural killer (NK) cells

absent: lymphoproliferation assay showed reduced response to phytohemagglutinin
lymphoproliferation assay showed reduced proliferation after stimulation with anti-CD3/CD28
naive and memory T lymphocyte subsets in proportions appropriate for age
ratio of gamma-delta T lymphocytes without alteration
translation:
Identification: girl, 9 years old, brought by mother, referred to the immunology outpatient clinic for evaluation of laboratory findings that are abnormal.

Main complaint: abnormalities in lymphocyte immunophenotyping.

Current disease history: mother brought previously performed tests, ordered by the attending pediatrician, reason for referral.

Additional tests: immunophenotyping of peripheral blood with reduced absolute count of CD3+ T lymphocytes. Percentage of CD4+ T cells within the CD3+ compartment below the reference range for age, as well as reduced percentage of CD8+ T cells. B lymphocytes (CD19+) with low absolute count. Natural killer (NK) cells with reduced absolute number. Naive and memory T lymphocyte subsets in proportions appropriate for age. Ratio of gamma-delta T lymphocytes without alteration. Lymphoproliferation assay showed reduced response to phytohemagglutinin and reduced proliferation after stimulation with anti-CD3/CD28.

findings.text: joints with range of motion beyond normal

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents, referred by pediatric cardiology for genetic evaluation.

Current illness history: parents report that the child delayed sitting and walking compared to other children. They also state that he began speaking late and still speaks few words for his age. He has had episodes of convulsive seizures.

History: follows up with cardiology for atrial septal defect and pulmonary stenosis.

Physical examination: atypical facial appearance. Narrow palate. Excess body hair. Joints with range of motion beyond normal.

Complementary tests: echocardiogram brought by parents confirms atrial septal defect and pulmonary stenosis, without ventricular septal defect, without patent ductus arteriosus, without aortic coarctation, without left ventricular hypertrophy, and without persistent left superior vena cava.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years and 5 months old, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Current illness history: Parents report that, shortly after birth, he had difficulty sucking and exhibited very weak sucking. During the neonatal period, he required intubation and remained on mechanical ventilation. He has had seizures from an early age. He was diagnosed with hydrocephalus. The mother states that he has always been very floppy and that he delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting, with global developmental delay. No vomiting. No diagnosis of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Small and retracted mandible. Hypotonia. Hyperreflexia of tendon reflexes.

Complementary tests: Plasma glycine elevated. Cerebrospinal fluid glycine increased. EEG showing seizure-suppression pattern. Brain MRI: dysplastic corpus callosum, without ventriculomegaly and without hypomyelination. Echocardiogram without patent foramen ovale.

findings.text: short stature for age and sex

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation. Accompanied by mother.

Main complaint: "delay in performing tasks".

Current illness history: mother reports that the child had delayed head control, sitting, walking, and speaking, always behind other children of the same age in all domains. She also reports significant learning difficulties and daily living independence issues, with prior psychological evaluation indicating intellectual disability.

History: during prenatal care, the first-trimester ultrasound showed increased nuchal translucency. The child was born prematurely, with less than 37 weeks of gestation.

Physical examination: short stature for age and sex. Atypical facial features.

Identification: boy, 13 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: skin changes and difficulty walking and speaking.

Current disease history: mother reports that the child's skin has always been very dry, shedding scales all over the body. She also notes that the palms of the hands and soles of the feet are thick and hardened. She states that the child speaks in a slurred manner, with difficulty articulating words, and walks with his legs widely apart. She also observes that one of the eyes "diverts" to the side. The child is followed by an ophthalmologist who diagnosed hypermetropia.

Physical examination: rounded face. Deep-set eyes, close together. Strabismus. No epicanthal folds. Eyebrows without sinuses. Nasal alae without anteversion. Intact eyelid, not bifid. Neurological examination: axial hypotonia, hypertonia in lower limbs, hyperreflexia.

Complementary tests: cranial MRI brought by family shows dysplastic corpus callosum; absence of polymicrogyria.

findings.text: serum testosterone level below reference value

translation:
Identification: Male, 32 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by andrology.

Main complaint: Difficulty conceiving children.

Current illness history: Patient reports that, together with his wife, he has been trying to conceive for some time without success, and infertility in the male partner was diagnosed during the couple's evaluation.

Complementary tests: Spermogram showed normal ejaculate volume, yet no spermatozoa were identified in the sample. Testicular biopsy revealed failure in sperm production, confirming non-obstructive azoospermia. Serum testosterone level below the reference value. Estradiol without changes. LH within normal limits. FSH without changes.

Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: fevers that come and go.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has recurrent febrile episodes throughout the year, without a clear relationship to triggering factors. She also reports recurrent pharyngitis, with multiple episodes per year that result in school absences. The child has had a seizure. Mother denies developmental delay; the child keeps up well with school, without mild intellectual disability.

History: no history of severe or opportunistic infections suggestive of immunodeficiency. Referred with documentation of an autoimmune process from a previous service. No vasculitis described.

Physical examination: appropriate height for age and sex, no short stature. Palpable lymphadenopathy.

Complementary tests: prior neuroimaging showed cerebral ventricular dilation.

findings.text: serum cortisol level below reference value
abdominal computed tomography showing macronodular adrenal hyperplasia

absent: endocrinology referral indication for developmental problem
abnormal laboratory test result not mentioned
translation:
Identification: female, 47 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by endocrinology for evaluation.

Main complaint: referral due to abnormal hormonal and imaging tests.

Current illness history: patient brings exams ordered by the assistant endocrinologist. Reports concern about the test results.

Physical examination: patient in good general condition, cooperative.

Complementary tests: serum cortisol level below reference value. Plasma ACTH level reduced. Abdominal computed tomography showing macronodular adrenal hyperplasia.

findings.text: urinary meatus below the tip of the penis

translation:
Identification: boy, 13 years old, brought by mother, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Current illness history: Mother reports that he delayed in sitting, walking, and speaking, falling behind other children in all developmental areas during early childhood. She also mentions episodes of seizures throughout life. No history of motor imbalance or coordination deficits.

History: Born with urinary meatus located below the tip of the penis.

Physical examination: No spasticity present in tone and reflexes.

Complementary tests: Serum ferritin elevated. Serum iron increased. Transferrin saturation elevated. Serum hepcidin reduced. Liver function assessment shows no cirrhosis and no hepatic insufficiency. Brain MRI shows no cerebral atrophy.

findings.text: estimated glomerular filtration rate between 60 and 89 mL/min/1.73 m²

translation:
Identification: male, 66 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of a renal finding.

Main complaint: "cysts in the kidneys".

Current illness history: Patient reports that imaging showed multiple cysts in both kidneys. States having high blood pressure for many years, under follow-up with a general practitioner.

Complementary tests: Renal function with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) between 60 and 89 mL/min/1.73 m², corresponding to stage 2 chronic kidney disease; no criteria for stage 3, nor for stage 4, and no evidence of stage 5 chronic kidney disease. Urine shows no protein loss. Abdominal imaging shows no hepatic cysts.

Identification: male, 29 years old, referred to the immunology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: red skin lesions and joint pain and swelling.

Current disease history: patient reports the onset of red skin lesions, as well as episodes of joint pain, heat, and swelling. He reports recurrent sinusitis throughout life, with several episodes treated. No fever. No muscle pain.

History: reports a previous severe infection due to Epstein-Barr virus, requiring hospitalization.

Physical examination: erythematous skin lesions. Joint inflammation on joint examination. Abdomen without splenomegaly.

Complementary tests: complete blood count showing leukocytosis. Serum ferritin within normal limits.

findings.text: urethral opening at lower part of penis

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatric neurology for genetic medicine evaluation.

Main complaint: "delay in performing tasks".

Current illness history: Mother reports that since infancy, the child has had significant delays in head control, sitting, speaking, and interacting, consistently lagging behind other children in all domains. She also notes that the child has always had great difficulty with feeding, with prolonged breastfeeding sessions, followed by problems with chewing and swallowing food. The parents have also observed that the child does not respond well to sounds.

History: At birth, it was noted that the urethral opening was located at the lower part of the penis, rather than at the tip.

Physical examination: Tetraparesis. Spasticity in all four limbs.

Complementary tests: Audiometry showing sensorineural hearing loss. Brain MRI revealing leucodystrophy and cerebellar hypoplasia.

findings.text: rigidity on passive movement of the limbs
postural tremor in the upper limbs

absent: perception of limb moving on its own or not belonging to her
translation:
Identification: Female, 51 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "Slowness in performing daily activities and tremor in the hands."

Current illness history: Patient reports that she has been becoming slower in carrying out daily tasks, such as dressing and cooking, taking significantly longer to complete movements. She also reports that her hands tremble when holding a cup or when her arms are extended. She denies sudden and involuntary muscle jerks. She denies falls or imbalance. She does not perceive a sensation of any limb moving on its own or not belonging to her.

Physical examination: Supranuclear vertical gaze palsy. Global hyperreflexia of osteotendinous reflexes. Rigidity on passive movement of the limbs. Bradykinesia. Postural tremor in the upper limbs. Involuntary glabellar reflex. No abnormalities on the push test; maintains balance without excessive steps. No apraxia. No dystonic postures in the limbs.

findings.text: muscle weakness predominantly proximal in upper and lower extremities
absent deep tendon reflexes in all four limbs

translation:
Identification: girl, 12 years old, referred to the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of a neuromuscular condition, accompanied by her mother.

Main complaint: "fatigue and weakness in the legs and arms."

Current illness history: The mother reports that the child feels constantly tired, lacking energy to perform simple daily tasks, although she wants to participate. She states difficulty climbing stairs, rising from the floor, and raising her arms above her head. No difficulty swallowing. No episodes of respiratory insufficiency.

History: In early childhood, there was delay in sitting, walking, speaking, and social interaction compared to other children. She has always had appropriate weight and height gain, without growth deficiency.

Physical examination: Lowered upper eyelids, covering part of the iris. Extraocular movements preserved, no progressive external ophthalmoplegia. Global hypotonia. Muscle weakness predominantly proximal in upper and lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes absent in all four limbs.

Complementary tests: Serum creatine kinase (CK) elevated. Muscle biopsy: increased variation in fiber diameter and predominance of type 1 fibers.

findings.text: upper eyelids drooping covering part of pupils

translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child delayed in holding her head up, sitting, walking, and speaking, always lagging behind other children in all domains. She reports that the child has had a seizure that did not subside, with prolonged duration, requiring emergency care. Negates episodes of typical absence, in which the child would suddenly stop what she was doing with a blank stare for a few seconds. Previous neuropsychological assessment revealed intellectual disability.

Physical examination: narrow forehead, no posterior forehead projection. Eyes widely spaced, palpebral fissures almond-shaped, upper eyelids drooping covering part of the pupils; no epicanthal folds. Broad nasal base, no nasal root prominence. Low-set ears. High palate. Hypotonic trunk; the child "falls" when sitting without support.

Complementary tests: brain MRI showing a slender corpus callosum, no cerebral atrophy.

findings.text: shortness of breath when climbing stairs
shortness of breath when walking longer distances
velcro-like crackles during inspiration in the base of the lungs
typical pattern of usual interstitial pneumonia
telomere length measurement below expected for age

translation:
Identification: male, 62 years old, referred to the pulmonology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: shortness of breath and cough.

Current illness history: patient reports experiencing shortness of breath when climbing stairs and walking longer distances, which improves with stopping and resting. He also reports a persistent dry cough without expectoration.

Physical examination: digital clubbing of fingers. Lung auscultation reveals velcro-like crackles during inspiration, in the base of the lungs.

Complementary tests: pulmonary function test showing reduced carbon monoxide diffusion capacity. High-resolution thoracic computed tomography showing typical pattern of usual interstitial pneumonia; report describes pulmonary fibrosis. Telomere length measurement in leukocytes below expected for age.

findings.text: small and malformed ears with posterior rotation

absent: calcifications in the subcortical white matter
translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: "she does not grow and lives with illness."

Current disease history: Mother reports that the child has always gained little weight and grown slowly since infancy, remaining significantly below other children. She states that the child frequently gets infections, one after another. She reports that the child took a long time to begin speaking and forming sentences. Denies hearing impairment. At school, the child is following the regular class; previous psychological evaluation did not reveal intellectual disability. Mother notes that the head has been becoming smaller over the years, although at birth it was of normal size.

History: Born prematurely, small for gestational age. Prenatal ultrasounds showed no evidence of intrauterine growth restriction.

Physical examination: Short stature. Microcephaly. Eyes widely spaced. Prominent nose. Small mandible. Small and malformed ears, with posterior rotation. Clinodactyly.

Complementary tests: Complete blood count showing neutropenia. Brain CT scan without calcifications in the basal nuclei and without calcifications in the subcortical white matter.

findings.text: muscle strength preserved in cervical and trunk muscles
fragmented red fibers on Gomori trichrome stain

translation:
Identification: Female, 61 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "Drooping eyelids and choking."

Current illness history: The patient reports that for years her eyelids have been drooping, to the point of covering part of her vision. She states difficulty swallowing food. Her daughter reports that her mother has been losing strength in her arms and legs, and that she currently cannot walk, although she used to be able to walk. No vomiting. No hearing loss.

Physical examination: Bilateral ptosis. Ophthalmoplegia with restricted extraocular movement. Peripheral upper and lower limb weakness. Muscle strength preserved in cervical and trunk muscles. No amyotrophy.

Complementary tests: Electromyography showing a myopathic pattern. Muscle biopsy revealing fragmented red fibers on Gomori trichrome stain and COX-negative fibers. Mitochondrial DNA analysis in muscle showing multiple deletions. AST within normal limits.

findings.text: heavy menstruations lasting more than one week
recurrent episodes of bleeding from the mouth
fingertips turning white, then red, then pink in cold weather

translation:
Identification: female patient, 70 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: reports that, throughout her reproductive life, menstruations were very heavy and lasted more than one week, although they occurred in regular intervals. Also reports recurrent episodes of bleeding from the mouth throughout her life. States that, in cold weather, her fingertips turn white, then red, and then become pink. Denies gastrointestinal bleeding. Denies prolonged bleeding after dental extractions.

Physical examination: skin without reticular livedo.

Complementary tests: normal bleeding time. Platelet count within normal limits.

Identification: female, 33 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: Reports difficulty with eating for years, with choking episodes and a sensation of food getting stuck. Already diagnosed with achalasia by a gastroenterologist. Also reports documented sensorineural hearing loss on audiometry. States that her skin is very dry and that she has always had very little body fat, from face to limbs. States that family members note she appears older due to severely wrinkled skin. Had prior ocular surgery for cataracts. Denies growth delay in childhood.

Physical examination: Height appropriate for age and sex, without short stature. Normal head circumference, without microcephaly. Triangular face, broad forehead, deep-set eyes, retruded midface third. Corneal opacity on inspection. Generalized lipodystrophy. Preserved muscle tone, without hypotonia.

Complementary tests: Echocardiogram showing thickened aortic valve cusps and aortic insufficiency. Lipid profile with hypercholesterolemia. Ophthalmological evaluation without retinal dystrophy.

findings.text: severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction below 30%

translation:
Identification: male, 16 years and 5 months old, referred to medical genetics by cardiology for evaluation, accompanied by mother.

Main complaint: "weak heart".

Current disease history: Patient under cardiology follow-up for congestive heart failure. Mother reports that the child has been followed for dilated cardiomyopathy.

Complementary tests: Echocardiogram showing severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, below 30%. Cardiac magnetic resonance showing myocardial fibrosis. Elevated NT-proBNP. 24-hour Holter monitor without episodes of ventricular tachycardia.

findings.text: difficulty organizing or planning daily activities
need for others to repeat themselves
hyperintensities in the deep white matter

absent: osmiophilic granular material deposits in vessels
translation:
Identification: female, 64 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: progressive memory loss.

Current illness history: The daughter reports that the patient has increasingly frequently forgotten people's names and appointments. She also states that she has lost mental abilities she previously had, and that she can no longer organize or plan daily activities, such as paying bills or preparing meals, without assistance. The patient complains of a constant ringing in her ears and says that she has difficulty hearing, requiring others to repeat themselves. She has had migraines for many years.

History: No history of hypertension.

Physical examination: Plantar reflexes bilaterally flexor, no Babinski sign.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI shows cerebral infarct and hyperintensities in the deep white matter, without reduction of white matter volume. Anticardiolipin IgG negative. Skin biopsy shows no osmiophilic granular material deposits in vessels.

absent: reduced bilateral tenar region volume in hands
translation:
Identification: male, 52 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of hematological abnormalities.

Main complaint: alteration in blood tests.

findings.text: rounded sperm heads with no identifiable acrosome

Regarding morphology, spermatozoa exhibit rounded heads with no identifiable acrosome. The tail shows irregular caliber along its course. No coiled flagella were observed.
