Physical examination: elongated face, oblique palpebral fissures downward, anteverted nares, long nasal bridge. No strabismus. Hands and feet with short fingers; broad hands. No syndactyly.

Identification: male, 23 years old, accompanied by mother.

Main complaint: referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Current illness history: mother reports that he spoke very late, with first words and phrases appearing much later than expected. Diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder since childhood. At school, the teacher observed that he could not stay still, was easily distracted by anything, and acted impulsively; diagnosed with ADHD. Presents intellectual disability, requiring support with daily activities. Mother reports that he has always been smaller than other children of the same age and grew slowly. Achieved sitting and walking at the expected age, without motor delay. Negates seizures. No aggressive behavior. Sleeps well, without sleep disturbances.

Physical examination: head circumference within normal limits for age and sex, no microcephaly.

findings.text: height below 3rd percentile for age and sex

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: "He does not grow and started speaking later than other children. He still speaks little for his age."

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child began speaking much later than other children and still speaks little for his age. He also started sitting and walking later than usual. She states that since infancy, he has grown slowly and is consistently shorter than his peers. She also reports that feeding has always been a problem: he has difficulty chewing and swallowing, and meals are prolonged. No different behaviors are reported, such as restlessness or isolation. Previous assessment did not identify intellectual disability.

Physical examination: Height below the 3rd percentile for age and sex. Low weight. Head circumference appropriate, without microcephaly. Facial shape deformity.

findings.text: extra fingers on hands and feet
right lung with only two lobes
duplication of the great toe of feet

absent: eyebrows not fused in the midline
translation:
Identification: male patient brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for multiple malformations.

Current disease history: parents report that at birth the infant had extra fingers on hands and feet. At birth, it was noted that the baby lacked an anal opening. Echocardiogram revealed a trunk artery without interventricular communication. Thoracic imaging showed a right lung with only two lobes. Brain MRI showed no agenesis of the corpus callosum. Radiograph of lower limbs showed no femoral shortening.

Physical examination: head circumference without macrocephaly. Frontal bones without widening. Eyebrows fused in the midline. Eyes well separated. Ears with low implantation. Small and retracted chin. Cleft palate. Hands with preaxial polydactyly and mesial polydactyly. Feet with duplication of the great toe and mesial polydactyly.

Identification: female adolescent, 15 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred by neurology for investigation.

Current disease history: mother reports that, since early childhood, the daughter had delayed milestones in sitting, walking, and social interaction, with developmental delay in all domains. She has never spoken any word. The mother also reports episodes of convulsive seizures. She states that the girl experiences episodes in which she hits people, shouts, and breaks objects at home. She has a prior assessment with diagnosis of intellectual disability.

Physical examination: skeletal muscle amyotrophy. Normal muscle tone in limbs, without appendicular hypotonia. Lips with usual thickness of erythema, without lip thinning. No nasal or ear elongation. Ears with normal implantation, not low. Nasal prominence absent.

findings.text: dark spot in the center of visual field
pallor of the optic disc temporal region

translation:
Identification: Female, 40 years old, referred to the neuro-ophthalmology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "My vision is getting worse."

Current illness history: Patient reports that she previously had good vision and over time has noticed a decline in vision. She describes a dark spot in the center of her visual field, which interferes when she focuses on an object. She also reports difficulty distinguishing colors. She complains of frequent headaches. She adds that she has been experiencing worsening hearing, and has already undergone audiometry, which revealed sensorineural hearing loss.

Physical examination: Visual acuity not reduced in this evaluation. Fundoscopy: optic atrophy; pallor of the optic disc temporal region.

findings.text: gastrostomy in first year of life
head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex
abnormal curvature of the spine in lateral and anteroposterior planes
complete absence of corpus callosum on brain MRI
patent foramen ovinale without ventricular communication and without pulmonary stenosis

absent: patent foramen ovale with ventricular communication
translation:
Identification: boy, 4 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child took a long time to hold his head up and sit, and to date he does not walk independently. He does not speak any words, only emitting sounds. He has episodes of convulsive seizures. Functionally, he is completely dependent on caregivers and has severe intellectual disability.

History: in the first year of life, he began to be fed via gastrostomy. Currently, he requires parenteral nutrition, as he is unable to receive sufficient intake either orally or through a tube. A previous echocardiogram showed a patent foramen ovale, without ventricular communication and without pulmonary stenosis.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Height below the 3rd percentile. Global hypotonia. Abnormal curvature of the spine in lateral and anteroposterior planes (cifoescoliosis). Hip dislocation. Knee dislocation.

Complementary tests: MRI of the brain with complete absence of the corpus callosum, not merely a thin corpus callosum. Lateral ventricles enlarged, without signs of hydrocephalus. No pachygyria.

findings.text: reduced proportion of spermatozoa moving forward in a straight line

translation:
Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by andrology.

Main complaint: unable to have children.

Current illness history: patient reports attempting to conceive with his partner for several years without success, and has been diagnosed with male infertility. He brings spermograms for evaluation.

Complementary tests: spermogram shows sperm concentration within the expected range, without oligozoospermia. Spermatozoa generally exhibit poor motility, with a significant reduction in the proportion moving forward in a straight line. In morphological analysis, many spermatozoa show short tails, and others have tails coiled upon themselves. No spermatozoa without tails were observed, nor any spermatozoa with bent flagella.

findings.text: NT-proANP below the lower limit of normality

translation:
Identification: Female, 48 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

Main complaint: Referral due to atrial arrhythmia.

Current illness history: Patient reports feeling her heart beating irregularly and out of rhythm. The electrocardiogram brought by the patient shows atrial fibrillation, with no atrial flutter recorded in the available tracings.

History: Long-standing hypertension, under clinical follow-up.

Physical examination: Irregular heart rhythm on auscultation.

Complementary tests: Echocardiogram shows enlarged left atrium with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. Cardiac magnetic resonance with delayed enhancement demonstrates fibrosis in the left atrium. Elevated BNP. NT-proANP below the lower limit of normality.

findings.text: global developmental delay in first years of life

translation:
Identification: male patient, 25 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for investigation of developmental delay since childhood.

Current disease history: mother reports that, as a child, he took a long time to sit, crawl, and walk, and also to grasp small objects with his fingers and hold utensils. She states that his first words came very late and that speech has always been significantly delayed compared to other children. She describes global developmental delay in the first years of life. She reports episodes of sudden, rapid muscle tremors, such as startle reactions, which cause arms to jump. Denies diagnosis of hypothyroidism.

History: mother denies polyhydramnios during pregnancy. No astigmatism.

Physical examination: microcephaly. Mouth permanently widely open, without a narrow mouth and without downturned labial commissures. Short philtrum. Micrognathia. Pointed chin. Fingertips tapered toward the tips. Short feet. Axial hypotonia. Spasticity.

findings.text: echocardiogram without persistence of the arterial canal

translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that the girl is delayed in all areas of development compared to other children of the same age. She states that the child took a long time to sit, crawl, and walk. She also notes that the child speaks very few words and does not form sentences. She additionally observes that one of the girl's eyes "turns inward."

History: echocardiogram without persistence of the arterial canal. Spinal resonance without siringomyelia.

Physical examination: oblique upward palpebral fissures. Low nasal bridge. Small mouth with downturned corners. Short chin, without retrognathia. Normal-sized uvula, not elongated. Esotropia on ophthalmologic examination. Global hypotonia. No joint hypermobility.

Identification: Female patient, 11 years and 6 months old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric endocrinology.

Main complaint: Assessment of ovarian developmental disorder.

Current disease history: Mother reports that the daughter experienced menarche later than expected, indicating delayed menarche. There is no primary amenorrhea.

Complementary tests: Pelvic ultrasonography shows ovarian aplasia. Hormonal assays reveal elevated FSH, elevated LH, and reduced antimüllerian hormone.

Identification: male patient brought by parents for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for investigation of hair changes and imaging study.

Current illness history: the mother reports that the child's hair breaks easily, even during brushing. She also notes that he has few eyelashes and that his eyebrows are sparse.

Physical examination: coarse facial features. Full cheeks. Narrow and high forehead, with anterior hairline placement.

Complementary tests: cranial magnetic resonance imaging showing cerebellar atrophy and a thin corpus callosum.

Identification: female, 34 years old, referred by the assisted reproduction clinic for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "I am unable to get pregnant."

Current illness history: Patient reports having tried to conceive for years without success, with a diagnosis of infertility made by the human reproduction team. She has undergone several in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles, in which the transferred embryos, described as of good quality, never implanted. According to the clinic reports, in IVF/ICSI cycles, the oocytes retrieved failed to complete maturation and remained blocked in an immature stage, rendering attempts with these oocytes impossible.

Physical examination: no particular findings to report during this visit.

findings.text: limited passive range of motion of hips
limited passive range of motion of shoulders
increased space between hallux and second pododactyl

translation:
Identification: girl, 13 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: mother reports that the child had delayed sitting, walking, and interacting during early development, falling behind other children in all areas. She began speaking her first words and phrases much later than expected. Currently, she attends school with significant difficulty and has been diagnosed with intellectual disability following neuropsychological assessment. The mother states that her speech is circumstantial and difficult for people unfamiliar with her to understand. She denies the presence of rapid, involuntary muscle movements. She wears glasses for astigmatism.

Physical examination: head circumference above the 97th percentile. Ears with normal implantation. Palpebral fissures without downward deviation. Nasal tip without projection. Global muscular hypotonia. Limited passive range of motion of hips and shoulders. In the feet, increased space between the hallux and the second pododactyl.

Complementary tests: EEG with abnormal tracing. Brain MRI without hypomyelination.

findings.text: previous ophthalmological assessment describes macular dystrophy

translation:
Identification: female patient, 39 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by ophthalmology for evaluation.

Main complaint: referred due to finding observed during fundus examination.

Current illness history: patient reports good vision, without noticing any deterioration of distant or near vision. Denies any central visual field defect or blind spot when fixating gaze on objects.

Physical examination: visual acuity preserved in both eyes. Fundoscopy: bilateral temporal optic disc pallor; macular atrophy present in both eyes.

Complementary tests: fundus autofluorescence shows hypoautofluorescent lesions in the retina. Previous ophthalmological assessment describes macular dystrophy.

findings.text: enlarged tongue occupying entire oral cavity

translation:
Identification: male, 15 years and 11 months old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for investigation of developmental abnormalities.

Current illness history: mother reports that he delayed significantly in speaking his first words and forming sentences. She also states that he had difficulty with holding small objects, buttoning clothes, and using utensils, achieving these skills much later than his siblings. He has a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder. Mother denies episodes of esophagitis.

Past medical history: in the neonatal period, persistent arterial canal was identified.

Physical examination: head circumference without macrocephaly. Broad forehead. Hypoplasia of the midface. Nose of normal length with broad nasal tip. Upper lip with fine redness. Normal mouth width. Enlarged tongue, occupying the entire oral cavity. Large ear lobes; no pre-auricular appendages. Excessive body hair. Digital clubbing. Hallux valgus.

findings.text: spermatozoa with more than one flagellum attached to the head

translation:
Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by urology.

Main complaint: difficulty conceiving children.

Current disease history: patient reports that, together with his partner, he has been trying to conceive for some time without success; he was evaluated by urology and diagnosed with male infertility. He brings a spermogram for assessment.

Complementary tests: spermogram shows sperm concentration within the reference range, without oligozoospermia. Asthenozoospermia is present, with reduced progressive motility. Morphological analysis reveals spermatozoa without flagella, spermatozoa with short flagella, flagella coiled upon themselves, and spermatozoa with more than one flagellum attached to the head.

findings.text: morphological alteration of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: female, 34 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of changes on cranial magnetic resonance imaging.

Main complaint: recurrent headache.

Current illness history: patient reports long-standing, episodic migraine attacks. No history of seizures. No history of episodes of altered consciousness. Family companion reports no behavioral changes. No difficulty walking.

Physical examination: gait without abnormalities.

Complementary tests: cranial magnetic resonance imaging shows cerebral atrophy, morphological alteration of the corpus callosum, alteration of the globus pallidus, and alteration of the cerebellar peduncles. Diffusion sequence shows no abnormalities.

findings.text: sudden successive contractions with trunk flexion and arm elevation
focal seizures with impairment of consciousness
no memory of seizure episodes afterward

absent: prolonged non-motor seizure without epileptic non-convulsive status epilepticus
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents, referred to the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of epileptic seizures.

Main complaint: epileptic seizures and developmental delay.

Current illness history: parents report that, already in the first year of life, the child began to have episodes of sudden, successive contractions, characterized by trunk flexion and arm elevation, repeated multiple times consecutively. Subsequently, episodes occurred in which the boy becomes motionless, with fixed gaze, does not respond when called, and has no memory of the event afterward, a presentation described as focal seizures with impairment of consciousness. Parents deny that these seizures progress to generalized limb convulsions. They deny that seizures are triggered by fever. There has never been an episode of prolonged non-motor seizure without epileptic non-convulsive status epilepticus.

History: the mother noticed that the child delayed in holding his head up, sitting, babbling, and interacting with people, falling behind other children of the same age in all areas.

Physical examination: child in good general condition, no other abnormalities to note at this visit.

findings.text: reduced proportion of B memory cells
reduced levels of CD4+ memory effector T cells
reduced levels of CD8+ memory effector T cells

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by mother, referred to the immunology/genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: fever and recurrent infections.

Current disease history: mother reports that the child has had frequent episodes of throat pain, ear pain, and sinusitis since early childhood, requiring multiple visits per year. For several weeks, she has had fever.

Physical examination: liver and spleen enlarged on abdominal palpation.

Complementary tests: complete blood count showing anemia, leukocytosis, and lymphopenia; no lymphocytosis; platelet count normal. LDH elevated. Bilirubin levels within normal limits. Immunophenotyping: increased absolute number of B lymphocytes, reduced proportion of B memory cells, reduced levels of CD4+ memory effector T cells and CD8+ memory effector T cells. No antibody response to tetanus vaccine. EBV PCR in blood persistently positive in serial testing.

findings.text: stumbles due to inability to lift tips of feet
distal muscle atrophy in upper and lower limbs
reduced muscle strength in distal upper and lower limb muscles

translation:
Identification: female, 45 years old, referred to the neurogenetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: difficulty walking since childhood.

Current disease history: the patient reports that she started walking later than her siblings and has always walked on the tips of her feet. She states that over the years her legs have become increasingly stiff, and currently she stumbles because she is unable to lift the tips of her feet. She also notes that her hands have become thinner and weaker, with difficulty buttoning clothes. No urgency to urinate. No tremor observed during movements or when holding objects.

History: no learning difficulties in school or professional life; no intellectual disability.

Physical examination: spastic gait. Spasticity in lower limbs. Hyperreflexia, with bilateral Achilles reflexes abolished. Babinski sign present. Distal muscle atrophy in upper and lower limbs. Reduced muscle strength in distal upper and lower limb muscles, with foot dorsiflexor paralysis. Flat feet, no cavus foot, and hammer toes. Spine without hyperlordosis.

Complementary tests: electromyography showing axonal motor neuropathy.

Identification: male patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by andrology.

Main complaint: the couple is unable to conceive.

Current illness history: patient reports attempts at conception with his partner, without success, which led to investigation and diagnosis of male infertility. He brings a spermogram for evaluation.

Additional tests: spermogram shows sperm concentration below 20 million/mL, structural abnormalities in sperm heads, and reduced progressive motility.

Management: patient is continuing outpatient follow-up.

findings.text: reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes

translation:
Identification: girl, 12 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: fevers that come and go.

Current illness history: mother reports recurrent episodes of fever over the years. She also describes episodic vomiting, occurring intermittently with symptom-free intervals between episodes, and in some instances the child became dehydrated. She states that the girl is very drowsy and has difficulty staying awake. The child has already experienced seizure episodes.

History: surgical correction of inguinal hernia. Mother reports a previously identified hepatic abnormality during prior follow-up. No global developmental delay in early childhood.

Physical examination: intact palate, no cleft palate.

Complementary tests: anemia. Elevated C-reactive protein. Low serum IgG. Immunophenotyping with reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes and inverted CD4/CD8 ratio. Brain MRI showing pineal cyst.

findings.text: sensation of pressure in the face

translation:
Identification: male, 52 years old, referred to the pneumology/genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

Main complaint: long-standing respiratory problems.

Current illness history: patient reports having lived with nasal congestion, nasal discharge, and a sensation of pressure in the face for many years, with no complete resolution, and with periodic worsening. He states he underwent a previous surgery for removal of "growths" inside the nose.

Physical examination: anterior rhinoscopy reveals bilateral nasal polyps.

Complementary tests: thoracic CT shows bronchiectasis. Facial sinuses CT shows chronic sinusitis. Nasal nitric oxide level is reduced. Echocardiogram shows no alteration in the spatial arrangement of cardiac segments.

findings.text: tiring quickly during play and physical education
increased variability in fiber size on muscle biopsy

absent: rolling waves of contraction throughout the muscular belly
translation:
Identification: girl, 11 years and 6 months, brought by mother, referred to the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: mother reports that the girl tires very quickly during play and physical education, needing to stop before her peers. Denies muscle pain. No difficulty with eating, chewing, or swallowing.

Physical examination: on muscular percussion with reflex hammer, no persistent localized muscle bulging is observed, nor rolling waves of contraction throughout the muscular belly.

Complementary tests: serum creatine kinase (CK) elevated. Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) within normal limits. Muscle biopsy brought by the family: increased variability in fiber size.

findings.text: red, very itchy plaques in the folds of the arms
red, very itchy plaques behind the knees
excessive skin flaking on the legs
diffuse scaling of an ichthyotic appearance on limbs and trunk

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "dry skin and itching since childhood."

Current disease history: Patient reports that since childhood, he has had red, very itchy plaques in the folds of the arms and behind the knees, which worsen and improve throughout the year. He also states that his entire body skin flakes excessively, with dry scales, especially on the legs. He reports having a chronically stuffy and runny nose for years, without lasting improvement. He notes that he has difficulty hearing, requiring increasing the television volume.

History: Asthma since childhood. Hypothyroidism under endocrinology follow-up.

Physical examination: Good general condition. Skin with diffuse scaling of an ichthyotic appearance on limbs and trunk; eczema in antecubital and popliteal fossae. Telangiectasias in malar and nasal regions.

Complementary tests: Tonal audiometry brought by the patient shows sensorineural hearing loss.

findings.text: skin folds covering inner corners of both eyes

translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: "developmental delay".

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always been slower than other children in all developmental stages. She states that he took a long time to begin walking independently. She also reports that he had difficulty speaking and still uses few words to request what he wants, although he appears to understand what is said to him. Since early childhood, the family has noticed that one of his eyes "stays crooked".

Complementary tests: brain MRI brought by family shows delayed myelination, without cerebellar vermis atrophy. Echocardiogram shows no patent foramen ovale.

Physical examination: skin folds covering the inner corners of both eyes. Low-set ears. Palpebral fissures without upward tilt. Eyebrows without marked arched appearance. Nasal openings not anteverted. Strabismus. Hypotonia. Hyperreflexia.

Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrician for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has always taken longer than other children to sit, walk, and play, showing global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. She states that he started speaking very late and still speaks only a few words, significantly fewer than peers of the same age. She also reports that he frequently swings his hands repeatedly, especially when excited.

Physical examination: appropriate height for age, no short stature. Triangular facial shape, wider at the temples and tapering toward the chin. Deep-set eyes. Lips with fine redness. No retrognathia. Ears without posterior rotation. Long and slender fingers of hands. Flat feet at orthostasis.

Complementary tests: cranial MRI without cleft of the septum pellucidum and without schizencephaly.

findings.text: resting hand tremors when hands are stationary and supported on thighs
difficulty with reasoning and problem-solving in daily life
push-test with retrograde movement requiring support from the examiner

absent: resting hand tremors when hands are stationary and supported on thighs
difficulty with reasoning and problem-solving in daily life
translation:
Identification: Male, 74 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of a movement disorder. Accompanied by his wife.

Current illness history: The wife reports that he has resting hand tremors when his hands are stationary and supported on his thighs, which diminishes when he picks up objects. She notes that he has experienced frequent falls at home. She observes that his handwriting has become progressively smaller. The family has noticed that he is becoming more forgetful and has difficulty with reasoning and problem-solving in daily life. A parkinsonian syndrome with good response to dopaminergic therapy, according to the source service report. The wife also describes involuntary body twisting movements throughout the day.

Past medical history: Gastric ulcer. Neoplasm under follow-up.

Physical examination: Push-test with retrograde movement, requiring support from the examiner.

findings.text: globally hyperreflexia in deep tendon reflexes
slowness and irregularity during rapid alternation between pronation and supination of hands

translation:
Identification: female, 32 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: difficulty walking.

Current illness history: patient reports that she has been walking progressively worse, tripping, and requiring support. She also states difficulty maintaining standing position for long periods and feels weakness in her legs. She complains of urinary incontinence. Denies memory loss or decline in intellectual abilities; family members confirm that she continues working and organizing herself normally. Denies weakness in her arms.

Past medical history: denies chronic liver disease; previous evaluation reported no cirrhosis.

Physical examination: nystagmus on lateral gaze. Spastic ataxia presentation. Spastic hypertonia in lower limbs. Globally hyperreflexia in deep tendon reflexes. Babinski sign present. Lower limb paresis, with preserved strength in upper limbs. On the index-nose test, misses the target, overshooting it. Slowness and irregularity during rapid alternation between pronation and supination of hands. Preserved muscle trophism, without amyotrophy.

Complementary tests: brain MRI brought by the patient shows no cerebellar atrophy.

findings.text: does not respond when called from a distance
significant effort required for bowel movements

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 22 years old, accompanied by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: Mother reports that during early childhood, the daughter delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting, falling behind other children in all areas. She also states that, after acquiring some skills, the daughter lost previously acquired abilities. Currently, the patient has intellectual disability. In adolescence, she developed a psychotic episode, managed in psychiatry. The family reports that she experiences episodes in which she shouts, curses, hits people, and breaks objects, and tends to bite and scratch her own body until causing injury. The mother denies that the patient is overly nervous or anxious. They also note that she has poor hearing and does not respond when called from a distance.

History of illness: Gastroesophageal reflux disease. Mother reports that for years the patient has had infrequent bowel movements, approximately once a week, with hard stools and significant effort required. Hyperopia on ophthalmological follow-up. Denies cardiac disease, with no ventricular septal defect.

Physical examination: Overweight. Strabismus on ocular examination. Normal muscle tone, without hypotonia. Spine without kyphosis. Feet with preserved plantar arch, no flat feet.

findings.text: thin translucent skin with visible veins
wide violaceous striae in abdomen and flanks
primary micronodular adrenal cortical disease with pigmentation

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "shortness of breath and fatigue."

Current illness history: Patient reports shortness of breath and inability to keep up with peers during physical activities, becoming extremely fatigued well before expected. Mother noticed that his face has become noticeably rounded and swollen, his abdomen has significantly enlarged, and there is a noticeable accumulation of fat on the neck. She also observed dark spots on his lips.

Physical examination: Thin, translucent skin with visible veins due to translucency. Wide violaceous striae in abdomen and flanks.

Complementary tests: Elevated serum cortisol. Increased free urinary cortisol. Suppressed plasma ACTH. Echocardiogram showing a cardiac myxoma. Histopathological examination of the adrenal glands revealed primary micronodular adrenal cortical disease with pigmentation.

Identification: female, 33 years old, referred by hematology to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: evaluation of hematological abnormalities.

Current disease history: patient reports ongoing hematology follow-up due to pancytopenia on serial hemograms, with thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and macrocytic anemia. Bone marrow biopsy and marrow smear revealed hypocellular marrow and dyserythropoiesis. Denies hearing loss. Denies any tumor diagnosis to date.

Physical examination: height within expected range for age and sex. Face shows malar hypoplasia, short chin, and small mandible. Palate with submucosal cleft on inspection and palpation. Hands with short fifth digits bilaterally and clinodactyly of the fifth digits. Nipples without increased separation. Perineal region without fistula.

findings.text: vision limited to directly in front of him

translation:
Identification: male patient referred by ophthalmology for genetic medicine evaluation.

Main complaint: difficulty seeing at night.

Current disease history: the patient reports poor vision in dark or low-light environments, frequently tripping at dusk. He also states that he now collides with objects located beside him, noting that he can only see clearly what is directly in front of him, "as if looking through a tube." Previous ophthalmological assessment concluded with rod and cone dystrophy.

History: denies seizures. Family denies diagnosis of autism or suggestive behavioral patterns.

Physical examination: no obesity. No hemiplegia on the right side.

Complementary tests: visual acuity with mild reduction, ranging from 20/40 to 2 as 20/70.

findings.text: embryos ceased dividing before adequate stage

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 29 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by the assisted reproduction clinic.

Main complaint: "I am unable to get pregnant."

Current illness history: Patient reports infertility, which is the reason she underwent in vitro fertilization cycles. According to the assisted reproduction clinic report, in part of the cycles, embryos ceased dividing before reaching an adequate stage for transfer. In cycles where embryos of good quality were transferred, implantation did not occur, a situation that repeated itself after multiple attempts.

Management: Follow-up in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

findings.text: ptosis on both sides of the eyelids
decreased muscle strength in all four limbs
global abolition of deep tendon reflexes
fragmented red fibers on Gomori trichrome staining
deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes

translation:
Identification: female, 34 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: fatigue and weakness.

Current illness history: reports persistent fatigue for years, with lack of energy that does not improve with rest. States difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair, as well as weakness in arms and legs. Reports recurrent infections, having previously been evaluated for immunodeficiency. Negates seizures.

Past medical history: prior cardiac evaluation without evidence of cardiomyopathy.

Physical examination: high palate. Ptosis on both sides of the eyelids. Ophthalmoplegia. Decreased muscle strength in all four limbs, with predominant proximal involvement. Global abolition of deep tendon reflexes.

Complementary tests: elevated creatine kinase. Normal triglycerides. Normal transaminases. Electromyography without peripheral neuropathy. Muscle biopsy showing fragmented red fibers on Gomori trichrome staining, increased fiber diameter variation, and COX-negative fibers; biochemical study revealed deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes. DNA mitochondrial analysis of muscle tissue demonstrated multiple deletions.

findings.text: sentence production below expected for age
wakes up several times during night

translation:
Identification: boy, 8 years and 9 months, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child took slightly longer than other children to sit, walk, and achieve the other developmental milestones, with a mild delay considered. He started speaking late and still has a vocabulary and sentence production below expected for his age. At school, he follows with difficulty; neuropsychological assessment concluded mild intellectual disability. He has a diagnosis of ADHD made by pediatric neurology. Mother reports that he has poor sleep, wakes up several times during the night, and has an agitated sleep. Negates hearing loss; family reports that he hears well.

Physical examination: Height above the 97th percentile for age and sex. No hypertelorism. Auricular pavilions of normal size, no macrotyia. No esotropia. Feet with preserved plantar arch, no flat feet.

Complementary tests: Ophthalmological assessment shows hypermetropia. EEG abnormal.

findings.text: eyes trembling from side to side
head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex

translation:
Identification: male child, 1 year of age, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: mother notes that her child is slightly delayed compared to other children of the same age in sitting, crawling, and interacting, although she considers this delay to be mild. She also reports that the child has not spoken any words and barely makes sounds. She additionally observes that his eyes "tremble" from side to side continuously.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 standard deviations for age and sex. Low-set ears with enlarged size. Prominent nose, without nasal lengthening. Oblique palpebral fissures upward. Absence of bitemporal depression. Nystagmus present; no exotropia. Involuntary movements with poor coordination, showing instability when attempting to reach objects, indicating ataxia. Presence of bulbar signs. Muscle tone preserved, without hypotonia.

Complementary tests: hepatic transaminases without elevation.

absent: joint dislocation beyond what was expected in childhood
translation:
Identification: Male, 39 years and 6 months, presented alone, referred from orthopedics for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: Joint pain.

Current illness history: Patient reports joint pain for several years, mainly at the end of the day. States that his joints sometimes become swollen. He also notes that he can no longer bend and stretch some joints as he used to. Family members have commented that he walks "rocking," swaying his hip from side to side.

History: Has always been the shortest among his peers. Denies having had a joint dislocation beyond what was expected in childhood.

Physical examination: Short stature. Anserine gait. Reduced joint range of motion. No kyphosis of the spine. No genu varum and no genu valgum in lower limbs.

Complementary tests: Bone densitometry showing decreased bone mineral density.

findings.text: diminished vibration sensation in distal extremities

translation:
Identification: male, 47 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: difficulty walking.

Current illness history: Patient reports difficulty walking. Denies weakness in the legs.

Physical examination: Spastic paraplegia. Patellar reflexes hyperactive bilaterally. Achilles reflexes hyperactive. No ankle clonus. No patellar clonus. Babinski sign present. Hoffmann's sign present. Vibration sensation diminished in distal extremities.

Complementary tests: Electromyography shows reduced motor conduction velocity, reduced sensory conduction velocity, and motor conduction block.

findings.text: red plaques in arm and knee creases
intense itching in arm and knee creases
food allergies to milk and eggs

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "delayed development and many allergies".

Current illness history: parents report that he delayed sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting compared to other children. Since early infancy, he has had dry skin with red plaques and intense itching in the arm and knee creases, which worsen over time. He experiences reactions after ingesting certain foods, such as milk and eggs. He reports recurrent episodes of pneumonia and bronchitis over the years, as well as recurrent fungal infections. He has a diarrhea with mucus and blood; colonoscopy revealed colitis, and biopsy showed eosinophilic infiltrate in the colon. Parents deny having seizures. No history of recurrent skin infections.

History: intrauterine growth restriction during gestation. At birth, head circumference below -2 standard deviations. Follow-up with ophthalmology for high myopia.

Physical examination: microcephaly. Marked thoracic kyphosis. Perineal fistula. Uvula without bifidness.

Complementary tests: complete blood count with eosinophilia. Elevated serum IgE, with monoclonal band on electrophoresis. Serum IgA without reduction. Echocardiogram without structural cardiac abnormalities.

findings.text: erythematous, scaly, intensely pruritic plaques in elbow and knee flexural regions
widespread warts distributed over neck, trunk, arms, and legs
extensive and atypical molluscum contagiosum with hundreds of umbilicated papules
reduced absolute number of CD3+ T lymphocytes
decreased percentage of CD8+ T cells
proportional reduction of naive CD4+ and naive CD-8+ T cells
low T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs)

absent: normal T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs)
translation:
Identification: male, 24 years, referred to the clinical immunology outpatient clinic for investigation.

Main complaint: recurrent skin lesions.

Current disease history: patient reports erythematous, scaly, and intensely pruritic plaques in the elbow and knee flexural regions for a long time. He also describes widespread warts distributed over the neck, trunk, arms, and legs. No reduction in sweating. Presented with prior diagnosis of combined immunodeficiency, previously managed with autoimmune thrombocytopenia.

Physical examination: erythematous, scaly plaques in flexural areas. Multiple cutaneous warts in the neck, trunk, and limbs. Extensive and atypical molluscum contagiosum with hundreds of umbilicated papules. Hair of usual thickness and texture, not fine.

Complementary tests: lymphopenia. Reduced absolute number of CD3+ T lymphocytes. Decreased percentage of CD8+ T cells. Proportional reduction of naive CD4+ and naive CD8+ T cells. Reduced lymphoproliferative response to phytohemagglutinin. Oligoclonal T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire. Low T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs). Eosinophils within normal limits. Normal serum IgA and IgG levels.

findings.text: frequent episodes of distress, restlessness, and agitation
fine, very curly, tightly coiled hair with a woolly appearance
right testicle not palpable in the scrotal sac

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years and 11 months, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Main complaint: developmental delay and school difficulties.

Current illness history: mother reports that since infancy, he has been delayed in achieving developmental milestones across all domains. He walked alone much later than his siblings. He started speaking late and still has a speech that is inadequate for his age. She reports frequent episodes in which the child becomes extremely distressed, restless, and agitated, sometimes leading to hitting people and himself. School psychological assessment indicates mild intellectual disability. Mother denies episodes of staring or loss of contact and does not report automatisms. The child interacts well with other children, maintains eye contact, and does not exhibit repetitive behaviors or restricted interests.

Physical examination: head circumference appropriate for age, no microcephaly. Height within expected range, no short stature. Fine, very curly, tightly coiled hair with a woolly appearance. Cardiac auscultation shows no murmurs; previous echocardiogram showed no ventricular communication. Genitalia: right testicle not palpable in the scrotal sac, left testicle is topical.

Complementary tests: brain MRI revealed absence of olfactory bulb.

findings.text: head circumference below expected values at birth
episodes of immobility with blank gaze
difficulties with thinking, reasoning, and remembering
dependence on others for daily activities

translation:
Identification: male, 19 years old, accompanied by mother, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Current illness history: Mother reports that since birth, the head has been small, with head circumference below expected values at birth. In the early years, there was global developmental delay; sitting and walking were achieved with significant delay, and speech development also occurred late. He has always been a "floppy" infant. He experiences episodes in which he becomes immobile, with a blank gaze, unresponsive to surroundings. He has significant difficulties with thinking, reasoning, and remembering things, and depends on others for daily activities, with severe intellectual disability. Mother also noted from an early age that the eyes "do not align."

Physical examination: Face with atypical morphology. Small mandible. Strabismus. Nystagmus (horizontal). Dysmetric saccadic movements. Axial hypotonia. Spasticity in lower limbs. Hyperreflexia of tendon reflexes. No intention tremor on index-nose test. Speech without dysarthria. No joint hypermobility. Nails without dysplasia.

Complementary tests: Fundoscopic examination without optic nerve hypoplasia.

findings.text: double superior vena cava (right and left)
heart in normal position in the left hemithorax
angular deviation of fingers at the interphalangeal joint level
significant dilatation of the renal pelvises

translation:
Identification: male patient brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred by pediatric cardiology for investigation.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child has "catching colds that descend to the chest," with multiple respiratory infection episodes throughout the year. The child has an asthma diagnosis under ongoing follow-up. Previous bronchoscopy described bronchomalacia. The child is under follow-up for high blood pressure, which has been confirmed in several consultations.

History: echocardiography and angiography reveal ventricular septal defect, anomalous pulmonary venous drainage, and double superior vena cava (right and left). The heart is in normal position in the left hemithorax, without dextrocardia. There is no transposition of the great arteries; the left ventricle has preserved dimensions, without hypoplasia; the pulmonary valve is patent, without atresia; and the coronary sinus is not dilated. Abdominal imaging shows abdominal organs without defined lateralization, with multiple small spleens, in addition to significant dilatation of the pelvis and renal pelvises.

Physical examination: ears with posterior rotation. Thorax with sternal depression. Angular deviation of fingers at the interphalangeal joint level.

findings.text: inability to coordinate mouth to form words
increased errors as word or phrase becomes longer
head hitting against wall when upset
muscle tone neither hypotonic nor hypertonic

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Main complaint: cognitive delay and speech difficulty.

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child has intellectual disability, attended in school with special educational support. She states that the child has had seizures since childhood. She reports that the child knows what he wants to say, but is unable to coordinate his mouth to form words, making more errors as the word or phrase becomes longer. She also observes that the child bites his own lips and hits his head against the wall when upset. Denies having sudden, unexplained laughing episodes. Denies having difficulty hearing.

Physical examination: Head appears disproportionately large in relation to the body, with head circumference within 2 standard deviations. Slow and incoordinate voluntary movements. Muscle tone neither hypotonic nor hypertonic. No convergent eye deviation.

findings.text: severe muscle pain throughout the body

absent: increase in volume of the lower limb muscles
muscular hypertrophy in the upper limbs
translation:
Identification: Female, 45 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

Main complaint: Previous episode of muscular destruction.

Current disease history: Patient reports that, during a viral infection, she developed rhabdomyolysis triggered by the viral illness, with severe muscle pain throughout her body. She states that during this period she noticed dark urine, colored like Coca-Cola, and the healthcare team documented myoglobinuria. Hospital admission records indicate acute rhabdomyolysis complicated by acute renal injury.

Physical examination: No increase in volume of the lower limb muscles. No muscular hypertrophy in the upper limbs.

findings.text: delay in beginning to walk independently
eyes set in a recessed position on the face

absent: acting without thinking or in an uncontrolled manner
translation:
Identification: girl, 7 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred by pediatrician for investigation of development.

Current illness history: mother reports that the girl took longer than other children to begin walking independently. She notes that, in general, the girl has always been slightly slower in acquiring age-appropriate skills, with mild global developmental delay. The mother also observes that "one eye sometimes drifts". She denies that the child acts without thinking or in an uncontrolled manner; describes the child as capable of waiting and following. She denies any heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding. She denies any tumor ever diagnosed.

Physical examination: strabismus on ophthalmologic examination. Eyes set in a recessed position on the face. Normal forehead, without prominent brow. Eyebrows without elongated hairs.

findings.text: frequent bumping into objects beside him
narrowing of visual field at peripheries
slightly reduced visual acuity in both eyes
speckled pigmentation at the peripheral retinal margin
concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field

translation:
Identification: male patient, 69 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for ophthalmological evaluation.

Main complaint: difficulty seeing at night.

Current illness history: the patient reports that he cannot see well at night or in poorly lit environments. He also states that he frequently bumps into objects beside him, noting that his visual field has been narrowing at the peripheries.

History: denies high myopia.

Physical examination: slightly reduced visual acuity, approximately 20/50 in both eyes. Fundoscopy: optic disc pallor, retinal pigment epithelium atrophy, and speckled pigmentation at the peripheral retinal margin.

Complementary tests: perimetry shows concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field, without annular scotoma.

findings.text: small for gestational age at birth
testes with reduced volume on palpation
IGF-1 below lower limit of normality

translation:
Identification: male, 32 years and 8 months old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: the mother reports that during pregnancy, she was informed that the baby was small for gestational age, with restricted uterine growth. After birth, she noticed that the child grew slowly, always smaller than other children. She also reports that the head has been becoming smaller over the years, although at birth it appeared to be of normal size. The patient has seizures. He completed his studies without specific difficulties in reading, writing, or attention; there is no intellectual disability.

Physical examination: short stature. Microcephaly. Scrotum in a sling. Testes with reduced volume on palpation. No café-au-lait spots. Normal nasal aperture (columella) insertion.

Complementary tests: anemia. Elevated TSH, with free T4 not reduced. IGF-1 below the lower limit of normality.

findings.text: developmental delay since first year of life
repeated hand and trunk swinging without purpose
short stature for age and sex

translation:
Identification: boy, 15 years old, brought by mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

Current disease history: Mother reports significant developmental delay in all developmental stages since the first year of life. He began walking independently only after his siblings. He has never spoken any words. He has always had difficulty with feeding, taking a long time during meals, and having trouble chewing and swallowing. He does not interact with others, does not seek contact, and remains stuck in the same activities and routines. He repeatedly swings his hands and trunk, without any apparent purpose. He presents generalized seizures and focal seizures, with episodes of epileptic status. Mother denies episodes of epileptic spasms. Has intellectual disability diagnosed in previous evaluation.

Physical examination: Short stature for age and sex. Absence of pubertal signs, indicating delayed puberty for age. Global hypotonia. Gait with widened base.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI shows a cleft of the septum pellucidum. No cerebral atrophy, adequate myelination, normal subarachnoid space, and normal thickness of the corpus callosum.

Identification: female patient, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: mother reports that the daughter always took longer than other children to sit, walk, speak, and use her hands. She also states that, at a certain point, the girl stopped doing things she previously knew, losing previously acquired skills. The patient has episodes of convulsive seizures. Neuropsychological evaluation revealed intellectual disability. Mother denies food intolerance.

History: on follow-up for hypothyroidism. No renal insufficiency. Echocardiogram shows no ventricular communication.

Physical examination: global hypotonia. Palate of normal width, without narrowing. Auricles well formed, without microtia.

findings.text: right lung with only two lobes

absent: deviation of fifth toes toward the hallux
abnormal brain MRI findings other than enlarged ventricles
translation:
Identification: female patient brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: referred for investigation of malformative findings.

Current disease history: parents report that since early childhood they have noticed that their daughter's jaw is small and retracted. They bring previous imaging studies.

Physical examination: micrognathia. Feet with straight fifth toes, without deviation toward the hallux.

Brain MRI showing enlarged ventricles; cerebellum of normal volume, without hypoplasia; corpus callosum of normal thickness, without thinning. Thoracic CT showing right lung with only two lobes; costal arches without fusions. Echocardiogram without tetralogy of Fallot.

findings.text: care in neonatal intensive care unit

translation:
Identification: male patient, 20 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: the mother reports that shortly after birth the child had significant respiratory difficulty, requiring care in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). In the first weeks of life, he underwent surgery for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. He states that he still tires easily and experiences shortness of breath, struggling to breathe with effort.

Physical examination: narrow thorax in the lateral direction, without a funnel-shaped appearance. No lumbar scoliosis present.

Complementary tests: thoracic X-ray shows short ribs and only 11 pairs of ribs, without thoracic dysplasia. Previous imaging report describes pulmonary hypoplasia. Echocardiogram shows no structural cardiac abnormalities.

findings.text: epilepsy with staring episodes and small rhythmic upward arm jerks
bilateral tonic-clonic seizures with generalized onset

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child has always been delayed in all aspects compared to other children during the early years of life. He walked alone much later than expected. He started speaking very late and still has a very poor speech. He has severe intellectual disability and is dependent for daily activities. The mother noticed that he repeatedly shakes his hands and trunk, without any apparent purpose. She also observed that his head has been getting smaller with growth, although it was normal at birth. He has epilepsy with several types of seizures: episodes in which he stops what he is doing, stares blankly, and his arms make small, rhythmic jerks that move upward; repetitive rhythmic shaking episodes; and bilateral tonic-clonic seizures starting from generalized onset.

Physical examination: Short stature. Microcephaly. Eyes widely spaced. Strabismus. Fingers of hands of normal length and thickness, without arachnodactyly. Patellar reflexes absent. Gait without instability.

Complementary tests: Abdominal ultrasound shows no dilation of intrahepatic biliary ducts. Hepatic elastography shows no fibrosis.

findings.text: increased range of motion in joints

translation:
Identification: girl, 9 years old, brought by mother, referred by pediatrician for evaluation in medical genetics.

Current illness history: mother reports that the child had significant delays in reaching all developmental milestones during early childhood. She began speaking words and sentences much later than other children. She also had difficulty holding a pencil, buttoning clothes, and grasping small objects with her fingers. Diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) by a pediatric neurologist. Neuropsychological assessment concluded intellectual disability.

History: previous renal ultrasound showed duplication of the pelvicaliceal system. Echocardiogram showed no ventricular septal defect. Brain MRI showed no cerebellar atrophy and normal-sized olfactory bulbs.

Physical examination: elongated face, deep-set eyes, large ears. Normal frontal width. Normally shaped pupils. High palate. Joints with increased range of motion. Bilateral cavovarus feet.

findings.text: episodes of strong and rapid heart beating in the chest

translation:
Identification: male patient, age not specified, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology.

Main complaint: "heart racing".

Current illness history: Patient reports episodes in which he feels his heart beating strongly and rapidly in the chest. No history of myocarditis.

Physical examination: No muscular dystrophy noted on neuromuscular examination.

Complementary tests: Echocardiogram brought by the patient shows hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with interventricular septal hypertrophy. 24-hour Holter monitor reveals sinus bradycardia, first-degree atrioventricular block, and periods of second-degree atrioventricular block. No atrial flutter, ventricular tachycardia, or ventricular extrasystoles were recorded.

findings.text: episodes of motionlessness and detachment from surroundings
loose, wrinkled, and hanging skin with poor elasticity

translation:
Identification: female patient, 19 years old, accompanied by mother, referred for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Current disease history: mother reports that as a child, the daughter delayed reaching all developmental milestones. She only managed to sit independently well after other children and began walking late. She also took a long time to speak her first words and form sentences. During school years, neuropsychological assessment revealed moderate intellectual disability, without criteria for severe level. Several years ago, she stopped walking, although she had previously walked. She experiences episodes during which she becomes motionless, detached from her surroundings, and does not respond when called; denies episodes with muscle rigidity and generalized tremors. Reports episodes during which she experiences difficult and fatiguing breathing. Has had numerous otitis throughout life. Denies difficulty with feeding. Mother denies that the daughter is excessively restless or agitated. Denies fever.

Physical examination: loose, wrinkled, and hanging skin with poor elasticity. Global hypotonia. Joint hypermobility. Scoliosis observed during spinal examination.

Complementary tests: pelvic radiograph showing hip dislocation.

findings.text: difficulties with independence in daily activities

translation:
Identification: female patient, brought by mother for first visit to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics.

Main complaint: "delay in learning things".

Current illness history: mother reports that the child took longer than other children to sit, crawl, and walk. She also reports significant difficulties with learning and with independence in daily activities, with prior assessment indicating intellectual disability. Developmental evaluation reveals moderate global developmental delay, without severe global developmental delay.

History: no atrial septal defect. No aortic root aneurysm.

Physical examination: head circumference without mild microcephaly. No unilateral cleft lip present.

findings.text: late acquisition of first words and phrases
increased interdigital distance between hallux and second pododactyl bilaterally
reduction in white matter volume on brain MRI

translation:
Identification: boy, 13 years old, brought by mother, referred to the genetic medicine outpatient clinic for investigation of developmental delay.

Current illness history: mother reports that he took a long time to sit independently and also began walking later than his siblings. The first words and phrases came late. Global assessment reveals moderate developmental neuropsychomotor delay. Diagnosed with ADHD by the school team and mental health services. Still requires assistance with bathing, dressing, and feeding. Mother denies that he has been below expected growth and weight gain. Reports that he walks with firmness, without imbalance.

Physical examination: narrow forehead, prominent nasal root, short philtrum, retrognathic mandible and broad chin. Long fingers on hands. Increased interdigital distance between hallux and second pododactyl bilaterally. Eyes aligned, no strabismus. No dystonic postures. Normal tendon reflexes, without hyperreflexia.

Complementary tests: EEG with interictal abnormalities. Brain MRI showing reduction in white matter volume.

Identification: female patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: ocular abnormalities and difficulty hearing.

Current illness history: the family reports that the patient has poor hearing, requiring others to speak louder and repeat their sentences. They have also noticed since early childhood that the girl's eyes have an unusual shape, resembling a lockhole.

History: previous ultrasound of kidneys and urinary tracts shows both kidneys present, without unilateral renal agenesis.

Physical examination: on ophthalmological examination, iris coloboma. Fundoscopy reveals coriocentral coloboma and optic disc coloboma. On biomicroscopy, posterior subcapsular cataract.

findings.text: decreased muscle strength in distal portions of all four limbs
distal muscle atrophy in the limbs
global absence of deep tendon reflexes
reduced amplitude of compound muscle action potentials

translation:
Identification: male, 50 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: difficulty walking.

Current illness history: patient reports having progressive difficulty walking. He also mentions generalized fatigue and weakness throughout the body, with a sensation of overall lack of strength. No history of generalized convulsive seizures.

History: according to family, there was no delay in neuropsychomotor development during childhood. No intellectual disability.

hand tremor when holding a cup
hand tremor when arms are extended
markedly arched sole of foot when standing

electromyography showing reduced amplitude of compound muscle action potentials

absent: normal tactile sensation in lower limbs
normal palmar sensation in lower limbs
normal muscle strength in distal upper limb muscles
normal muscle strength in distal lower limb muscles
absent postural tremor in upper limbs
translation:
Identification: male, 35 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: weakness in hands and feet.

Current illness history: patient reports progressive difficulty in buttoning clothes and holding small objects, as well as frequent tripping due to inability to lift the tips of his feet. He reports that his hands tremble when holding a cup or when arms are extended. He notices that both his hands and legs have become thinner. He observes that the sole of his foot is markedly arched, even when standing.

Muscle strength grade 4 in distal upper limb muscles and distal lower limb paresis. Postural tremor in upper limbs. Achilles reflexes abolished (not merely hypoactive). Biceps and triceps reflexes without hyperreflexia. No Babinski sign. Hypoesthesia tactile and reduced pallial sensation in lower limbs.

Complementary tests: electromyography showing reduced amplitude of sensory action potentials and reduced amplitude of compound muscle action potentials.

findings.text: inability to maintain attention during school tasks
need for support in daily activities

absent: brain MRI abnormalities other than thinning of the corpus callosum
translation:
Identification: female, 26 years old, accompanied by mother.

She also began speaking her first words and forming sentences much later than expected. In childhood, she was extremely restless, impulsive, and unable to maintain attention during school tasks, having received a diagnosis of ADHD. She has intellectual disability with need for support in daily activities. Mother denies repetitive behaviors, social isolation, or restricted interests. She also denies anxiety, excessive worry, or fear episodes.

findings.text: short stature for age and sex

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 17 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

She reports episodes in which the child becomes rigid throughout the body and then begins to move in a rhythmic, alternating manner on both sides of the body. Identification: Male, 27 years old, referred to the neurogenetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current illness history: Patient reports walking with a staggering gait, with legs widely apart, and has a tendency to fall. His mother, who accompanies him, states that he has always been clumsy, frequently dropping objects and bumping into furniture. He also reports that his speech is slow and difficult to understand. The family has noticed that his head moves back and forth.

closing of eyes in bright light

erythema on face and dorsal hands
scars on face and antibrachial regions
translation:

findings.text: loose body when picked up in arms
cortical thickening of diaphyses of long bones

Identification: male, 17 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: short stature.

Current illness history: the mother reports that the child has always been shorter than peers of the same age, with a small body in a harmonious proportion. findings.text: early walking followed by loss of ability to walk
seizures starting with tremors on one side of the body
seizures starting with loss of consciousness and tremors in all four limbs

findings.text: volumetric reduction of cerebral white matter

findings.text: generalized tonic-clonic seizures with bilateral involvement

translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years and 6 months, brought by mother, referred to the genetic medicine outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Current disease history: Mother reports that, since early years, the child has been delayed in reaching developmental milestones across all domains. She also states that the child sat and walked later than other children. To date, the girl has never spoken any word. She has had generalized tonic-clonic seizures since onset, with bilateral involvement. The mother denies that the child is overly restless or hyperactive. The child interacts well with family members and other children, without social behavior abnormalities.

Physical examination: Moderate intellectual disability; does not fall into the category of mild intellectual disability.

Complementary tests: Abnormal EEG. Brain MRI shows no abnormal myelination and no pituitary cyst.

translation:
Identification: Male newborn, 5 days of life, evaluated in the neonatal ICU at the request of the team for genetic assessment.

Current illness history: The mother reports that shortly after birth the baby "became stiff", with arms and legs difficult to bend. The infant progressed with seizures and respiratory insufficiency requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Currently receiving nasogastric tube for feeding due to inability to suck. The team reports prolonged neonatal jaundice. Parents report that the skin has never turned blue.

Physical examination: Newborn on mechanical ventilation, with nasogastric tube. Global hypertonia. Global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. Hands with an extra digit on the fifth digit, bilaterally. Feet with post-axial polydactily. No cyanosis.

Complementary tests: Hyperbilirubinemia. EEG showing interictal epileptiform activity.

absent: deep tendon reflexes diminished in upper limbs
translation:
Identification: Female patient, 76 years old, brought by her daughter, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: "Stopped walking."

Current illness history: The daughter reports that her mother began walking unsteadily, with staggering, and over time, lost the ability to walk, being currently confined to a wheelchair. She also notes that her speech has become slurred and slow. The patient reports increased irritability, becoming easily angered by minor things, and occasionally claims to see people and animals inside the house that no one else sees. The family has noticed that her head moves back and forth involuntarily. No tremor is reported in hands, arms, or legs.

Physical examination: Conscious. Dysarthria. Cerebellar tremor. Horizontal nystagmus. Sacadic eye pursuit. When placed standing with support, maintains a wide base of support; no spastic gait pattern. Deep tendon reflexes in upper limbs are not diminished. In lower limbs, reflexes are normal, without hyperreflexia or hyporeflexia.

Complementary tests: Brain MRI brought by the family shows cerebellar atrophy.

findings.text: head turning instead of eye movement when looking to the side
brief involuntary jerks in arms and body

translation:
Identification: girl, 4 years old, brought by mother, referred from pediatrics to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: "she is losing what she already knew how to do."

Current illness history: Mother reports that the child had been developing normally until she began to lose previously acquired skills. She also notes that, when looking to the side, the child turns her entire head instead of moving her eyes. She additionally observes brief, involuntary jerks in the arms and body, sometimes occurring at rest, sometimes when trying to grasp objects. She has experienced generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

Physical examination: Unstable gait, with widened base and dysmetria during object grasp. Oculomotor apraxia. Palpable spleen, enlarged in size.

Complementary tests: Complete blood count showing leucopenia and anemia; platelet count within normal limits. Bone marrow examination brought by family describes Gaucher cells.

Identification: Male, 31 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: Referred due to laboratory test abnormalities.

Current disease history: Patient brought for investigation after routine laboratory tests showed serum creatine kinase (CK) levels above the upper limit of normal in repeated measurements.

Complementary tests: Maximal pressure (PImáx) and maximal ejection pressure (PEmáx) reduced in manometry. Echocardiogram showed no evidence of cardiomyopathy. Posteroanterior (PA) thoracic radiograph with normal cardiac index, no increase in cardiac area.

translation:
Identification: male infant, 3 months old, brought by parents for genetic medicine evaluation.

Main complaint: "white spots on the skin and white hair".

Current illness history: the mother reports that since birth, the infant has areas of skin lacking pigmentation on the face, trunk, and limbs, which have not changed. She also notes that both the eyebrows and eyelashes are completely white, and that there are already several gray hairs, which she finds surprising given the infant's age. She further reports that the infant consistently keeps both hands bent downward and is unable to straighten them.

Physical examination: prominent nasal bridge. Telecanthus. Short palpebral fissures. Leukodermia in patches, distributed over the face, trunk, and limbs. Membranous skin folds in both axillae. Upper limbs with reduced muscle mass, thin. Flexion contractures in both hands. Fingers of the hands fixed in flexion, with no complete passive extension.

translation:
Identification: Female, 26 years old, referred to medical genetics for investigation.

Main complaint: "Yellowing of eyes and skin."

Current illness history: Patient reports that, since she can remember, she has experienced episodes in which her skin and eyes turn yellow, without any other associated symptoms reported. She has previously undergone relevant examinations.

Physical examination: Yellowing of skin and sclerae. Flaccid abdomen, palpable spleen below the left costal margin.

Complementary tests: Hemolytic anemia. Elevated reticulocyte count. Peripheral blood smear showing presence of spherocytes. Increased osmotic fragility test of red blood cells.

findings.text: acanthosis nigricans in posterior cervical region

translation:
Identification: female patient referred to the endocrinology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Main complaint: amenorrhea and hirsutism.

Current illness history: patient reports having missed menstruation for more than six months. She also describes the development of coarse hair in the pubic area, jawline, periareolar region, and abdominal line, which she finds very bothersome. She additionally notes dark, velvety patches on the neck and axillae.

Physical examination: hirsutism observed on face, thorax, and abdomen. Hyperpigmented, thickened, and velvety plaques in the posterior cervical region and axillae, suggestive of acanthosis nigricans.

Complementary tests: pelvic ultrasonography showing bilateral polycystic ovaries. Elevated fasting insulin levels. Oral glucose tolerance test revealing glucose intolerance. Laboratory assessment indicative of insulin resistance. Hormonal testing with elevated serum androgens. Skin biopsy of the cervical lesion showing epidermal acanthosis.

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Main complaint: skin and hair changes since birth.

Current disease history: mother reports that the child was born with red, scaly skin over the entire body, a condition that persists to the present day. She also states that, after sun exposure, the skin becomes red and easily irritated. She notes that the hair has always been rough to the touch. She also observes that there are two missing front teeth, located beside the upper central incisors. Good school performance, without intellectual disability.

Physical examination: congenital non-bullous erythrodermia with ictiosiform pattern. Agenesia of upper lateral incisors. Height appropriate for age, without short stature. Fundoscopy: pigment epithelial mosaic of the retinal epithelium.

Complementary tests: serum IgE elevated. Polarized light microscopy of hair shaft showing "tiger tail" pattern.

Main complaint: "Her hair is falling out and becoming fragmented."

Complementary tests: Hair microscopy revealed moniliosis.
