translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: referred by nephrology for renal function alteration.

History of present illness: patient followed in nephrology for renal insufficiency. Reports that routine examinations revealed anemia. Brings reports of previous biopsies performed.

Complementary examinations: renal biopsy with amyloid deposition in the renal parenchyma. Hepatic biopsy also showing amyloid deposition in the liver.

Treatment: outpatient follow-up.

Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "doesn't hear well" and very pale skin.

History of Present Illness: Family reports that the patient has always had difficulty hearing. Audiometry brought shows sensorineural hearing loss. The family noted from an early age that the eyebrows are white and that the eyelashes are also white. They also report that the skin and hair are much lighter than those of everyone in the family, diffusely throughout the body. They deny involuntary eye movements.

Physical Exam: Generalized hypopigmentation. Iris of intense blue color, same color in both eyes, without heterochromia. Absence of nystagmus.

Fundoscopy: Hypopigmented fundus.

findings.text: concentric constriction of the peripheral fields

translation:
Identification: Woman, 34 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of visual complaints.

Chief complaint: "I can't see almost anything."

History of present illness: Reports that for many years she has had significant difficulty seeing at night and in dimly lit environments. She also reports losing peripheral vision, bumping into objects and people that approached laterally. Currently, she can only distinguish light from dark.

Physical examination: On ophthalmic examination, fundoscopy reveals pallor of the optic disc and pigmentary retinopathy, in addition to coro-capillary atrophy.

Complementary examinations: Perimetry with concentric constriction of the peripheral fields. Electroretinogram extinguished.

translation:
Identification: male, 45 years old, referred to neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: long-standing muscle weakness.

History of Present Illness: Patient reports difficulty climbing stairs, rising from a chair, and elevating arms above the head. Refers to repeated episodes of pneumonia throughout life, with the need for medical attention. Also complains of cough.

History: According to the mother’s report, he was a “slovenly” baby, who slipped out of his hands when held by the axillae. Completed studies regularly and works; there is no intellectual deficit. Previous cardiology evaluation without alteration of ventricular function.

Physical exam: Reduced muscle strength in the scapular and pelvic regions.

findings.text: suprasternal elevation of the ST segment

translation:
Identification: male, 45 years old.

Chief complaint: referred to the cardiology genetics outpatient clinic for electrocardiographic abnormalities.

History of present illness: patient reports that, in a previous Holter recording, a ventricular tachycardia episode was documented. Denies syncope. Denies sensation of a racing heart or palpitations. Denies prior cardiac arrest episode.

History: no report of sudden death.

Physical examination: patient in good general condition, conscious and oriented.

Complementary examinations: resting ECG shows suprasternal elevation of the ST segment and incomplete right bundle branch block. QT interval without prolongation.

findings.text: reduced creatine peak in the brain

translation:
Identification: female patient, brought by her mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the daughter took much longer than other children to start walking independently. She also reports that she never spoke any words. She refers to a brief generalized seizure crisis, lasting only a few minutes, during a febrile episode, without recurrence on the same day and without associated central nervous system infection.

Physical exam: patient with evident intellectual disability noted on examination.

Complementary examinations: proton spectroscopy MRI of the skull with reduced creatine peak in the brain. Diminished urinary guanidinoacetic acid. Diminished plasma guanidinoacetic acid. Serum creatinine within the normal range.

translation:
Identification: woman, 48 years old, accompanied by her sister, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "episodes."

History of present illness: The sister reports that the patient has had epileptic seizures since her young adult life, of intermittent occurrence. She also reports that she has always had difficulty learning in school, but is able to perform daily activities alone; a previous neuropsychological evaluation concluded with mild intellectual deficit, without impairment to moderate or severe degree. The family perceives that her speech is "tangled," sometimes difficult to understand.

Physical examination: conscious, cooperative. Speech is dysarthric. Gait and coordination tests without ataxia. Absence of dystonia; without abnormal postures of trunk or limbs.

Complementary examinations: Cerebrospinal fluid brought by the family shows low glucose levels.

findings.text: atrophy of the thenar muscles bilaterally
TGO (AST) above the upper limit of normal

translation:
Identification: woman, 25 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "heart racing".

History of present illness: Patient reports episodes in which she feels her heart beat hard and fast, without a clear triggering factor. The family denies any loss of cognitive abilities she may have had, such as memory or reasoning.

Physical examination: Reduced strength in cervical flexion. Atrophy of the thenar muscles bilaterally.

Complementary examinations: CK elevated. DHL increased. TGO (AST) above the upper limit of normal.

findings.text: rapid, involuntary movements in the limbs

translation:
Identification: 56-year-old patient, brought in by a family member for evaluation in neurology outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “memory loss” progressive.

History of present illness: Family reports that the patient has begun to forget names, dates, and recent appointments, with gradual worsening. He/She also reports difficulty remembering the names of people and objects, being able to describe them but unable to find the word. There are episodes in which he/she becomes disoriented, with disorganized thinking and unable to understand what is happening around him/her. Currently needs help with bathing, dressing, and taking care of the house. The family describes further episodes of generalized seizure crises since the beginning, with loss of consciousness, and rapid, involuntary movements in the limbs.

Past medical history: Previous diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease, referred for follow-up.

Physical exam: Patient with established dementia. Myoclonias were observed during the exam.

Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of visual complaints.

Chief complaint: "discomfort with brightness."

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that bright light is uncomfortable and can hurt her eyes, requiring her to use sunglasses or avoid brightly lit environments. She also reports difficulty seeing moving objects, such as a ball being thrown or cars passing on the street. She states that she takes time to adapt when going from a dark place to a bright one, or vice versa, spending some time without seeing well until her vision adjusts.

Physical Exam: Reduced visual acuity bilaterally. Eye movements without nystagmus.

Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: nasal bleeding.

History of present illness: family reports recurrent episodes of nasal bleeding. Also reports episodes of seizures. Denies prior stroke.

History: Previous upper endoscopy and colonoscopy with multiple juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine, according to the pathology report. No anemia in previous laboratory assessments.

Physical examination: finger tips are enlarged and rounded, with curved watch glass nails. No telangiectasias in skin, lips, tongue, or mucous membranes.

Complementary examinations: abdominal imaging revealed hepatic arteriovenous malformation.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
decreased resistance to passive movement of the limbs
tremors in the arms and legs lasting a few minutes and resolving spontaneously
focalized isoelectric transferrin with type I pattern

translation:
Identification: female patient, brought by her mother for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “developmental delay”.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter delayed head support, sitting, and babbling, and has not yet interacted or played like other children of the same age. She also reports episodes in which the child has a fixed stare and presents with tremors in the arms and legs, lasting a few minutes and resolving spontaneously.

Gestational History: Mother denies decreased fetal movements during pregnancy. No immune hydrops.

Physical Exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Child is “floppy” to handling, with decreased resistance to passive movement of the limbs. Abdomen: palpable enlarged liver.

Complementary Examinations: Focalized isoelectric transferrin with type I pattern.

Identification: Woman, 40 years old, presents to the medical genetics consultation for evaluation, referred by orthopedics.

Chief complaint: Back pain.

History of present illness: Patient reports chronic back pain that bothers her in daily activities. She states that she has always been the shortest in her family and that she noticed that her trunk was short in relation to her arms and legs.

Physical exam: Short stature disproportionate, with a short trunk and limbs of normal length.

Complementary examinations: Radiographs of the spine brought by the patient show hemivertebrae and fusion of adjacent vertebral bodies.

Identification: female patient, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for evaluation of physical characteristics.

History of present illness: The mother noticed that one of the daughter’s eyes “drifts outward” sometimes, primarily when she is tired. She also reports that the eyebrows have always been thin, with few hairs. Denies that the daughter has difficulty hearing; there is no complaint of conductive hearing loss.

Physical examination: Rounded face. High forehead, without low insertion of hair in the frontal region. Sparse supercilium. Bilateral iris without coloboma. Nostrils without nasal divergence. Smooth filter, without deep filter. Fine upper lip vermillion. Hands with wide thumbs, poorly developed thenar eminence and reduced hypothenar eminence. Feet with depressed longitudinal plantar arch and long hallux.

findings.text: feeling his heart beating fast and accelerated in the chest
episodes of feeling like he is going to faint
mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction

translation:
Identification: male, 35 years old, referred to the cardiology genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "heart racing".

History of Present Illness: Patient reports episodes in which he feels his heart beating fast and accelerated in the chest. He also reports episodes of feeling like he is going to faint, with vision darkening and weakness, without actually losing consciousness. There is no record of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in previous monitoring.

Past medical history: Denies a previous episode of sudden cardiac arrest with the need for resuscitation.

Additional examinations: Resting ECG with short QT interval. Patient-brought echocardiogram with mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction.

findings.text: liver and spleen were enlarged upon palpation of the abdomen
increased proportion of gamma-delta T lymphocytes

translation:
Identification: patient of 1 year and 1 month, brought by the mother, referred to the pediatric immunology outpatient clinic for investigation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child had several episodes of bronchiolitis, more frequent and more severe than in siblings and other children in daycare. She also refers to hospitalization for severe cytomegalovirus infection. She has already received a diagnosis of autoimmune hemolytic anemia during hospital follow-up.

Physical Exam: Liver and spleen were enlarged upon palpation of the abdomen.

Complementary Examinations: FAN reagent positive. Hemogram without eosinophilia and without lymphopenia. There is no autoimmune neutropenia. Immunophenotyping with an increased proportion of gamma-delta T lymphocytes. Lymphocyte transformation test with a diminished response to phytohemagglutinin.

findings.text: hypoesthesia in hands and feet of a distal predominance
open wounds on the tips of his feet
open wounds on the tips of his hands
loss of parts of some fingers
spontaneous amputation of distal phalanges of some fingers
reduction in the number of myelinated fibers

translation:
Identification: male, 39 years old, referred to neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: reports that he has not felt pain when he is injured for many years, only noticing injuries when he sees them. Reports open wounds on the tips of his feet and hands, with difficult healing. States that he has lost parts of some fingers, which detached themselves over time. His wife observes that he has an uncontrollable habit of picking and chewing his own nails, until they are injured. Denies absence of sweating and denies excessive sweating.

Physical Exam: Hypoesthesia in hands and feet, of a distal predominance. Deep tendon reflexes globally hypoactive. Ulcers on the digital extremities. Spontaneous amputation of distal phalanges of some fingers.

Complementary Exams: ENMG with reduction of the amplitude of sensitive action potentials. Sural nerve biopsy showing reduction in the number of myelinated fibers and demyelination, without onion bulb formation in the basal lamina.

Identification: girl, 8 years old, accompanied by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by the pediatrician for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "difficulty learning."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter has always had difficulty learning and performing daily activities compared to other children of the same age. Psychological testing with standardized tests revealed intellectual disability. She refers that, at birth, she was informed that the child's head was small; the maternity records confirm a head circumference below -2 SD at birth.

Physical Exam: Microcephaly since birth, as confirmed by the records. On inspection of the profile, the forehead is markedly sloping backward.

Management: Follow-up appointment.

Identification: male, 22 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: follow-up of endocrine disorder and recurrent infections.

History of present illness: patient reports that since childhood he has experienced recurrent episodes of fungal infections that return even after resolution. He has been following with endocrinology for hypoparathyroidism. He also reports red, irritated eyes with a sandy sensation, accompanied by ophthalmology, which described keratoconjunctivitis. According to the ophthalmological evaluation, there is no cataract. In endocrinological follow-up, primary adrenal insufficiency was ruled out.

Physical exam: patient in good general condition, cooperative.

findings.text: thick, greasy layer, similar to a white varnish

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of skin and hair changes.

Chief complaint: scaly skin and fragile hair.

History of present illness: The family reports that at birth, the skin was covered with a thick, greasy layer, similar to a white varnish, which subsequently peeled off. Since then, the skin has remained dry and scaly. They report frequent itching over the body. The caregivers note that the hair is thin, lacks shine, and breaks easily when combed. They also report that the patient is uncomfortable with bright light, closing his/her eyes in bright environments. They deny decreased sweating.

Physical examination: Generalized ichthyosis. Curly hair. Conical teeth. Nails without changes. On ocular examination, corneal opacity; eyelids without signs of inflammation; absence of pinguety.

Complementary examinations: Trichoscopy with hair shaft microscopy revealing pili torti.

findings.text: absence of radius and ulna short

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of upper limb malformations and cardiomyopathy.

Chief complaint: "different arms and heart problem".

History of present illness: The family noticed since birth that the arms were shorter in the upper part. They bring a previous echocardiogram performed.

Physical examination: upper limbs present, with hands implanted in the forearm, without appearance of hands directly attached to the trunk; there is no absence of upper limb. Bilaterally shortened brachial segment.

Complementary examinations: Radiography of upper limbs shows absence of radius and ulna short; it is not just a short radius. Echocardiogram shows CIV and CIA, without patent foramen ovale and without total atrioventricular septal defect.

Identification: male, 43 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: difficulty with walking.

History of present illness: Patient accompanied by his wife, who reports that he has begun to walk in an awkward and insecure manner. The wife notes that he frequently forgets names and appointments and that he can no longer organize and plan daily tasks, leaving them unfinished. Denies involuntary urinary loss.

Physical examination: Slurred speech, with poor articulation of words. Supranuclear gaze palsy, with preserved reflexive eye movements. Nystagmus present. Muscle strength preserved in all four limbs. Spasticity in the lower extremities, with exaggerated patellar and Achilles reflexes; reflexes in the upper extremities normal, without exaggeration. Babinski sign present. Index-nose and heel-knee tests with dysmetria and decomposition of movements. Altered gait.

Complementary examinations: Head MRI showing cerebellar atrophy. Somatosensory evoked potentials without abnormalities.

findings.text: shortening of the middle segments of the limbs (forearms and legs)
testicular tissue in the bilateral scrotum

translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child has always been the smallest in the class, significantly shorter than other children. She also reports that his head always seemed large and that his forehead is very prominent. She has also noted that the fingers of his hands and feet are short. She states that his gum is thick and grows over the teeth.

Past Medical History: Interventricular communication previously diagnosed by cardiology.

Physical Exam: Short stature. Macrocephaly. Hypertelorism. Downward slanting palpebral fissures. Short nose with anteverted nostrils. Oral cavity with crowding of teeth; no absence of teeth in the arch. Shortening of the middle segments of the limbs (forearms and legs). Male genitalia with micropenis; testicular tissue in the bilateral scrotum.

findings.text: hands with fifth finger short and curved towards the fourth finger, bilaterally
magnetic resonance imaging of lumbar sacral spine showing anchored spinal cord

translation:
Identification: girl, 1 year and 7 months, brought by her mother, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Chief complaint: recurrent urinary tract infections.

History of present illness: mother reports that the child has had several episodes of urinary tract infection. She also reports that the daughter has difficulty evacuating and with little frequency, remaining for several days without evacuating. Accompanied by pediatric urology with diagnosis of neurogenic bladder.

History: mother reports that the girl was born with feet turned inward and downward.

Physical examination: hands with fifth finger short and curved towards the fourth finger, bilaterally; short thumbs. Flat feet; short halluxes.

Complementary examinations: uretrocystography with vesicoureteral reflux. Magnetic resonance imaging of lumbar sacral spine showing anchored spinal cord and lipoma of the filum terminale. Gynecological evaluation with longitudinal vaginal septum and double cervix.

findings.text: reduced visual acuity in both eyes
retinal pigmentation in osteosclerosis spiculation in the mid periphery

translation:
Identification: Woman, 35 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for ophthalmological evaluation.

Chief complaint: "I can't see at night."

History of present illness: Patient reports having significant difficulty seeing in dark environments or with low light, needing assistance to walk at night. She also reports that her visual field has been narrowing increasingly over the years, causing her to bump into objects on her side. She also notes that her vision is worse for reading and recognizing faces.

Physical examination: Reduced visual acuity in both eyes. Fundoscopy: Retinal pigmentation in osteosclerosis spiculation in the mid periphery and diffuse arteriolar and venular tapering.

Complementary examinations: Electroretinogram with present responses, not extinguished.

findings.text: knees crossing one in front of the other
bowed feet turned inward and downward

absent: rigidity with passive movement of the limbs
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought for evaluation in the neurology outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: difficulty with walking.

History of present illness: The family reports that he walks with his legs stiff, with his knees knocking and sometimes crossing one in front of the other with each step. They also report that he was born with bowed feet, turned inward and downward. Family denies that his speech has become monotonous, without intonation.

Physical exam: facies with preserved expression and mimicry, without hypomimia. Absence of rigidity with passive movement of the limbs. Movements performed with adequate speed, without bradykinesia. Does not present a parkinsonian picture. Deep reflexes are exaggerated globally. Babinski sign present. Congenital bowed foot observed.

findings.text: weakness of predominance proximal in the four limbs

translation:
Identification: Woman, 57 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of weakness.

Chief complaint: "Difficulty climbing stairs."

History of present illness: Patient reports having had a lot of difficulty climbing stairs, needing to support herself with the handrail. She also reports that she cannot stand for long without getting tired and needing to support herself. Her daughter, who accompanies her, noticed that she is swaying her hips from side to side.

Physical exam: Weakness of predominance proximal in the four limbs. Weakness of the cervical flexors. No facial muscle weakness. Deep reflexes hypoactive globally.

Complementary exams: Elevated serum CK. Muscle biopsy: fibers with increased caliber variation, marginated vacuoles, increased internalized nuclei and angular fibers.

findings.text: ear pain several times a year
blisters on the lips that reappear several times
red lesions in the creases of elbows and knees

translation:
Identification: girl, 6 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: recurrent infections.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter has had infections since early childhood: many ear infections, ear pain several times a year, as well as frequent colds, sore throats, and sinusitis. She also reports recurrent viral infections. She has had several episodes of pneumonia throughout her life. The child has oral ulcers that recur repeatedly, and blisters on the lips that reappear several times. She had an episode of red, hot, and swollen skin, treated as cellulitis. Denies mastoiditis. Denies keratitis. No asthma episodes and no recurrent bronchitis.

Past medical history: Allergy to cow's milk protein and allergy to egg. Denies medication allergy. Since infancy, she has had dry skin with intense itching and red lesions in the creases of elbows and knees. The mother notices that she has always been smaller than other children and grows slowly.

Physical exam: Growth delay. Prominent forehead.

findings.text: thick redness of the superior lip
head circumference within the expected range for age and sex

translation:
Identification: male patient, 34 years old, brought by his sister for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for etiological investigation.

History of present illness: the sister reports that he has always been frequently ill with recurrent infections throughout the year. Followed in ophthalmology with a report of rod and cone dystrophy. Presents with severe intellectual disability, dependent on others for daily activities.

History: according to the family, the pregnancy occurred without an increase in amniotic fluid.

Physical exam: head circumference within the expected range for age and sex, without microcephaly and without macrocephaly. Ears with low insertion. Superior lip with thick redness. Hands without extra fingers on the ulnar side; feet without extra fingers on the lateral side.

Complementary exams: Brain MRI with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and molar tooth sign.

findings.text: joints without excessive range of motion
whitish retrolental mass of the type pseudoglioma

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “recurring fractures and vision problem”.

History of present illness: Patient reports that since childhood he has broken bones easily, having presented with several fractures throughout his life. He refers to always having had poor vision. The mother reports that when he was small, she noticed a white glare in the pupil in photographs. Denies difficulty with school or learning, with adequate cognitive development.

Physical examination: Short stature. Spine with lateral deviation associated with increased dorsal curvature. Muscle tone preserved. Joints without excessive range of motion. Small eyes. Leucocoria. Diminished visual acuity.

Complementary examinations: Ophthalmological evaluation with retinal detachment, whitish retrolental mass of the type pseudoglioma and persistent hyaloid vascular remnants; transparent crystalline lens, without opacities. Radiographs of the spine with flattened vertebrae and compression vertebral fractures. Long bones of normal diameter, without scalloping. Bone mineral density with reduced bone mineral density.

findings.text: prominent eyes, projected forward of the facial plane
flat feet bilaterally, with longitudinal arch supported on the ground in orthostasis

translation:
Identification: boy, 12 years old, brought by his mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: "breaks bones easily".

History of Present Illness: mother reports that the child has had several fractures throughout childhood, repeatedly, after minor traumas. She refers that he took longer than his siblings to sit, crawl, and walk. Denies fractures identified at birth or in pregnancy ultrasounds.

Physical exam: prominent eyes, projected forward of the facial plane. Occipital region flattened. Thorax narrow in lateral-lateral diameter. Feet flat bilaterally, with longitudinal arch supported on the ground in orthostasis.

Complementary exams: bone densitometry with T-score between -1 and -2.5, without reaching osteoporosis range. Radiographs show widened diaphyses of long bones, with deficient tubular modeling. Spine without compression fractures.

findings.text: Muscle weakness of predominance proximal in the scapular and pelvic regions
Hypermobility of the fingers of the hands
increase in the number of fibers with centralized nuclei

translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years and 4 months, brought by her mother, referred to the neuromuscular clinic.

Chief complaint: weakness for climbing stairs and lifting herself up from the floor.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the daughter has always been “sluggish” since infancy and that she only walked well after the other children in the family. Currently, she has difficulty lifting herself up from the floor, climbing stairs, and raising her arms above her head. She has also noticed that the girl’s arms and legs are thin, “without muscle.”

Physical examination: global hypotonia. Muscle weakness of predominance proximal in the scapular and pelvic regions. Diffuse amyotrophy. Contractures in elbows, knees, and ankles. Hypermobility of the fingers of the hands. Fingers of normal length. Palate of usual height. Neck of normal length. No retrocalcaneal valgus.

Complementary examinations: CK serum within the normal range. Muscle biopsy: variation increased in fiber diameter, increase in the number of fibers with centralized nuclei, foci of fiber necrosis and increased endomysial connective tissue.

findings.text: hard protrusions on each side of his nose
bony overgrowth of the nasal bones bilaterally

translation:
Identification: male patient, 43 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "nose always congested."

History of present illness: Patient reports that he has had difficulty breathing through his nose since childhood. He presented with a previous otorhinolaryngological evaluation with nasal endoscopy revealing narrowing of the nares bilaterally. He also reports that he has noticed, over the years, hard protrusions on each side of his nose.

Physical examination: eyes well separated from each other on inspection, with increased interpupillary distance. Palpation revealed bony overgrowth of the nasal bones bilaterally, of stony consistency.

Complementary examinations: CT scan of the head brought by the patient shows hyperostosis of the calota craniana.

findings.text: penis of very small dimensions for age
absence of spermatozoa even after centrifugation
IGF-1 serum below the lower limit of normal

absent: tingling, numbness or weakness in hands and feet
translation:
Identification: male, 36 years old, accompanied by his sister.

Chief complaint: referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

History of present illness: Patient and sister report that he has been progressively losing hair for years, with areas of thinning in the scalp. The sister noticed that he began to close his eyes forcefully several times a day, without being able to control it, as if the eyelids were "locked." Married for years, the couple is trying to conceive unsuccessfully. Denies hearing loss. Denies sudden muscle spasms. Denies tingling, numbness or weakness in hands and feet.

Past medical history: Intellectual disability since childhood, with the need for support in daily activities. Undergoing treatment for hypothyroidism. Previous diagnosis of hypogonadism. Does not have diabetes.

Physical examination: Diffuse alopecia of the scalp. Blepharospasm observed during the consultation. Penis of very small dimensions for age.

Complementary tests: spermogram with absence of spermatozoa even after centrifugation. IGF-1 serum below the lower limit of normal.

findings.text: absence of ossification of the calota craniana
upper limbs short due to osseous underdevelopment
lower limbs short due to osseous underdevelopment

translation:
Identification: patient referred for evaluation in medical genetics; sex and age not provided.

History: during gestation, the mother reports that the baby moved less than expected.

Physical exam: cleft palate. Eyes of reduced size (microphthalmia). Nose of altered shape. Thin skin. Absence of ossification of the calota craniana. Muscle tone underdeveloped. Upper limbs short due to osseous underdevelopment, as well as the lower limbs. Omphalocele.

Complementary exams: cranial image shows cystic lesion intracranially. Both lungs with three lobes. Skin biopsy without visible granular layer in the epidermis. No horseshoe kidney. No diaphragmatic hernia congenital. Echocardiogram without tetralogy of Fallot.

findings.text: increased projection of the nasal tip

translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: evaluation of articular osteoarthritic changes.

History of present illness: patient reports long-standing joint pain; prior imaging studies brought to the consultation show osteoarthritis and degenerative disc disease. He also presents with osteochondritis dissecans on articular imaging. He reports being diagnosed with premature cranial suture closure in childhood.

Past medical history: denies hiatal hernia.

Physical exam: chest with depressed costal cartilage. Nose without increased projection of the nasal tip. Spine without lateral deviation.

Complementary exams: abdominal angiography without aneurysm. Cranial angio-MRI without dilation of cerebral arteries.

findings.text: aneurysmal dilation of the aortic root

translation:
Identification: girl, 7 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatric cardiology for genetic evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that since infancy, the daughter was “floppy,” with a loose body when carried. She also noticed that the girl’s eyes “do not look in the same direction.” She refers that the child has never had difficulty seeing far away. She is followed by a cardiologist for interatrial communication and persistent arterial duct.

Physical Exam: Eyes well separated from each other, without strabismus. Nasal bridge without flattening. Nasal filter of normal length. High palate; bifid uvula. Chest with depression of the sternum. Long and thin fingers. Feet with medial foot deviation; absence of congenital knock-knees. Global hypotonia on examination.

Complementary Examinations: Echocardiogram with aortic insufficiency and aneurysmal dilation of the aortic root. Angiography showing tortuosity of the carotid arteries.

findings.text: proximal muscle weakness in the upper and lower limbs
episode of a seizure with shaking of the four limbs, initially generalized

translation:
Identification: female patient, 11 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: fatigue and pain in the legs and arms.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter frequently complains of weakness throughout the body and lack of strength for daily activities. She refers frequent pain in the limbs, without defined location, and that after playing or doing physical education, the girl feels a lot of pain in the muscles. She states that the child has fainted several times, losing consciousness for a short time and returning to normal on her own. There was also an episode of a seizure with shaking of the four limbs, initially generalized. There is a report of a previous episode of sudden death reversed. Low blood glucose levels have been documented.

Physical examination: Proximal muscle weakness in the upper and lower limbs. Ankle dorsiflexion limited bilaterally.

Complementary examinations: Ischemic exercise test of the forearm without lactate elevation. Muscle biopsy with atrophy of type 2 fibers, reduced muscle glycogen content, and fatty replacement of the skeletal muscle.

findings.text: diminished vibratory sensation in the distal portions of the limbs

translation:
Identification: female patient, 18 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "weakness in the legs and arms".

History of present illness: The patient reports experiencing muscle weakness, with progressive difficulty performing daily activities. The mother, who accompanies her, noticed that the daughter's hands and legs became thinner in the extremities.

Physical examination: Increased tone, with spasticity in the limbs. Patellar and Achilles reflexes are exaggerated bilaterally. Babinski sign is present. Vibratory sensation is diminished in the distal portions of the limbs. Hypoalgesia to needle test. Eye movements of pursuit are slow without saccadic intrusions. Finger-nose and heel-to-knee tests are without dysmetria.

findings.text: horizontal corneal diameter increased, 13 mm or more, with transparent cornea
grayish halo peripheral to the pupil, separated from it by a clear corneal band, in both eyes
polygonal opacities in a mosaic pattern in the central corneal stroma

translation:
Identification: male patient, 72 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by ophthalmology for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "seeing poorly".

History of present illness: patient reports noticing a worsening of vision, with difficulty reading and recognizing faces at a distance.

Physical examination (ophthalmological): reduced visual acuity. Horizontal corneal diameter increased, 13 mm or more, with transparent cornea. Grayish halo peripheral to the pupil, separated from it by a clear corneal band, in both eyes. At biomicroscopy, deep anterior chamber and Iranian transillumination defects. Polygonal opacities in a mosaic pattern in the central corneal stroma.

Complementary examinations: paquimetry with decreased corneal thickness.

findings.text: doesn’t grow”, “smaller than other children of the same age”,

translation:
Identification: female infant, 6 months, brought by the mother, referred to the pediatric immunology outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “wart that doesn’t heal”.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child presents with repeated oral candidiasis and candidiasis in the diaper area, which improve and then return. She also refers that the daughter “doesn’t grow,” becoming smaller and smaller than other children of the same age since birth.

Physical exam: Low weight for chronologic age postnatally. Abdomen: palpable enlarged liver, approximately a few centimeters from the right costal margin; palpable spleen below the left costal margin.

Complementary exams: Serum immunoglobulins with low IgG and low IgA for age; IgM without reduction. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping with reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes relative to CD3+. Lymphocyte transformation test with diminished response to phytohemagglutinin.

Identification: Woman, 56 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "I have been losing weight and having loose stools for a long time."

History of present illness: Patient reports that she has been losing weight progressively, noticing her clothes becoming increasingly loose. She also reports liquid stools, multiple times a day, that have persisted for several months without improvement.

Additional examinations: Brings result of peripheral nerve biopsy showing amyloid deposits in the nerve.

Management: Ambulatory follow-up.

Identification: male, 32 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that he has always been the tallest in his class. He reports that he can bend his joints much beyond the normal range since childhood. He states that he noticed skin markings, initially pink and then whitish, in the lumbar and thigh regions. He reports having been operated on for inguinal hernia.

Physical Exam: Tall stature. Downward-slanting palpebral fissures; without hypertelorism. High palate. Retrognathic mandible. Sternum deformity. Long, thin fingers. Skin without increased soft tissue palpability. Scoliosis on examination of the spine. Flat feet bilaterally, without congenital clubfoot.

Complementary Examinations: Echocardiogram with mitral valve prolapse and aortic root aneurysm. Lumbar-sacral spine MRI without dural ectasia and without Tarlov cysts.

Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: delay in development and seizures.

History of present illness: mother reports that the child delayed reaching developmental milestones in all areas, always behind other children of the same age. She refers that he sat and walked much later than expected. The boy almost never looks into the eyes, does not play with other children, spends long periods lining up objects, and repeats the same movements with his hands. There was a brief shaking episode throughout the body during fever, which lasted a few minutes and did not recur on the same day. Subsequently, he presented seizures without fever, with loss of consciousness and shaking of the four limbs since the beginning.

Physical exam: head circumference appropriate for age, without microcephaly. Cognitive assessment reveals intellectual disability.

Complementary exams: EEG with interictal epileptiform activity. Plasma amino acids with low valine, low leucine, and low isoleucine.

findings.text: shaking of the arms and legs

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: "episodes and a lot of weakness."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter had episodes in which she became stiff, with shaking of the arms and legs and without responding for a few minutes. She also reports that, in some periods, the child is very still, slow, without energy to play or do schoolwork, although she says she wants to do them. She also complains of abdominal pain on some days.

Additional Examinations: Brought from previous hospitalization: elevated plasma ammonia. Plasma amino acids with increased citrulline.

findings.text: above the reference value serum uric acid

translation:
Identification: male, 21 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: alteration in renal function in follow-up.

History of present illness: patient presents accompanied by his mother, bringing a nephrology report that informs chronic kidney disease in follow-up. He brings recent laboratory tests.

Additional examinations: serum uric acid above the reference value. Elevated serum creatinine. Renal ultrasound without renal cysts.

findings.text: wedged feet inward with metatarsal adductus

translation:
Identification: male, 16 years old, brought by the mother for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “he is much shorter than his peers.”

History of present illness: The mother reports that the son has always been the smallest in the class, with a stature well below that of adolescents of the same age. She also reports that since early childhood, the upper eyelids droop over the eyes. She refers that he sat, walked, and spoke at the expected time, without delay in development. He attends regular school, without learning difficulties, and there is no intellectual deficit.

Physical examination: Short stature. Ptosis of the upper eyelids. Hypertelorism. Short nose with inverted nostrils. High palate, without cleft palate. Without labial cleft. Micrognathia. Genitalia: the scrotal sac surrounds the base of the penis above it, with implantation above it; testicular tissue bilaterally, without cryptorchidism. Feet: wedged feet inward, with metatarsal adductus.

findings.text: large head in relation to body size

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation. Sex and age not provided.

Chief complaint: referral for skeletal abnormalities.

History of present illness: the family reports that the patient needs help with breathing, with a picture of respiratory failure. The accompanying observers also noted that the feet appear too small for the body.

Physical examination: head that appears large in relation to body size, although the head circumference does not exceed two standard deviations. Normal forehead, without frontal bossing. Low nasal bridge and short nose. Low-set ears. Short palms of the hands.

Complementary examinations: skeletal radiographs show shortened long bones, cup metaphyses and delayed ossification of the epiphyses.

Identification: boy, 3 years old, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric cardiology.

Chief complaint: "his heart stopped".

History of present illness: The parents report that the child fell suddenly unconscious, without pulse, and needed to be revived by the emergency team. At the examination, the monitor recorded ventricular fibrillation, reversed with defibrillation. During hospitalization, episodes of polymorphous ventricular tachycardia were documented.

Complementary examinations: 12-lead ECG with prolonged QTc, alternating T waves, and 2:1 AV block.

Management: Instructions to the family and follow-up together with cardiology.

Identification: female patient, referred to the hematology/genetics outpatient clinic for investigation of a hematological abnormality.

Chief complaint: "low platelets on blood test".

History of present illness: Patient reports that routine tests showed a reduced platelet count. Denies nasal bleeding.

Complementary examinations: Complete blood count with thrombocytopenia. Elevated VPM (likely von Willebrand factor). Peripheral blood smear with platelets of very varied sizes. Platelet aggregation with ADP preserved. Coagulation retraction normal.

findings.text: fingers stuck together by the skin
distance between the nipples without increase
male genitalia with topographic testes bilaterally

translation:
Identification: boy, 1 years and 6 months, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by the pediatrician for craniofacial and limb abnormalities.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that from early on she noticed the child’s head was “tall and short,” the forehead was very prominent, and the eyes were “protruded.” She also noted that some fingers of the hands and feet were stuck together by the skin and that the big toe was wide.

Past History: Gravidity without oligohydramnios, according to the mother.

Physical Exam: Brachyturcifacial. Prominent forehead with frontal bossing. Proptosis. Hypertelorism. Low nasal bridge, flared nostrils. Hypoplasia of the midface. Fine upper lip vermillion. High palate. Ears without low ear pinnae and without posterior rotation. Distance between the nipples without increase. Cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers and cutaneous pododactyly syndactyly. Wide halluxes. Male genitalia with topographic testes bilaterally.

findings.text: anterior projections in the form of a tongue

translation:
Identification: male, 31 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of skeletal dysplasia.

Chief complaint: “bent spine”.

History of present illness: patient reports that the spine is curved to the side and forward since childhood, with progressive worsening of the kyphosis. Denies foot deformity at birth. Denies history of hip dislocation.

Physical examination: muscle tone preserved in all four limbs. Hands with full range of motion in all joints, without contractures.

Complementary examinations: skeletal radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies, with anterior projections in the form of a tongue at some levels. Hypoplastic iliac bodies. Enlarged trochanteric bones. Widened metaphyses of long bones. Femoral heads of normal morphology, without dysplasia.

Identification: girl, 4 years old, brought by her mother, referred by the pediatrician for genetic evaluation due to facial features.

Chief complaint: "her hair doesn't grow much at all."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that her daughter's hair grows very slowly, needing to be cut rarely. She also noted that the eyelashes are very sparse at the tips, near the temples. She refers that the child follows other children of the same age in walking, talking, and playing, without delay in neuropsychomotor development. At school, the teacher does not observe learning difficulties; without intellectual disability.

Physical Exam: Wide forehead. Bulbous and voluminous nose. Long labial frenulum. Thin upper lip vermillion. Hands with metacarpal shortening on palpation.

Complementary Examinations: Hand and wrist radiography with delayed bone age for chronological age.

findings.text: ear with a cleft between the helix and the lobe
male genitalia with a penis length greater than 2 SD for age

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics.

Chief complaint: “different way of relating”.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that the child avoids eye contact, does not play with other children, speaks little and almost does not interact, maintains very restricted interests and repeats movements and routines in an insistent manner, becoming irritated when there are changes. They deny difficulty with breastfeeding, chewing, or swallowing.

Past Medical History: Shortly after birth, he needed support for neonatal respiratory discomfort. There was no omphalocele.

Physical Exam: Full cheeks and rounded. Micrognathia. Ear with a cleft between the helix and the lobe. Male genitalia with a penis length greater than 2 SD for age.

findings.text: episodes in which the child has stiff and extended arms and legs, with a hard neck
distonia in limbs and trunk, with abnormal postures

absent: seizures that begin in one side of the body
translation:
Identification: female infant, 11 months, brought by her mother, referred for neurological evaluation.

Chief complaint: seizures and developmental delay.

History of present illness: mother reports episodes in which the child has stiff and extended arms and legs, with a hard neck, for a few seconds. Denies seizures that begin in one side of the body. Refers that the daughter does not babble or emit intentional communicative sounds, as expected for her age. Also notes that she cannot sit, even with support, and that her head “falls” when placed sitting on her lap. Generally observes delay in all acquisitions since the first months.

Physical exam: global delay of neuropsychomotor development. Precarious head support. Distonia in limbs and trunk, with abnormal postures maintained. No chorea. Does not present ataxia. No opisthotonos.

Complementary exams: EEG with hyparrhythmia; in another recording, burst-suppression pattern. Brain MRI without cerebral atrophy.

findings.text: retinal pigment epithelium with a corrugated appearance

translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by ophthalmology.

Chief complaint: ocular abnormalities.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter frequently inserts her fingers into her eyes and repeatedly presses them, several times a day. She also noted that the child’s eyes were shaking, swaying from side to side continuously.

Physical examination: Rhythmic bilateral involuntary eye movements. On inspection and biomicroscopy, corneas with reduced curvature, without protrusion in relation to the sclera, without thinning or conical deformity. Fundoscopy: retinal pigment epithelium with a corrugated appearance, with spots of different colors; optic discs with pink coloration, without pallor.

Complementary examinations: Refraction under cycloplegia demonstrating hyperopia, without myopia.

findings.text: malformed pinnae with atresia of the external auditory canal
hair implantation projecting onto the tongue in front of the ears towards the cheeks

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 17 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: Referred by otorhinolaryngology for evaluation of facial and auditory abnormalities.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter was born with an opening in the palate. She also reports that she has always had hearing loss, and audiometry showed conductive hearing loss. She further states that the daughter has never had eyelashes. Denies a prior diagnosis of hydrocephalus.

Physical exam: Face with malar hypoplasia and micrognathia. Oblique downward palpebral fissures. Coloboma of the lower eyelids. Malformed pinnae with atresia of the external auditory canal. Hair implantation projecting onto the tongue in front of the ears towards the cheeks. Patent nostrils, without coanate atresia.

Complementary exams: Cranial tomography without coronal, lambdoid, or scfalotic craniosynostosis.

Identification: Woman, 68 years old, referred to the neuromuscular clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Weakness throughout the body and fatigue."

History of present illness: Patient reports feeling of weakness and loss of strength that accompanies her daily activities, with increasing difficulty with activities. The daughter noticed that the mother began to walk swaying from side to side. She reports having had several pneumonias over the past few years. She progressed with difficulty breathing attributed to muscle weakness of the respiratory musculature, reaching a respiratory failure status with the need for hospitalization.

Past medical history: Previous diagnosis of myopathy, under follow-up.

Physical exam: Generalized muscle weakness, proximal and distal. Weakness of the cervical flexors. Diffuse muscle atrophy. Global areflexia. Thoracic scoliosis. Eyelids without ptosis. Extraocular motility preserved, without ophthalmoplegia.

Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: referred following a diagnosis of thyroid tumor.

History of present illness: patient reports noticing a nodule in the neck, in the thyroid region. In investigation, the serum calcitonin level was above the reference value. The histological examination of the lesion revealed medullary thyroid carcinoma. Denies episodes of very high blood pressure of sudden onset.

Past medical history: no hyperparathyroidism. No pheochromocytoma.

Physical examination: palpable nodule in thyroid.

Identification: male, 21 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for etiological investigation.

History of present illness: The mother reports that he was delayed in sitting, walking, and in all areas in childhood, being behind compared to other children. He began to speak very late and his speech is still limited; he tends to repeat words and phrases he has just heard, without intention to converse. Since childhood, he avoids contact with other people, has very restricted interests, and exhibits repetitive movements. He becomes very nervous and tense in the face of changes or new situations, with exaggerated fear. He needs help with practically all daily activities, with severe intellectual disability.

Past medical history: In childhood, he had several ear infections, with recurrent middle ear infections.

Physical examination: Short stature. Gross facial features. Widow’s peak hair implantation. Bulbous nose. Small hands with short fingers. Prominent digital papillae.

Complementary tests: Urinary organic acids without alterations; normal plasma amino acids; urinary mucopolysaccharide search negative; urinary oligosaccharides absent; serum IGF-1 within the normal range.

findings.text: limited extraocular motility in multiple directions
muscle strength grade 4 in the scapular and pelvic girdles
deficit of strength in the distal musculature of the four limbs
shortening of the calcaneal tendon bilaterally

translation:
Identification: woman, 35 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for investigation of a neuromuscular condition.

Chief complaint: muscle weakness.

History of present illness: patient reports difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair, as well as difficulty holding objects with her hands and frequent stumbles due to weakness in her feet. She reports difficulty maintaining her head upright when lying down. Family members noted that the eyelids droop. She is currently ambulating independently, without loss of gait.

Physical examination: Ptosis present. Limited extraocular motility in multiple directions. Facial muscle weakness, with difficulty closing her eyes forcefully and whistling. Cervical flexor and extensor paresis. Muscle strength grade 4 in the scapular and pelvic girdles and deficit of strength in the distal musculature of the four limbs. Deep tendon reflexes abolished globally. Shortening of the calcaneal tendon bilaterally. Spine without lumbar hyperlordosis.

Complementary examinations: Elevated serum CK. Muscle biopsy with increased fibers with centrally located nuclei.

findings.text: arched eyebrows in a high arch shape
prolonged palpebral fissures with eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelids
prominent digital phalanges in the pulp of the fingers

translation:
Identification: female infant, 8 months, brought by the mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for referral from pediatrics.

Chief complaint: “she is delayed for her age.”

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter still does not hold her body well or interact or babble like other children of the same age, with delays in all areas of development. She believes the girl is “floppy” on the chest. She has also noted that one of the eyes sometimes “looks” to the side. Denies that the upper eyelids are droopy.

Past history: Prior echocardiogram showed ventricular septal communication and coarctation of the aorta; without aortic valve stenosis, without left ventricular hypoplasia, and without right pulmonary vein drainage to the inferior vena cava. Renal and urinary ultrasound showed duplication of the calyces and ureter.

Physical exam: Length appropriate for age, without short stature. Axial and appendicular hypotonia. Arched eyebrows in a high arch shape. Prolonged palpebral fissures with eversion of the lateral third of the lower eyelids. Bluish sclerae. Strabismus. Wide nasal base. Large ears. Prominent digital phalanges in the pulp of the fingers. Clinodactyly of the hands.

findings.text: droplets on the posterior surface of the Descemet membrane without endothelial cells

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "seeing worse and worse."

History of Present Illness: Patient reports progressively worsening difficulty seeing, with decreased visual acuity in both eyes. Previously evaluated by an ophthalmologist, who recommended genetic follow-up.

Physical examination / ophthalmic evaluation: Reduced visual acuity. At biomicroscopy, corneal dystrophy bilateral. Presence of droplets on the posterior surface of the Descemet membrane, visualized as dark areas without endothelial cells under specular microscopy.

Identification: female patient, 16 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "fainting spells".

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter has experienced episodes in which she lost consciousness suddenly, falling, with spontaneous and complete return within a few seconds, without confusion afterward.

Complementary exams: Resting electrocardiogram with sinus bradycardia. Transthoracic echocardiogram showing mitral valve prolapse and non-contracted left ventricular myocardium.

Management: Joint follow-up with cardiology.

findings.text: reduction in the proportion of memory B cells with class switching
NK cell count below the reference value

translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years and 8 months, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for immunological investigation.

Chief complaint: recurrent infections.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child has soft and frequent stools for many months, without improvement. She refers to several pneumonias since the first year of life, in addition to repeated episodes of bacterial infections that required antibiotics. She also reports that the daughter “catches viruses all the time,” with viral episodes in sequence. Since infancy, she has oral thrush and fungal rashes that always return after treatment.

Past medical history: Vaccinated with BCG at birth, without local or lymph node reaction after the vaccine.

Additional tests: Low IgA and low IgM. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping with reduced total B lymphocytes, reduction in the proportion of memory B cells with class switching and NK cell count below the reference value. Total T lymphocytes (CD3+) within the normal range for age; B lymphocytes not increased.

Identification: girl, 6 years and 6 months, brought by her mother, referred by the pediatrician for evaluation in hematology/genetics.

Chief complaint: "red spots on the skin".

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter frequently presents with small, reddish-purple spots on the skin, which appear easily, even without significant trauma. Denies nosebleeds.

Additional examinations: Complete blood count with thrombocytopenia. VPM decreased. Bone marrow aspirate with preserved number of megacaryocytes.

findings.text: rough, elevated papules centered on the hair follicles

translation:
Identification: boy, 2 years old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in dermatology/genetics.

Chief complaint: "the hair is falling out."

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child’s hair is falling out progressively, leaving thinning areas on the scalp. She also refers that the strands break very easily when combed or when touched to the pillow.

Physical exam: Scalp with rough, elevated papules centered on the hair follicles, with cornified white plaques. Under trichoscopy, the shafts appear beaded, with elliptical nodules regularly interspersed with narrowed segments.

findings.text: rhythmic shaking of both sides of the body
long time to say her first words
speaks much less than other children of the same age

translation:
Identification: girl, 6 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that, in the first few days of life, the child had a yellowish skin and had a great deal of difficulty breastfeeding, refusing the breast and accepting little volume. She also frequently vomited after feedings. She also reports episodes in which the daughter was completely rigid and then presented with rhythmic shaking of both sides of the body. She states that the girl took a long time to say her first words and still speaks much less than other children of the same age.

Physical Exam: Global hypotonia.

Complementary Tests: Elevated serum galactose. Reduced erythrocyte galactosyl-1-phosphate uridylate transferase activity.

absent: hitting her head against the wall
translation:
Identification: female patient, 64 years old, accompanied by her sister.

Chief complaint: referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of present illness: the sister reports that in childhood the patient was delayed in sitting, walking, and everything else compared to other children, and that she only began to speak words and phrases much later than expected. She refers to the fact that her mood changes very quickly, from crying to joy for small reasons. She has episodes in which she screams, curses, and even hits people in the house. Sometimes she bites her own hands and hits her head against the wall. She needs to repeat certain actions, such as closing doors and arranging objects, several times, saying that "she has to do it." The family notices that she laughs loudly in awkward situations, including funerals. They also note that her hands tremble when she holds a cup. The sister informs that she can wait and control her impulses without difficulty.

Past medical history: previous neuropsychological evaluation with moderate intellectual disability, without severe intellectual disability. Ultrasound of the urinary tract without ureteral duplication and without duplication of the renal pelvis.

Physical examination: head circumference appropriate, without microcephaly. Narrow palpebral fissures. Large ears. Long palate. High palate. Mandibular prognathism. Small hands. Hand tremor.

findings.text: height below -2 SD for age and sex
absence of firm or calcified nodules in the subcutaneous tissue

translation:
Identification: girl, 1 year and 10 months, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “She is very overweight and small for her age.”

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child is gaining weight excessively and that she notices that she is much shorter than other children of the same age. Previous multidisciplinary assessment with standardized tests revealed intellectual disability.

Physical examination: obese child. Height below -2 SD for age and sex. Hands with fingers of proportional length, without brachydactyly. Palpation, absence of firm or calcified nodules in the subcutaneous tissue.

Complementary examinations: Hand radiography shows shortening of the metacarpals. Serum calcium within the normal range. Serum phosphorus without alterations.

absent: episodes of generalized stiffening of the limbs with loss of consciousness
translation:
Identification: girl, 5 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter delayed in reaching milestones in all areas, both motor and speech and interaction, and that she sat and walked much later than other children. She refers that to this day the child stumbles and easily loses her balance. In school, she presents with intellectual disability according to neuropsychological assessment. She was diagnosed with cataract by ophthalmology. The mother denies difficulty swallowing. Denies episodes of generalized stiffening of the limbs with loss of consciousness.

Past medical history: No birth anomaly detected on examination.

Physical exam: Height appropriate for age. Flat face in profile. Ears with distorted folds and supernumerary folds, appearing crumpled. Bowed knees. Tibias present bilaterally on palpation. Ataxic gait, with dysmetria on index-nose tests.

Complementary exams: MRI of the head with reduced cerebellar volume and preserved form. Radiographs with delayed ossification of the epiphyses.

findings.text: limbs without shortening of the middle segments (forearms and legs) in relation to the rest
fingers and toes with complete extension, without camptodactyly
increased bone density of the calvaria

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "doesn't hear well," according to the companion.

History of present illness: the family reports that the patient was born with an opening in the mouth roof. They also report that many teeth never erupted. Denies gum growth or swelling over the teeth.

Physical examination: eyes well separated. Limbs without shortening of the middle segments (forearms and legs) in relation to the rest. Fingers and toes with complete extension, without camptodactyly.

Complementary examinations: audiometry reveals conductive hearing loss and sensorineural hearing loss. Cranial radiography shows increased bone density of the calvaria.

Identification: male patient, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “it’s much smaller than his peers and has short fingers.”

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child has always been the shortest in the class and that his fingers are short since childhood. She also noticed that some toes are shorter than others and that the big toe is wide. He refers good academic performance and denies intellectual disability.

Physical exam: Short stature. Hands with short fingers. Bounded hallux bilaterally.

Complementary exams: Hand radiographs show short and widened metacarpals, as well as widened phalanges. Lower extremity radiographs show short tibias and hypoplastic fibulas.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
weight and height significantly below the expected, with significant weight deficit
fundus of the eye with pale papilla bilaterally
episodes in which she becomes stiff, with rigid arms and neck
episodes of sudden frights, with brief shaking of the arms
episodes in which she arches her body intensely backwards, from the nape of the neck to the heels

absent: seizures with stiffening followed by rhythmic generalized shaking
translation:
Identification: girl, 5 years old, brought by parents, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

Chief complaint: delay in development and seizures.

History of present illness: The parents report that the child always delayed sitting, speaking, and interacting, lagging behind other children in all areas. Since early childhood, “she does not gain weight as she should” and grows little since birth. The mother reports that she regurgitates frequently after feedings and meals, with the milk returning from the stomach. She presents with episodes in which she becomes stiff, with rigid arms and neck, and other episodes of sudden frights, with brief shaking of the arms. She denies seizures with stiffening followed by rhythmic generalized shaking. The parents also report episodes in which she arches her body intensely backwards, from the nape of the neck to the heels.

Past medical history: Pregnancy without decreased amniotic fluid.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Weight and height significantly below the expected, with significant weight deficit. Global hypotonia. Eyebrows without accentuated arching. Chest without sternal protrusion. Fundus of the eye with pale papilla bilaterally. No cortical visual impairment.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI with ventricular dilation and thinned corpus callosum. Spectroscopy with lactate peak and reduction of N-acetyl aspartate. Altered intercritical EEG.

findings.text: below the lower limit of normal serum vitamin B12 level
protein in increased quantity in urine

translation:
Identification: female patient, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: alterations in laboratory tests.

History of present illness: patient brings previously requested tests by the general clinic, which motivated the referral. She reports that she was instructed to seek specialized evaluation after the results.

Additional examinations: complete blood count and bone marrow examination demonstrating megaloblastic anemia. Serum vitamin B12 level below the lower limit of normal. Urine examination with presence of protein in increased quantity.

Management: discussion of the case in a team and return with the tests brought.

findings.text: mouth pulled down on one side
head tilted to look at things

translation:
Identification: girl, 4 years and 7 months, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child began walking alone much later than expected and that she still speaks very few words, with speech and language delay. She refers that the daughter does not stay quiet, she runs around the house, cannot concentrate on a toy for more than a few minutes and acts without thinking, picking up objects and crossing without waiting. She also reports that she chokes and has difficulty swallowing food. Since infancy, when crying, the mouth was pulled down on one side only, while the other side remained still. The family also noted that she often keeps her head tilted to look at things.

Past medical history: Head circumference at birth was appropriate, without microcephaly at birth.

Physical examination: Height appropriate for age and sex. Head circumference within the normal range, without acquired microcephaly. Eyes spaced apart, nostrils anteverted, high palate. Global hypotonia. Compensatory head position.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI with corpus callosification.

findings.text: cerebellar ataxia of a non-progressive nature
push test with multiple steps backward requiring support from the examiner

translation:
Identification: male patient, 40 years old, referred to the neurology genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: imbalance and altered speech since childhood.

History of present illness: accompanied by his sister, who reports that he was delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and learning in early childhood, falling behind other children in everything. Since childhood, he has been stumbling and losing his balance, a picture that, according to the family, has never worsened over the years. He reports that he falls easily and has difficulty standing without support when pushed or changing position. The sister also observes that his speech is slurred and unclear.

Physical examination: cerebellar ataxia of a non-progressive nature, with wide-based gait. Push test with multiple steps backward, requiring support from the examiner. Dysarthria. Nystagmus present. Limitation of extraocular movement, with ophthalmoplegia.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI shows a reduced cerebellar volume, with preserved morphology.

findings.text: papular, follicular lesions, rough and brownish, on the outer face of the arms and thighs

translation:
Identification: girl of 3 years and 3 months, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that the daughter took longer than other children to sit, crawl, and walk. She also reports that the child has always been the smallest in the class. She noticed rough bumps on the outer parts of the arms and thighs. She denies that the child turns easily pale. There is no complaint of difficulty seeing far away.

Past Medical History: In prenatal care, the ultrasound showed a single umbilical artery. She is followed with cardiology for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and pulmonary stenosis. Hematology without record of juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.

Physical Exam: Short stature. High forehead. Hypertelorism, oblique downward palpebral fissures, and ptosis. Low-set ears with posterior rotation. Winged neck. Thorax with depression of the sternum. Smooth, non-curly hair. Papular, follicular lesions, rough and brownish, on the outer face of the arms and thighs.

Complementary Examinations: Ophthalmological evaluation without myopia and without keratoconus.

findings.text: medium vertical groove from the dorsum to the tip
U-shaped vermillion of the upper lip, with the central portion much higher than the commissures
testicles not palpable in the scrotum, located in the inguinal canal
hands without extra digit on the thumb side
feet without duplication of the hallux
lipomas along the midline of the central nervous system

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics for evaluation of facial abnormalities.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that the child takes longer than other children to sit, walk, speak, and interact, with delays in all developmental areas. They also report that he always seemed to have drooping upper eyelids, covering part of his eyes.

Physical Exam: Eyes well-spaced apart, palpebral fissures with downward slant, superior ptosis. Broad nasal base. Nose with medium vertical groove from the dorsum to the tip, dividing it into two halves. Median facial cleft. U-shaped vermillion of the upper lip, with the central portion much higher than the commissures. Testicles not palpable in the scrotum, located in the inguinal canal. Hands without extra digit on the thumb side; feet without duplication of the hallux and without congenital twisted foot. No encephalocele.

Complementary Examinations: Brain MRI with lipomas along the midline of the central nervous system. Cranial radiography without parietal foramina.

findings.text: palpable fusion of coronal sutures bilaterally

translation:
Identification: 4-year-old girl, accompanied by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “She was slow to do everything.”

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter was slow to support her head, sit, walk, and speak, always lagging behind other children in all areas. She also reports that the child does not respond when called from a distance and needs to speak loudly to be heard. In psychological evaluation with standardized tests, intellectual deficit was noted. Denies seizures at any time.

Past Medical History: No other relevant information.

Physical Exam: Child in good general condition, active. Cranium with palpable fusion of coronal sutures bilaterally, confirmed on imaging exam.

Complementary Examinations: Cranial tomography showing bilateral coronal craniostenosis.

Identification: girl, 12 years old, brought by her mother for the first consultation at the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neurology.

Chief complaint: "she was very delayed since she was little."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter delayed sitting, walking, speaking, and playing like other children, being described in the first years as global developmental delay. She refers to a previous hospitalization in the ICU in which the patient was in a coma. In previous hospitalization reports, low blood glucose, lactic acidosis, and a rhabdomyolysis episode are noted. The mother also reports that over time, the legs became hard, making walking difficult.

Physical exam: Spasticity in the lower extremities.

Complementary exams: Acylcarnitine profile brought by the family with an increase in tetradecenoic carnitine (C14:1).

findings.text: liver not palpable below the costal margin
focalization isoelectric of transferrin with type II pattern

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Accompanied by the mother, who reports that since infancy, the daughter was “floppy,” seemed lacking firmness in her body when picked up in the arms. She also reports that in early childhood, she delayed sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting, lagging behind other children in all areas.

Physical Exam: Generalized decreased muscle tone. Abdomen flaccid, non-tender, liver not palpable below the costal margin, without hepatomegaly.
