Complementary Examinations: Liver elastography with fibrosis. Lipid profile with elevated total cholesterol and increased LDL. Elevated alkaline phosphatase. Elevated AST and ALT. Low serum ceruloplasmin. Focalization isoelectric of transferrin with type II pattern.

findings.text: tremors when hands are resting in his lap
tremor improves when he uses them
feet stick to the ground for a few seconds
plastic rigidity to passive mobilization of the limbs
fixed dystonic postures in the limbs

absent: seeing or hearing things that do not exist
neuronal loss in the central nervous system
translation:
Identification: male, 49 years old, brought by his wife, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "memory loss and difficulty walking".

History of present illness: The wife reports that the patient has progressively lost the ability to remember, reason, and judge, to the point where he can no longer work or maintain social life. She states that he trembles his hands when they are resting in his lap, and the tremor improves when he uses them. He reports difficulty starting any movement and that when attempting to walk, his feet "stick to the ground" for a few seconds. He has had several falls at home. Some time ago, he stopped walking and today does not ambulate. He reports that the parkinsonian syndrome showed good improvement with levodopa. Denies urinary incontinence. Denies seeing or hearing things that do not exist. The family does not observe apathy or lack of motivation, and he does not present with episodes of confusion.

Physical examination: Vigilance. Reflexes osteotendinous are globally exaggerated. Plastic rigidity to passive mobilization of the limbs. Akinesia. Fixed dystonic postures in the limbs.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI without cortical atrophy. Pathological anatomy of previous cerebral biopsy: neuronal loss in the central nervous system, neurofibrillary tangles and Lewy bodies.

findings.text: increased percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes

translation:
Identification: 11-year-old boy, brought by his mother, referred to the pediatric immunology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: recurrent infections.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child lives with infections of the throat, nose, and sinusitis, several times a year. Denies recurrent otitis. Denies recurrent pneumonias. No chronic diarrhea. Does not present with recurrent episodes of herpes labialis.

Complementary exams: thrombocytopenia with positive antiplatelet antibodies, characterizing PTI. Low serum IgA and low serum IgM. Immunophenotyping with reduced absolute lymphocyte count and increased percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes, without reduction in the CD4+ ratio.

findings.text: spastic hypertonia in the lower extremities
reduced muscle strength in the lower extremities
exaggerated deep tendon reflexes in the upper and lower extremities

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 31 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: “Slurred speech and weak legs.”

History of present illness: Patient reports that people have difficulty understanding her because her speech is slurred, with mispronounced words. She also refers weakness in the legs, with difficulty climbing stairs. Denies imbalance or lack of coordination of movements.

Physical examination: Dysarthria. Spastic hypertonia in the lower extremities. Reduced muscle strength in the lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are exaggerated in the upper and lower extremities. Babinski sign is present. Absence of ankle clonus. Cerebellar tests without abnormalities, without ataxia. Calcanei deviated outwards in orthostasis, with bilateral valgus retrofoot; there is no cavus foot. No signs of peripheral neuropathy.

findings.text: triangular-shaped face, wide in the temples and tapering towards the chin
elbows extend beyond the normal, in hyperextension
partial agenesis of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: boy, 12 years old, brought by his mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that he was very late to speak and that he still expresses himself with simpler sentences than other children his age. She also reports that since childhood he did not hear well; previous audiometry showed neurosensory hearing loss. Prior neuropsychological evaluation concluded intellectual disability.

Physical Exam: Triangular-shaped face, wide in the temples and tapering towards the chin. Deep-set eyes. Thin eyebrows. Ears with posterior rotation. Feet with syndactyly between the 2nd and 3rd toes. Elbows extend beyond the normal, in hyperextension. Hypermobility of the knees.

Complementary Examinations: MRI of the head brought by the family shows partial agenesis of the corpus callosum and arachnoid cyst.

findings.text: height below the expected level for age

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: skin changes and short stature.

History of present illness: the family reports that the patient has always been shorter than their peers of the same age. They have also noticed, for years, spots on the skin with areas of lighter and darker pigmentation, thin and wrinkled skin, and small visible capillaries.

Physical examination: height below the expected level for age. Skin with poikiloderma.

Complementary examinations: complete blood count with neutropenia. Hormone evaluation with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Chest CT showing bronchiectasis and interstitial lung changes.

Identification: male, 16 years old, brought by the mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by hematology.

Chief complaint: "purple spots on the body”.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child frequently appears with small red spots on the skin, primarily in the legs. She also refers to large purple bruises, larger than a coin, appearing after minor traumas. Denies alteration in speech; does not present with dysarthria.

Physical examination: Ecchymoses in the lower extremities and forearms. Speech without articulatory changes.

Complementary examinations: Complete blood count with pancytopenia, with plateletopenia highlighted. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with hypocellular bone marrow and reduced number of megakaryocytes. Brain MRI showing cerebellar atrophy.

findings.text: non-compacted cardiomyopathy of the left ventricle

translation:
Identification: boy, 3 years old, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric cardiology.

History of Present Illness: Parents report a previous hospitalization in pediatric intensive care unit for a cardiogenic shock episode. They deny a cardiac arrest episode. They bring cardiology reports and examinations, described below.

Additional Examinations: ECG with sinus bradycardia, average sinus frequency at rest below 50 bpm, and prolonged corrected QT interval. On another tracing, a 2:1 AV block was observed. Holter showed no ventricular fibrillation and no polymorphic ventricular tachycardia; there is no T-wave inversion. Echocardiogram showed non-compacted cardiomyopathy of the left ventricle.

findings.text: ideomotor apraxia in the upper extremities

translation:
Identification: male, 57 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for investigation.

History of Present Illness: The wife reports that he began to walk unsteadily, losing his balance and bumping into things. Over time, he stopped walking and now uses a wheelchair. The family also noticed that he became forgetful, with difficulty in reasoning and following conversations. Denies hearing loss.

Physical Exam: Nystagmus present. Fundoscopy with bilateral papilla pallor. Spastic paraparesis. Ideomotor apraxia in the upper extremities.

Complementary Examinations: Head MRI with cerebellar atrophy. Cerebrospinal fluid with elevated lactate.

findings.text: severe short stature, below -4 SD for age and sex
thickened upper eyelids, without signs of inflammation

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by the mother for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: short stature and hair loss.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the son has always been much smaller than other children of the same age. She reports that his hair has always been thin and that over time it has started to fall out, leaving patchy areas on the scalp. She has also noticed that one of his eyes “is crossed,” deviating from the other when looking. She also reports that some teeth have never erupted, even much later than the expected age.

Physical examination: severe short stature, below -4 SD for age and sex. Small, short, and narrow face. Lateral bilateral frontal bumps. Prominent supraorbital ridges. Deep orbits with prominent eyeballs. Thickened upper eyelids, without signs of inflammation. Concave nasal dorsum. Thick upper lip vermilion.

findings.text: proximal paresis in the lower limbs

translation:
Identification: Male, 37 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of muscle weakness.

Chief complaint: Weakness in the legs.

History of present illness: Patient reports progressive difficulty climbing stairs and rising from low chairs, referring weakness in the thighs and hips. The wife noticed that the "scapulae are jumping" in the back when he raises his arms. He continues to ambulate without assistance, having not lost the ability to walk.

Physical examination: Evident muscular atrophy observed upon inspection. Bilateral winged scapula noted with elevation of the upper limbs. Proximal paresis in the lower limbs.

Complementary examinations: Elevated serum CK. Muscle MRI with fatty replacement of muscle groups. Spirometry with reduced FEV1/FVC ratio.

findings.text: increased spacing between the hallux and the second toe
reduced strength in the distal musculature of the lower limbs
fingers that do not fully extend passively at the interphalangeal joints

translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “walks and speaks with difficulty”.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter delayed sitting, crawling, and walking more than other children. She reports that her speech has always been slurred, with unclear words and difficult to understand. She also notes that the girl is shorter than her peers of the same age. Denies recurrent respiratory infections, such as frequent pneumonia or bronchitis.

History: Congenital bowed feet, noted since birth.

Physical Exam: Height below the expected for age and sex. Spine without scoliosis. Long, thin fingers. Fingers that do not fully extend passively at the interphalangeal joints. Feet in bilateral equinovarus, with increased spacing between the hallux and the second toe. Global muscle tone decreased. Reduced strength in the distal musculature of the lower limbs; preserved strength in the proximal musculature of the lower limbs and the proximal and distal musculature of the upper limbs. Absent reflexes globally. Dysarthric speech.

findings.text: short eyelids and with little vertical opening

absent: loose, wrinkled skin hanging in folds
skin returning to its place when pulled
aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by the parents, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child has little facial expression, with a fixed gaze and the mouth always slightly open. She also noticed that his skin is loose, wrinkled, and hangs in folds, not returning to its place when pulled. She refers that he has always been “soft” when carried.

Lower eyelids turned inward, towards the eyeball. Low-set ears. Global hypotonia. Clear crystals, without cataract. Testicles were palpated bilaterally, without cryptorchidism. No disproportionate tall stature. Spine without kyphoscoliosis.

Complementary Exams: Echocardiogram without aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
ears in cup shape, projected laterally, without helix fold

absent: conductive hearing loss in the audiometry
translation:
Identification: Girl, 12 years and 4 months, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: Evaluation of facial abnormalities and short stature.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter was born with a cleft of the lip bilaterally and a cleft of the palate also bilaterally, not restricted to one side. She refers that the girl has always been the shortest in her class. She states that the daughter uses very high prescription glasses to see far away since early childhood. Denies conductive hearing loss in the audiometry performed.

Physical exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Height below P3. Eyes well apart. Wide nasal base and sunken nasal root. Small and receded mandible. Ears in cup shape, projected laterally, without helix fold. No frontal boss. Chest with sternal depression. Corneal opacity on ocular examination.

Complementary exams: Echocardiogram without persistent superior vena cava and without triatriatum.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex

short fingers in the hands and feet

translation:
Identification: boy, 8 years and 3 months, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for short stature and school delay.

History of present illness: the mother reports that he delayed sitting, walking, and speaking, being behind other children in everything since infancy. Currently he has intellectual disability with significant learning difficulties. He reports episodes of seizures. He also states that the child is always sick, with infections that repeat throughout the year. He has a previous diagnosis of severe combined immunodeficiency; there is no isolated severe T-cell immunodeficiency.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Facial appearance is coarse, wide nasal tip. No hypertelorism and no superior oblique palpebral fissures. Short stature disproportionate, with short limbs and a normally sized trunk; limb shortening due to limited bone growth. Short fingers in the hands and feet. Single transverse palmar crease. Chest without pectus excavatum.

Complementary examinations: radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies and proximal femoral epiphyses are hypoplastic. Renal ultrasound shows no multiple cysts.

Identification: boy, 10 years and 7 months, brought by his mother, referred for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that, in the first years, he was delayed in everything compared to other children, with global developmental delay. He sat and walked much later than expected. He started speaking very late and still has poor speech. From infancy, he had a lot of difficulty breastfeeding and eating. He does not like to interact with other people, makes repetitive movements and always fixates on the same toys. He presents with seizures. The mother notes that he does not hear well. In school, accompanied by psychological evaluation, with a diagnosis of intellectual disability.

Past Medical History: During the neonatal period, patent arterial duct persistence was identified. There is ureteral duplication on imaging. Followed in ophthalmology for cortical visual deficiency.

Physical Exam: Ears with low set ears. No retrognathia and no micrognathia. Eye alignment preserved, no strabismus. Short thumbs bilaterally. Male genitalia with a penis of very small size for age; scrotal testicles in the scrotum, without cryptorchidism; meatus urethral on the tip of the glans, without hypospadias.

Identification: woman, 47 years old, referred to the neurology genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: progressive loss of neurological functions.

History of present illness: The family reports that the patient lost the ability to manage finances and the house, forgetting appointments and no longer being able to follow conversations, resulting in significant social impairment. The husband noticed that her speech became slurred and difficult to understand. She no longer moves her legs, which have become rigid. She presents with urinary incontinence and difficulty controlling her bladder, attributed by the team to neurological bladder dysfunction. The family denies episodes of aggression.

Physical examination: demented state. Dysarthria. Paraplegia spastic. Ataxia in the upper extremities. Supranuclear gaze palsy; saccades with preserved velocity. No tremor. Absence of signs of parkinsonism. There is no amyotrophy.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI with cerebellar atrophy and cerebral cortical atrophy. ENMG showing axonal motor neuropathy.

findings.text: macular hyperchromatic plaque on the trunk

translation:
Identification: male infant, 3 months, brought by the mother, referred to medical genetics by pediatrics.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the baby became jaundiced shortly after birth and that the jaundice persisted for many weeks. She states that his skin was becoming all red, scaling in practically the entire body. She also noted several dark spots scattered over the skin. She says he is not gaining weight or growing appropriately. Denies persistent diarrhea.

Physical Exam: Infant with erythrodermia. Macular hyperchromatic plaque, well-defined, on the trunk. Prominent forehead. No hypertelorism. Enlarged palpable liver.

Complementary Exams: Hypoalbuminemia. Elevated GGT; decreased serum IgG; IgA and IgM within the normal range. Reduced NK cell count. Persistent CMV viremia. Chest X-ray with interstitial pneumonitis.

findings.text: below -2 SD for age and sex

findings.text: absence of hair follicles in the scalp
absence of hair follicles throughout the body

Identification: Female, 25 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

findings.text: no edema on the backs of the hands
alteration of the cortical gyri pattern

translation:
Identification: girl, 2 years and 3 months, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neuropediatrics.

Chief complaint: developmental delay and seizures.

History of present illness: parents report that the child is delayed in all areas of development. She does not speak any words. It took a long time to hold her head up and sit, and to this day she does not crawl or walk. She also has difficulty picking up small objects and using her hands. The mother noted that the eyes shake from side to side. She has been presenting with generalized seizures since the first year of life. In the chart, head circumference has stopped growing, with a flattened curve.

findings.text: without significant interaction with the examiner

She refers to episodes of sudden and very rapid arm and trunk movements, as if he were shocked, several times a week. Since early childhood, he noticed that one of his eyes “goes into the nose,” deviating towards the nose. Today he does not speak, does not understand simple commands, and is completely dependent on caregivers.

findings.text: penis with stretched length below the expected for age
urethral meatus in ventral position, outside the tip of the glans
scrotal sac divided by a fissure in the midline
testicles not palpable in the sac, located in the inguinal canal, both of reduced volume
rough skin with red plaques that itch a lot, primarily in the creases of the arms and behind the knees

findings.text: urinary L-glycerate dosage above the upper limit of normal

findings.text: absence of fusion between the second and third toes of the feet

findings.text: continuous atetoid movements in the upper extremities

translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a pediatric neurology clinic.

findings.text: slip when picked up in the arms

translation:
Identification: Male infant, 2 months of age, brought by parents for initial consultation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neonatology.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that the baby is “floppy,” appears to slip when picked up in the arms. They report that he does not yet sustain eye contact or smile, and that he spends most of the time sleepy and unresponsive to stimuli. They deny episodes of seizures.

findings.text: diminished response to non-conjugated pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine

Identification: Female patient, 21 years old, referred to the outpatient immunology clinic for evaluation of laboratory abnormalities.

findings.text: involuntary and rhythmic movements of the eyes

Identification: female patient, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “episodes”.

History of present illness: mother reports that the daughter has episodes in which she becomes rigid and struggles, unresponsive, lasting for a few minutes, resolving spontaneously. She also reports that since childhood she has noticed some lighter patches on the skin of the trunk in a leaf-like shape.

Physical examination: hypochromic macules on the trunk. Does not present with papular, erythematous lesions on the face. No thickened, wrinkled, orange-peel-like skin plaque in the lumbar region. Fundoscopy without nodular retinal lesions.

Complementary examinations: MRI of the head shows nodules subependymal in the walls of the lateral ventricles and frontal and parietal cortico-tuberal. Ultrasound of the kidneys shows no renal tumors with fatty content. Chest CT shows no pulmonary cysts or other alterations suggestive of lymphangiomyomatosis.

findings.text: yellow white part of her eyes
enlarged liver below the right costal margin

translation:
Identification: Girl, 3 years old, brought by her mother, referred for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “Yellowish skin.”

History of present illness: The mother noticed that the daughter had yellowish skin and that the white part of her eyes was also yellow.

Physical examination: Active child. Liver palpable below the right costal margin, enlarged. Spleen palpable, enlarged.

Complementary examinations: Complete blood count with anemia. Reticulocyte count elevated. Peripheral blood smear with numerous elliptical red blood cells, cigar-shaped. Electrophoresis of hemoglobin without imbalance in globulin chain synthesis. G6PD level normal.

findings.text: multiple renal and pancreatic cysts of reduced dimensions

translation:
Identification: male, 21 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "high blood sugar".

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that elevated blood glucose was detected in routine tests. Followed by endocrinology, which recorded diabetes of onset in youth, without insulin dependence and with a profile suggestive of MODY type. Brings recent tests.

Additional examinations: Increased HbA1c. Anti-GAD antibodies negative, anti-insulin negative and anti-IA2 negative. Abdominal imaging revealed multiple renal and pancreatic cysts of reduced dimensions, atrophic.

findings.text: loose stools several times a day
below the expected weight for his age
small notch in front of the ear

translation:
Identification: male infant, 2 months, brought by the mother.

Chief complaint: referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the baby has loose stools several times a day and is not gaining weight as expected, being significantly below the expected weight for his age. She also reports that he has a dry mouth, cries without tears, and wets few diapers.

Physical examination: prominent forehead. Labial cleft and palatal cleft. Small notch in front of the ear. Ears with normal impaction. Patent nostrils, without coana atresia. Perineal opening, in the usual position. Signs of hypovolemia on examination.

Fundoscopy: chorioretinal coloboma.

Complementary exams: hyponatremia.

findings.text: skin with residual and loose, drooping folds

translation:
Identification: male, 24 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "loose skin that tears easily".

History of present illness: Patient reports that the skin stretches excessively when pulled and returns to its place immediately afterward. He refers to cuts and scratches taking a very long time to heal. He also notes that the joints bend beyond the normal range in multiple parts of the body since childhood.

History: Mother reports that she did not have difficulty breathing at birth.

Physical examination: Skin with residual and loose, drooping folds. Generalized hypermobility of the joints. Flat feet bilaterally, with bunion and hammer toes. Thoracic spine without scoliosis.

Complementary examinations: Bone densitometry with osteopenia. Radiography of the pelvis without squared iliac wings. Angiography without thoracic aortic aneurysm. Cranial MRI without empty atlanto-occipital sulcus.

findings.text: short stature for age and sex

translation:
Identification: boy, 8 years old, brought by his mother, referred to medical genetics for recurrent fractures.

Chief complaint: "He breaks bones easily."

History of Present Illness: Mother reports that her son has had several fractures throughout childhood, often after minor falls. The last was a fracture of the elbow. She also reports that he has always been the smallest in his class. Denies that the child has difficulty hearing.

Past medical history: Good school performance, no intellectual disability.

Physical exam: Bluish sclerae. Short stature for age and sex. Abdomen without hepatosplenomegaly. Range of motion articular passive preserved, without articular contractures.

Complementary exams: Bone densitometry with reduced bone mineral density. Alkaline phosphatase serum within the normal range.

findings.text: without adequate verbal interaction for age

translation:
Identification: girl, 9 years and 6 months, brought by her mother for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that since early childhood, the daughter has been delayed in reaching all developmental milestones, with global delay. She sat and walked much later than other children. Speech was also significantly delayed. She has always had difficulty feeding. The mother noticed that while sleeping, she snores and stops breathing several times during the night due to obstruction; polysomnography confirmed obstructive sleep apnea. She is followed by ophthalmology for high myopia and low vision of cortical origin.

Past Medical History: hydrocephalus previously diagnosed. Head MRI with hypertrophic corrugated plexus of the choroid plexus. Echocardiogram without bicuspid aortic valve. Uro-cystography without vesicoureteral reflux. Complete blood count without thrombocytopenia.

Physical Exam: brachycephalic skull. Global hypotonia. No hypermobility of joints. Does not present with knee subluxation. Severe intellectual disability, without adequate verbal interaction for age.

Identification: Female, 14 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: "She breaks bones easily."

History of Present Illness: Mother reports that the daughter has had several fractures throughout her life, often with minor traumas. She states that she took longer than other children to sit, crawl, and walk, although in other areas she developed at the expected rate, without global developmental delay. She does well in school; without intellectual disability.

Past Medical History: Pregnancy with premature rupture of membranes.

Physical Exam: Short stature. Drooping upper eyelids bilaterally, covering part of the iris. Sclerae of normal color, without bluish tint. Teeth without alteration of color or translucency, without dentinogenesis imperfecta. Limbs with bowing of long bone diaphyses secondary to multiple fractures.

Complementary Examinations: Radiograph of spine with platypondyly. Bone density scan with osteopenia.

Identification: newborn male, 25 days old, brought by parents and referred from the neonatal intensive care unit for genetic evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that since the first few days, the baby has been “swollen all over,” with the swelling spread over arms, legs, trunk, and face. The UTI team reports that the patient progressed with chronic kidney disease stage 5.

Physical Exam: Eyes well apart. Small and retracted jaw. Low-set ears.

Complementary Examinations: Renal ultrasound with bilateral reduction of corticomedullary differentiation. Magnetic resonance imaging of the head demonstrating microlissencephaly.

Identification: male, 14 years old, brought by the mother, referred by the school for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: "eats too much and doesn't learn like the other classmates."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that since childhood he was slow to sit, walk, and do things that other children his age did. He began to speak words and phrases much later than his siblings. She states that he constantly asks for food, eats in large quantities, and seeks out food hidden even shortly after meals. At school, the teachers report that he doesn't stay quiet, is easily distracted, and acts impulsively; he has a diagnosis of ADHD. The mother denies that he is aggressive towards people, animals, or objects. Previous neuropsychological evaluation revealed intellectual disability.

Physical Exam: Obesity. Esotropia on ocular exam.

Complementary Exams: Thyroid function without hypothyroidism. Normal EEG. Serum cortisol without elevation. Glucose within the normal range.

findings.text: visual acuity of 20/100 in both eyes
atrophy of the pigment epithelium of the retina

translation:
Identification: male, 19 years old, referred to medical genetics for ophthalmological evaluation.

Chief complaint: “the vision is getting worse”.

History of present illness: patient reports that he saw better before and that the vision has been worsening progressively. He refers discomfort and pain in the eyes when exposed to bright light, preferring dark environments. He also reports having great difficulty seeing at night and in poorly lit places. He notices that he bumps into objects next to him because he only sees well what is in front of him.

Ophthalmological physical examination: visual acuity of 20/100 in both eyes. Fundoscopy with atrophy of the pigment epithelium of the retina and branching of the retinal vessels.

Complementary examinations: perimetry with constriction of the peripheral field. Electroretinogram with a pattern of cone-rod dystrophy.

findings.text: reduced visual acuity in both eyes
retinal pigmentation in bony spicules in the mid periphery

translation:
Identification: boy, 8 years old, brought by his mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for ophthalmological evaluation.

Chief complaint: "doesn't see well in the dark".

History of present illness: The mother reports that her son has a lot of difficulty seeing at night and in poorly lit places, stumbling and asking to turn on the light. She also reports that he needs to get very close to the board in school and the television to be able to see.

Physical exam: Reduced visual acuity in both eyes. Fundoscopy: pale optic disc bilaterally, sharp retinal vessels and retinal pigmentation in bony spicules in the mid periphery. No areas of congenital chorioretinal atrophy in corrugated plaques.

Complementary exams: Prior electroretinogram shows dystrophy of rods and cones.

findings.text: diffuse muscle volume increase throughout the body

translation:
Identification: male, 21 years old, referred to neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "stiff muscles".

History of present illness: Patient reports feeling stiff muscles, with difficulty moving quickly. He also reports that after closing his hand forcefully, it takes him a while to be able to open it again, without pain. Denies weakness.

Physical exam: Diffuse muscle volume increase throughout the body, athletic appearance. Muscle strength preserved in all four limbs. Deep tendon reflexes hypoactive globally.

Complementary exams: Elevated serum CK. Muscle biopsy without COX-negative fibers.

Identification: female infant, 5 months, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics to the pediatric hematology outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: "bleeding easily".

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child bleeds easily, with bleeding that takes a long time to stop after minor traumas and blood collections. Denies projectile vomiting since birth; previous assessment without pyloric hypertrophic stenosis.

Physical examination: Infant in good general condition. Cardiac auscultation without relevant findings.

Complementary examinations: Complete blood count with thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, and anemia; total leucocyte count within the reference range, without leukopenia. In the peripheral blood smear, presence of giant platelets, larger than the erythrocytes in the field. Bone marrow aspirate with dysmegacaryopoiesis. FAN non-reactive. Echocardiogram without mitral valve prolapse and without tricuspid valve prolapse.

findings.text: thumb adducted, with the tip resting on the palm, near the base of the fifth finger
upper lip with a thin vermillion

translation:
Identification: boy, 3 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: delay in sitting and walking.

History of present illness: the mother reports that he took longer than his siblings to support his head, sit, and walk, and that she always found the child “soft” in her arms. She also reports that his feet were born twisted, turned inward and downward. She noticed that his skin stretched a lot when pulled and then returned to its place.

Past medical history: ultrasound of the kidneys and urinary tract with dilation of the pelvis and renal calyces. No testicles palpated in the scrotal sac since birth.

Physical exam: global hypotonia. Hypermobility of joints. Thumb adducted, with the tip resting on the palm, near the base of the fifth finger. Congenital clubfoot. Face: hypertelorism, oblique downward palpebral fissures, eyebrows joined in the midline, low-set ears, marked nasolabial folds, upper lip with a thin vermillion, and high palate.

findings.text: palpebral fissures without upward palpebral elevation

absent: decreased fetal movement perceived by the mother
rhythmic shaking on one side of the body
translation:
Identification: girl, 2 years and 4 months, brought by her mother, referred to the pediatric neurology clinic.

Chief complaint: seizures and developmental delay.

History of present illness: The mother reports episodes in which the child suddenly bends the trunk and arms forward, several times in a row. Denies rhythmic shaking on one side of the body. She refers that the daughter is delayed in everything: in sitting, in walking, in speech, and in interaction. She noticed that she almost doesn’t look people in the eyes and that she moves very little, staying stationary for long periods. Accompanied by a diagnosis of epileptic encephalopathy.

Past medical history: Pregnancy without decreased fetal movement perceived by the mother.

Physical exam: Spasticity in all four limbs. Palpebral fissures without upward palpebral elevation. No forehead bossing.

Complementary exams: Abnormal EEG. Cranial MRI with cerebral atrophy and corpus callosum thinning; adequate myelination for age.

findings.text: replacement of muscle fibers with adipose tissue

translation:
Identification: Woman, 65 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Accompanied by cardiology for cardiomyopathy. Reports a previous episode of transient weakness and slurred speech with recovery complete in a few minutes, evaluated at the time as a TIA.

Complementary Examinations: Echocardiogram with left ventricular hypertrophy. CK serum within the normal range. ENMG with myopathic pattern; normal nerve conduction velocities. Muscle biopsy showing increased variation in fiber caliber, increased centralized nuclei, and replacement of muscle fibers with adipose tissue.

findings.text: does not look people in the eyes

translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years and 1 month, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neuropediatry.

Chief complaint: “developmental delay”.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that from an early age, the child was delayed in reaching developmental milestones in all areas, with global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. He sat and walked later than other children in the family. He spoke his first words late and still speaks very little for his age. The mother notices that he almost never looks people in the eyes, plays alone, strings objects, and gets very irritable with changes in routine. He has presented with epileptic seizures, the reason for the neurological follow-up. He frequently complains of nausea. For more than a year, he has had few bowel movements per week, with hard stools and a lot of effort.

Additional Examinations: Brain MRI with a narrowed corpus callosum. Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy with reduced creatine peak in the brain. Elevated cerebral creatine in urine.

findings.text: episodes in which the entire body stiffens
struggles with shaking on both sides of the body
shows little interest in playing or interacting with other people

translation:
Identification: girl, 12 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: delayed development and seizures.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter was very late to speak and her speech and comprehension are still significantly behind other children of the same age. She states that she shows little interest in playing or interacting with other people, rarely makes eye contact, remains fixed on the same activities and repeats movements for long periods. She presents with episodes in which the entire body stiffens and then she struggles with shaking on both sides of the body. Denies prolonged seizures or seizures followed by no recovery between them. Denies hallucinations, delusional thoughts, or changes in personality.

Physical exam: patient with severe intellectual disability; does not fit into mild or moderate intellectual disability by the degree of functional and cognitive impairment observed.

findings.text: liver palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin
spleen palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin

translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by her mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by the pediatrician for evaluation.

Chief complaint: “she doesn’t hear right.”

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child has always been “floppy,” appearing looser in the arms than other children. She refers to the daughter not responding when called if she is not looking. Audiometry brought reveals sensorineural hearing loss. Mother denies seizures.

Physical exam: Gross facies. Forehead narrow. Low nasal bridge. Abdomen: liver palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin; spleen palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. Neurological: Generalized diminished muscle tone; deep tendon reflexes hypoactive.

findings.text: short middle phalange in the 5th finger
short middle phalange in the 2nd finger

translation:
Identification: boy, 3 years old, brought by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for evaluation due to developmental delay.

History of present illness: The parents report that he was delayed in sitting, walking, and speaking, being behind other children in everything. They report that the delay in establishing trunk control and walking was the most noticeable. The mother reports that he always had excessive flat foot and has had reflux since infancy. There were episodes in which he had difficulty breathing and was tired, requiring treatment.

Past medical history: Gravida without polyhydramnios. Previous respiratory investigation without bronchomalacia and without interstitial emphysema.

Physical examination: Narrow forehead, occipital flat. Eyes widely set and prominent, with proptosis. Wide nasal base and low nasal bridge; nostrils not anteverted. Hands with clinodactyly of the 5th finger bilaterally. Muscle tone preserved, without hypotonia.

Complementary examinations: Hand radiographs show short middle phalange in the 5th finger and short middle phalange in the 2nd finger.

findings.text: vocabulary well below the expected level for her age
upper eyelids covered with skin folds with eyes open
clinodactyly of the fifth finger of the hands

translation:
Identification: boy, 27 months, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: "still speaks very few words”.

History of Present Illness: Mother reports delay in speech and language, with a vocabulary well below the expected level for her age. She refers to general development being slightly slower than other children, with mild global delay. She states that since infancy, he had difficulty feeding, but that currently he eats excessively, always asking for more food and seeming never to be satisfied. She reports that the child frequently hits, bites, and throws objects at others. Denies autistic behavior: he interacts, looks into the eyes, and plays with his siblings. Does not present signs of anxiety. Mother noticed that his skin is very dry.

Past Medical History: Sensorineural hearing loss already documented in a previous audiological evaluation.

Physical Exam: Height appropriate for age, without short stature. Global hypotonia. Broad nasal base. Upper eyelids covered with skin folds with eyes open. Clinodactyly of the fifth finger of the hands. Dry skin. No hypertrichosis. Spine without thoracic lordosis.

findings.text: brisk and increased globally deep tendon reflexes
ulcers are present on the pododactylic tips

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a pediatric neurology clinic.

Chief complaint: "He falls a lot."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child frequently falls, trips, and easily falls to the ground while walking and playing. She also reports that open wounds have appeared on the tips of his feet, which take a long time to heal.

History: He walked alone at the expected age, without delay in his gait.

Physical exam: Spasticity in the lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are brisk and increased globally. Cutaneous plantar reflex is flexor bilaterally. Tactile, pain, and vibration sensation are preserved distally. Ulcers are present on the pododactylic tips.

Complementary exams: Electroneuromyography showing peripheral neuropathy axonal.

Identification: girl, 1 year and 11 months, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “yellow skin and a lot of itching”.

History of present illness: The mother noticed that the child has yellow skin for several months. She reports that she scratches herself all the time, even waking up at night to scratch. She also refers that the daughter grows little, always being smaller than children of the same age.

Physical examination: Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly upon palpation of the abdomen. Scoliosis on examination of the spine. Pointed helix of the ear.

Complementary examinations: Direct hyperbilirubinemia; elevated total bilirubin; elevated serum bile acids; elevated AST; elevated ALT. Coagulation study without changes. Plasma amino acids within the normal range. Serum immunoglobulin dosage normal. Echocardiogram without structural heart disease.

Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by the pediatrician.

Chief complaint: “developmental delay”.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter was more delayed than other children in sitting, walking, and speaking, with global developmental delay since early years. At school, the teacher reports that she is easily distracted and cannot maintain attention for long periods on tasks. The mother denies that the child is hyperactive or constantly in motion. She denies autistic behavior: she interacts well with other children, maintains eye contact, and has no restricted interests or repetitive movements. The family noted that her eyes “sometimes become misaligned”.

Physical examination: Head circumference appropriate for age and sex, without microcephaly. Upward oblique palpebral fissures, bilateral epicanthic folds, without hypertelorism. Bulbous nasal base; well-formed nasal alae, without hypoplasia. Smooth nasal filter and upper lip with thin vermillion. Strabismus on examination. Sharp fingers at the extremities. Joint hypermobility.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in medical genetics, referred by neuropediatrics.

Chief complaint: developmental delay and epileptic seizures.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the daughter has never spoken any words. She also reports that she is unable to hold her head steady when placed sitting, causing her to fall to the sides. She presents with generalized epileptic seizures since childhood.

Physical exam: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Eyes apart. Small and retracted jaw. Global muscle tone decreased, with little resistance to passive movement. Tendon reflexes are brisk, 3+, without clonus. To plantar stimulation, extension of the hallux bilaterally.

Complementary exams: Altered intercritical EEG. Cranial MRI with sharp corpus callosum.

findings.text: widening of the fissures between the folia

translation:
Identification: female infant, 9 months, brought by the mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neurosurgery.

Chief complaint: “she is delayed in everything.”

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter still cannot turn from tummy to back independently, while other children in the family had already done this well before. She also reports that the child does not progress as expected for her age in any area, both motor and in interaction and sounds. She notes that when the baby’s head turns to one side, the arm and leg on that side extend and the ones on the other side fold, “as if it were fencing,” and this continues to happen to this day.

Physical exam: Reflexes are globally exaggerated. Asymmetric tonic cervical reflex is present.

Complementary exams: Family-provided brain MRI reveals semilobar holoprosencephaly, hydrocephalus, dilation of the cerebral ventricles, volumetric reduction of the cerebellum with widening of the fissures between the folia, and a arachnoid cyst.

findings.text: nails damaged since he was little
nails thin, brittle, with an irregular surface, breaking easily
able to bend his fingers and elbows backwards much further than other children
dark pigmented area around the central portion of the iris in a cloverleaf shape

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: "his nails are damaged since he was little".

History of present illness: The mother reports that the nails of the hands have always been thin, brittle, and with an irregular surface, breaking easily. She also refers that the son has always been "soft" in the arms when he was a baby and that he is able to bend his fingers and elbows backwards much further than other children do.

Physical examination: Good general condition. Global muscle hypotonia. Generalized joint hypermobility. Palpation of the knees, patellae are not identified bilaterally. Ungual dystrophy in the hands. On examination of the eyes, a dark pigmented area around the central portion of the iris, in a cloverleaf shape, is observed.

Complementary examinations: Type I urine without proteinuria.

findings.text: high hyperopia, above +5.00 D in both eyes
visual acuity with moderate reduction, between 20/200 and 20/70

translation:
Identification: boy, 1 year old, brought by the mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by pediatric ophthalmology.

Chief complaint: "little eyes moving from side to side".

History of present illness: The mother noticed that the child's eyes move back and forth horizontally. She also noted that the eyes "turn inward" when he tries to look at toys up close. Denies that the child raises his chin to look and denies that he tilts his head to the left shoulder.

Physical exam: Horizontal nystagmus. Accommodative esotropia. Anterior segment without changes in both eyes. Fundoscopy with absent foveal reflex bilaterally. Refraction under cycloplegia with high hyperopia, above +5.00 D in both eyes, not representing moderate degree. Visual acuity with moderate reduction, between 20/200 and 20/70, not being only mildly low.

Identification: boy, 1 years and 9 months, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: “developmental delay”.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that since the first months, the child suckled weakly, took frequent pauses and fell asleep during feedings, with great difficulty to feed. She reports that he took longer than other children to hold his head up, sit, walk, and speak, and still interacts and communicates less than expected for his age. Denies seizures.

Past medical history: no other intercurrent illnesses reported.

Physical examination: good general condition. Weight and height appropriate for age, without growth delay. Oropharynx: cleft palate; dental abnormalities.

Complementary examinations: cranial MRI without abnormalities.

findings.text: absence of permanent upper lateral incisors

translation:
Identification: Woman, 43 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: Neck pain.

History of present illness: Patient reports chronic cervical pain. Denies headache. Reports regular menstrual cycles, however, very voluminous and prolonged, with the need to change pads frequently. Reports having had an episode in which the patella dislocated.

Past medical history: Reports that the lateral teeth in the upper arch never erupted.

Physical examination: Enlarged mandible on frontal inspection. Absence of permanent upper lateral incisors. Presence of a palatal torus.

Complementary examinations: Radiographs with osteopetrosis. PTH without elevation and without reduction, within the normal range. Serum calcium normal. Serum phosphorus normal.

findings.text: thick eyebrows that join in the midline
excessive hair of male pattern on the face
excessive hair of male pattern on the back
excessive hair of male pattern on the limbs

translation:
Identification: girl, 11 years old, brought by her mother, referred from pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: difficulties with behavior and learning.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter was delayed in sitting, walking, and interacting when young, with global developmental delay in the first years. She started speaking words very late and her speech is still poor for her age. She has a diagnosis of intellectual disability by the school team and ADHD by the neuropediatrist. The mother reports that she avoids contact with other children, almost never looks people in the eye, plays always the same things and repeats movements with her hands. She has episodes in which she hits her siblings, screams and breaks objects. She becomes very nervous and anxious in the face of changes in routine, fearing what will happen. She has never had seizures.

Past Medical History: Gastroesophageal reflux disease since infancy. Prior echocardiogram without communication between the atria and without tetralogy of Fallot.

Physical Exam: Head circumference appropriate for age, without microcephaly. Thick eyebrows that join in the midline, with accentuated arching. Nostrils flared, facing forward. Mandible of normal size, without micrognathia. Excessive hair of male pattern on the face, back, and limbs.

Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "purple spots appear on the body easily".

History of present illness: patient reports that purple spots appear on the skin even without having been hit or after light touches, which he has been noticing frequently.

Past medical history: systemic hypertension.

Physical examination: patient in good general condition, conscious and oriented.

Complementary examinations: blood count brought by the patient shows thrombocytopenia. Liver biopsy previously performed shows amyloid deposition in the liver.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
verrucous lesions on the dorsum of the hands
verrucous lesions on the soles of the feet

translation:
Identification: male, 24 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation, accompanied by the mother.

Chief complaint: chronic cough with sputum production and warts.

History of present illness: patient reports productive cough almost daily for years, worsening in winter, accompanied by pulmonary consultation for chronic bronchitis. The mother reports that he has always heard poorly, needing them to repeat what he said. He has presented with warts on his hands and feet for years, which reappear after removal. Denies recurrent ear infections, sore throat, or facial sinus infections. Denies recurrent herpes zoster. Denies recurrent herpes labialis.

Past medical history: difficulty in school since childhood; previous neuropsychological evaluation showed borderline IQ.

Physical examination: short stature. Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Multiple verrucous lesions on the dorsum of the hands and soles of the feet.

Complementary examinations: Chest CT scan with bronchiectasis. Lymphocyte immunophenotyping: reduced absolute lymphocyte count, reduced NK cell absolute count, decreased percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes, and decreased proportion of naive CD4+ T cells. Serum IgA within normal limits. Serum IgM within normal limits.

findings.text: uvula divided into two parts at the tip
tricuspid pulmonary valve without bicupid pulmonary valve

translation:
Identification: female patient, 61 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Patient reports being admitted to the emergency department for ascending aorta dissection. In cardiology follow-up, she knew she had mitral valve regurgitation, according to explanation received from the team that follows her.

Physical Exam: Upon examination of the oropharynx, the uvula is divided into two parts at the tip. Mandible of normal size, without micrognathia. Auricles with normal implantation, without low-hanging ears.

Complementary Examinations: Echocardiogram brought by the patient describes mitral insufficiency and aneurysm of the aortic root; tricuspid pulmonary valve, without bicupid pulmonary valve. Thoracic CT angiography shows no pulmonary artery aneurysm and no descending thoracic aorta aneurysm. Lumbar sacral spine MRI shows dural ectasia.

findings.text: cystic formations in the basal ganglia

translation:
Identification
Male patient, brought in by family members for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by the intensive care team.

History of Present Illness
Family reports that the patient ceased to awaken and does not respond to anything, not even when called, touched, or stimulated with pain.

Physical Exam
Patient in a comatose state, without response to any external stimuli.

Supplemental Tests
Brain MRI reveals cystic formations in the basal ganglia.
Elevated urinary sulfite level.

findings.text: webbing (moleira) took much longer than expected to close
pallor of the optic papilla bilateral

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: “loose skin and difficulty walking,” according to the family.

History of present illness: The parents report that the skin has always been wrinkled, sagging and drooping, without elasticity. They report a delay in sitting and walking. The mother noticed that the voice is very thin, high-pitched, persistently. They also report that the webbing (moleira) took much longer than expected to close. There is no intellectual deficit. They deny an acute hepatic failure episode.

Physical examination: Short stature. Flattening of the malar bone. Thorax with costal depression. Global hypotonia. Long fingers; without metacarpal shortening. Flat feet. Fundoscopy with pallor of the optic papilla bilateral.

Complementary examinations: Bone densitometry with reduced bone mass. Peripheral blood smear with hypolobulated neutrophils. Serum IgA without reduction. NK cell count without decrease.

Identification: boy, 8 years old, brought by his mother to the pediatric neurology clinic for referral for investigation of imbalance.

Chief complaint: "falls a lot".

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child falls frequently, several times a week, since he started walking. She states that he took longer than his siblings to sit, crawl, and walk alone. She also reports that his hands "shake" without him being able to control them, mainly when holding objects. She has also noticed that one of his eyes "is crossed" in relation to the other.

Physical examination: Esotropia on ocular examination. Ataxic gait, with widened base. Dysmetria on index-nose and heel-knee tests. Tremor in upper extremities. Achilles tendon reflexes abolished bilaterally. Distal muscle atrophy in limbs.

Complementary examinations: Elevated serum lactate. Elevated lactate in liquor. ENMG: axonal peripheral neuropathy. Brain MRI: vermis cerebellar atrophy.

findings.text: height elevated for age and sex

translation:
Identification: Woman, 52 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that she has always been the tallest in her family and at school. Refers to being born with bowed feet, turned inward. Denies a prior diagnosis of hip dysplasia.

Physical Exam: Height elevated for age and sex. Facial appearance elongated. Cranium without increase in anteroposterior diameter. No hypertelorism. Dental arches without crowding. Skin texture soft to palpation. Feet with equinovarus deformity. Absence of hallux valgus bilaterally.

findings.text: poorly developed base of the thumb
cannot bend the tip of the thumb
thin vermillion on the upper lip

translation:
Identification: female patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by immunology for evaluation.

Chief complaint: changes in the hands and face.

History of present illness: the mother noticed early on that the patient’s hands were thin and narrow and that the base of the thumb was poorly developed. She also reports that the girl cannot bend the tip of her thumb. Denies delay in neurodevelopment.

Physical examination: upper lip with thin vermillion. Eyes apart, without epicanthus. Nostrils underdeveloped. Small mandible. Hands with single transverse palmar crease, distal phalanges of fingers elongated and clinodactyly. No syndactyly. Clitoris enlarged in size.

Complementary examinations: hand radiographs with simphalangism of the thumb and short first metacarpal; immunoglobulin dosage with reduced IgA and IgM; lymphocytophenotyping with absence of circulating B lymphocytes.

findings.text: thinning of the nerve fiber layer of the retina

translation:
Identification: male, 60 years old, referred to the neuro-ophthalmology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "the vision was getting weaker."

History of present illness: Patient reports progressive worsening of vision, with difficulty seeing far and near. He also reports confusion regarding colors, particularly when choosing clothes. He has been followed by an ophthalmologist for glaucoma for years. Denies depressed mood, persistent sadness, or suicidal ideation. Family members deny involuntary, jerky, and irregular movements of the body or face, as well as excessive motor agitation. Denies nystagmus since birth.

Physical exam: Reduced visual acuity bilaterally. Fundoscopy with pale optic disc bilaterally. Neurological exam without chorea and without hyperkinesia.

Complementary exams: OCT of the optic nerve showing thinning of the nerve fiber layer of the retina. Brain MRI without structural abnormalities of the cerebellum.

findings.text: salvos de flexão súbita do tronco e membros

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by the mother, referred to the pediatric neurology clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that, still in the first year of life, the child began to present with salvos of sudden flexion of the trunk and limbs, consistent with infantile spasms. Subsequently, epileptic crises of multiple foci emerged. She also reports that he has difficulty feeding, takes a very long time to feed, and that he gags and has difficulty swallowing. She states that he delayed achieving sitting, well beyond the expected age.

Past Medical History: At birth, there was umbilical cord circulation around the neck.

Physical Exam: Global hypotonia. Does not present with nystagmus. Fundus of the eye without palor of the optic disc, without optic disc coloboma, and without optic atrophy.

Complementary Examinations: EEG showing hypsarrhythmia. Vascular imaging without vascular dilation.

Identification: male infant, 7 months, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics clinic.

Chief complaint: referred by pediatrics for investigation of malformations.

History of present illness: The parents report that the baby was born with an opening in the lip and the palate. They report that he does not hold his head well or roll over, and he little interacts or babble for his age. The mother noticed that he sometimes has his arms and trunk twisted in strange postures that take time to resolve.

Physical exam: Grimy facies. Labial cleft and palatal cleft. Wide palms. Hands with articular contractures, without central splits or absence of rays. Wide feet.

Complementary exams: Laboratory with low serum sodium and elevated urinary sodium excretion, characterizing renal salt loss. Renal ultrasonography without multilocular dysplasia, without hydronephrosis and without increased cortical echogenicity. Neuroimaging shows ventricular dilation without obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow, that is, communicating hydrocephalus, without obstructive hydrocephalus.

findings.text: fifth finger with radial deviation bilaterally

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 14 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Does not see well in the dark."

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter has significant difficulty seeing at night and in poorly lit places, stumbling over objects at dusk. She also reports that the girl has been complaining of poor vision, both near and far, even during the day. At school, she always needed support, with a slower learning pace than her peers; a previous neuropsychological evaluation concluded mild intellectual disability.

History: The mother recounts that the patient was born with an extra finger beside the little finger.

Physical examination: Hands with short fingers, disproportionate to the size of the hands. Fifth finger with radial deviation bilaterally. Presence of postaxial polydactyly.

Complementary examinations: Ophthalmological evaluation with reduced visual acuity.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
absence of syndactyly between the 2nd and 3rd toes

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 40 years old, brought by her sister for evaluation in Medical Genetics.

Chief complaint: Referred for etiological investigation.

History of present illness: The sister reports that when young, the patient was delayed in sitting, walking, and speaking, being behind other children in everything. Since childhood, she has presented with seizures. She also reports that she has always walked unsteadily, with difficulty of balance and coordinating movements. She presents with intellectual disability, depending on family members for daily activities.

Physical exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Nostrils anteverted. No hypertelorism, no proptosis, and no frontal bossing. Chest without pectus excavatum. Feet with bunion; absence of syndactyly between the 2nd and 3rd toes. Ataxic gait.

Complementary exams: Brain MRI brought by the family shows atrophy of the parietal cortex.

Identification: Female patient, 75 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: Elevated skin lesions.

History of present illness: The patient reports that, after minor cuts and scars, the skin grows excessively, forming thick, elevated, and hardened scars that exceed the boundaries of the original wound. She also refers to “overgrown flesh” in the eye, progressing from the corner towards the colored part, in a wing-like shape.

Physical examination: Height appropriate for age and sex. Nasal bridge without alterations. Nose of usual morphology. Hair without alterations. Presence of cutaneous fibroma. On ocular examination, pterygium invading the cornea.

Complementary examinations: Radiographs without signs of osteolysis.

absent: involuntary movements of the head and neck
translation:
Identification: woman, 64 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that the skin of the body has been becoming loose, wrinkled, and drooping, without elasticity. She also reports that the upper and lower eyelids have become flabby and with bags. She complains of imbalance and lack of coordination of movements. Denies hypertension, denies chest pain with exertion, and denies palpitations or irregular heart rhythm. Does not present with abnormal posture or involuntary movements of the head and neck, nor involuntary contractions of the face, jaw, or tongue.

Physical Exam: Gait and coordination tests with ataxia. On ophthalmic examination, cataract and trefoil corneal dystrophy. Fundoscopy revealing optic neuropathy.

Complementary Examinations: Perimetry with concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field. Skin biopsy showing amyloid deposition in the superficial dermis. Cranial tomography with cerebral calcifications.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
short stature for age and sex
spine with lateral curvature on inspection

translation:
Identification: female, 22 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation; accompanied by her mother.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that, in childhood, the daughter was delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and learning compared to other children. She also states that she was always the shortest in her class. She refers to previously documented neurosensory hearing loss in a prior audiological evaluation. She is followed with endocrinology for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Denies hair loss. Does not have high myopia.

Physical Exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Short stature for age and sex. Spine with lateral curvature on inspection and Adams test.

Complementary Examinations: FSH and LH reduced, without hypergonadotrophic hypergonadism. TSH low. GH serum below reference values. No diagnosis of hypopituitarism.

findings.text: reduced absolute count of CD3+ T lymphocytes
percentage of CD4+ T cells within the CD3+ compartment is below the reference range for age
percentage of CD8+ T cells also decreased
low absolute count of B lymphocytes (CD19+)
reduced absolute number of natural killer cells
proportion of gamma-delta T lymphocytes unchanged
reduced proliferation after stimulation with anti-CD3/CD28

translation:
Identification: girl, 9 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the immunology outpatient clinic for evaluation of altered laboratory tests.

Chief complaint: alterations in lymphocyte immunophenotyping.

History of present illness: mother brings previous tests performed, requested by the attending pediatrician, reason for referral.

Additional tests: lymphocyte immunophenotyping of peripheral blood with reduced absolute count of CD3+ T lymphocytes. Percentage of CD4+ T cells within the CD3+ compartment is below the reference range for age, as well as the percentage of CD8+ T cells also decreased. B lymphocytes (CD19+) with low absolute count. Natural killer cells with reduced absolute number. Naive and memory subpopulations of T lymphocytes in appropriate proportions for age. Proportion of gamma-delta T lymphocytes unchanged. Lymphoproliferation assay showed decreased response to phytohemagglutinin and reduced proliferation after stimulation with anti-CD3/CD28.

findings.text: joints with range of motion beyond the normal

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by parents, referred by pediatric cardiology for genetic evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that he was delayed in sitting and walking compared to other children. They also report that he started speaking late and still speaks only a few words for his age. He presented with episodes of seizure crises.

Past Medical History: Follows with cardiology for atrial communication and pulmonary stenosis, without congenital heart disease, without patent ductus arteriosus, without coarctation of aorta, without left ventricular hypertrophy, and without persistent left superior vena cava.

Physical Exam: Facial shape is atypical. Narrow palate. Excessive hairiness throughout the body. Joints with range of motion beyond the normal.

Complementary Examinations: The echocardiogram brought by the parents confirms CIA and pulmonary stenosis, without CHD, without PDA, without coarctation of aorta, without left ventricular hypertrophy, and without persistent left superior vena cava.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
increased glycine in the cerebrospinal fluid
discal body of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years and 5 months, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that shortly after birth, he could not feed properly, sucking very weakly. In the neonatal period, he needed to be intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. He presented with seizures from an early age. He had a diagnosis of hydrocephalus. The mother reports that he has always been very floppy and that he was slow to sit, walk, speak, and interact, with global developmental delay. Denies vomiting. No diagnosis of pyloric stenosis.

Physical Exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Small and retracted mandible. Muscle hypotonia. Hyperreflexive tendon reflexes.

Complementary Examinations: Elevated plasma glycine. Increased glycine in the cerebrospinal fluid. EEG with burst-suppression pattern. Brain MRI: discal body of the corpus callosum, without ventriculomegaly and without hypomyelination. Echocardiogram without patent foramen ovale.

findings.text: premature birth (less than 37 weeks of gestation)
short stature for age and sex
facial features with an atypical appearance

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation. Accompanied by the mother.

Chief complaint: "delay in doing things."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child delayed in supporting their head, sitting, walking, and speaking, consistently behind other children of the same age in all areas. She also reports significant learning difficulties and autonomy issues in daily activities, with a previous psychological evaluation indicating intellectual disability.

Past Medical History: In prenatal care, the first trimester ultrasound showed an increased nuchal translucency. Born prematurely, less than 37 weeks of gestation.

Physical Exam: Short stature for age and sex. Facial features with an atypical appearance.

findings.text: shedding scales all over his body
thick and hardened palms of his hands
thick and hardened soles of his feet
one eye wanders to the side

translation:
Identification: boy, 13 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: skin changes and difficulty walking and speaking.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child’s skin has always been very dry, shedding scales all over his body. She also reports that the palms of his hands and the soles of his feet are thick and hardened. She reports that he speaks in a slurred manner, with difficulty articulating words, and that he walks with his legs widely apart. She noticed that one of his eyes “wanders” to the side. He is followed by an ophthalmologist, who diagnosed hyperopia.

Physical exam: Rounded face. Deep and close-set eyes. Strabismus. No epicantic fold. Eyebrows without eyebrow ridge. Nostrils without nasal divergence. Uvula intact, not bifid. Neurological: axial hypotonia, hypertonia in lower extremities, deep tendon reflexes exaggerated.

Complementary exams: Family-provided cranial MRI shows displastic cerebellar body; absence of polymicrogyria.

findings.text: serum testosterone below the reference value

translation:
Identification: Male, 32 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by andrology.

Chief complaint: Difficulty in having children.

History of present illness: Patient reports that, together with his wife, he has been trying to conceive for some time without success, and male infertility has been diagnosed in the couple’s investigation.

Additional examinations: Semen analysis with volume within the normal range, but without any sperm identified in the sample. Testicular biopsy revealed a failure in sperm production, characterizing non-obstructive azoospermia. Serum testosterone below the reference value. Estradiol unchanged. LH within the normal range. FSH within the normal range.

Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: intermittent fevers.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter has repeated episodes of fever throughout the year, without a clear relationship to triggering factors. She also reports recurrent tonsillitis, with several episodes per year that keep her out of school. She presented with a seizure. The mother denies delay in neurodevelopment; the child is doing well in school, without mild intellectual disability.

Past Medical History: No serious or opportunistic infections suggesting immunodeficiency. Referred with a report of an autoimmune process documented in a previous service. No vasculitis described.

Physical Exam: Height appropriate for age and sex, without short stature. Palpable lymphadenopathy.

Complementary Examinations: Previous neuroimaging showing dilation of the cerebral ventricles.

findings.text: serum cortisol level below the reference value

translation:
Identification: woman, 47 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by endocrinology for evaluation.

Chief complaint: referral due to alterations in hormonal and imaging tests.

History of present illness: patient brings tests requested by the attending endocrinologist. Reports being concerned about the results.

Physical examination: patient in good general condition, cooperative.

Complementary examinations: serum cortisol level below the reference value. Reduced plasma ACTH. Abdominal CT scan showing macronodular adrenal hyperplasia.

findings.text: urethral opening outside the tip of the penis

translation:
Identification: boy, 13 years old, brought by his mother, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that he was delayed in sitting, walking, and speaking, being behind other children in everything when small. She also refers to episodes of seizures throughout his life. Denies imbalance or lack of coordination of movements.

Past Medical History: Born with a urethral opening outside the tip of the penis, at the lower part.

Physical Exam: Tone and reflexes without spasticity.

Complementary Examinations: Elevated serum ferritin. Increased serum iron. Elevated transferrin saturation. Reduced serum hepcidin. Liver evaluation without cirrhosis and without hepatic insufficiency. Brain MRI without cerebral atrophy.

findings.text: estimated creatinine clearance between 60 and 89 mL/min/1.73 m²

translation:
Identification: male, 66 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of renal finding.

Chief complaint: “cysts in the kidneys”.

History of present illness: Patient reports that imaging showed multiple cysts in both kidneys. Refers to hypertension for years, under follow-up with a general practitioner.

Additional examinations: Renal function with estimated creatinine clearance between 60 and 89 mL/min/1.73 m², corresponding to Chronic Kidney Disease stage 2; no criteria for Chronic Kidney Disease stage 3, nor for stage 4, and without Chronic Kidney Disease stage 5. Urine without protein loss. Abdominal imaging without hepatic cysts.

Identification: male, 29 years old, referred to the immunology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: red lesions on the skin and pain and swelling in the joints.

History of present illness: patient reports the appearance of reddish lesions on the skin, in addition to episodes of pain, heat, and swelling in the joints. He denies fever. He denies muscle pain.

Past medical history: reports a previous severe infection with the Epstein-Barr virus, requiring hospitalization.

Physical examination: erythematous lesions on the skin. Arthritis on articular examination. Abdomen without splenomegaly.

Complementary tests: complete blood count with leukocytosis. Serum ferritin within the normal range.

findings.text: meatus located at the lower part of the penis

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years old, brought by the mother, referred by neurology for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: "delay in doing things”.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that since infancy, the child was very delayed in supporting his head, sitting, speaking, and interacting, always lagging behind other children in all areas. She also reports that he always had a lot of difficulty feeding, with prolonged feedings and, subsequently, problems chewing and swallowing food. The parents also noted that he did not respond well to sounds.
