Past Medical History: At birth, it was observed that the meatus was located at the lower part of the penis, and not at the tip.

Physical Exam: Tetraparesis. Spasticity in all four limbs.

Complementary Examinations: Audiometry with neurosensory hearing loss. Brain MRI showing leukodystrophy and cerebellar hypoplasia.

findings.text: increased rigidity to passive movement of the limbs
postural tremor in the upper limbs

absent: sensation of any limb moving on its own or not belonging to her
translation:
Identification: Woman, 51 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Slowed down with doing things and tremor in the hands."

History of present illness: Patient reports that she has been getting slower to perform daily tasks, such as dressing and cooking, taking much longer to complete movements. She also reports that her hands tremble when holding a cup or keeping her arms extended. Denies sudden, involuntary muscle jerks. Denies falls or imbalance. Does not perceive the sensation of any limb moving on its own or not belonging to her.

Physical examination: Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy. Reflexes throughout are brisk. Increased rigidity to passive movement of the limbs. Bradykinesia. Postural tremor in the upper limbs. Unending corrugator reflex. Push test without alterations, recovers balance without excessive steps. Absence of apraxia. No dystonic postures in the limbs.

findings.text: muscle weakness of predominance proximal in the upper and lower limbs
absent deep tendon reflexes in all four limbs

translation:
Identification: girl, 12 years old, referred to the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of a neuromuscular condition, accompanied by her mother.

Chief complaint: "fatigue and weakness in the legs and arms."

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter is constantly tired, without energy to perform simple daily tasks, although she wants to participate. She reports difficulty climbing stairs, getting up from the floor, and raising her arms above her head. Denies difficulty swallowing. Denies episodes of respiratory failure.

Past medical history: In early childhood, she presented with delays in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting with other children. She has always had adequate weight gain and stature, without growth deficit.

Physical examination: Drooping upper eyelids, covering part of the iris. Extraocular movement preserved, without progressive external ophthalmoplegia. Global hypotonia. Muscle weakness of predominance proximal in the upper and lower limbs. Deep tendon reflexes absent in all four limbs.

Complementary tests: Elevated serum CK. Muscle biopsy: increased variability in fiber diameter and predominance of type 1 fibers.

findings.text: without posterior inclination of the forehead
drooping upper eyelids covering part of the pupils
without prominence of the nasal root
loses balance when sitting without support

translation:
Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter delayed in supporting her head, sitting, walking, and speaking, always behind other children in all areas. She reports that the child had a seizure crisis that did not respond, with prolonged duration, requiring urgent care. Denies episodes of absence typical, in which the child would suddenly stop what she was doing with a fixed stare for a few seconds. Previous neuropsychological evaluation revealed intellectual deficit.

Physical exam: Narrow forehead, without posterior inclination of the forehead. Eyes apart, narrow palpebral fissures, drooping upper eyelids covering part of the pupils; without epicantic folds. Wide nasal base, without prominence of the nasal root. Low-set ears. High palate. Hypotonic trunk, the child "loses balance" when sitting without support.

Complementary exams: Head MRI with sharp falciform cerebral body, without cerebral atrophy.

findings.text: velcro rales in the bases on inspiration
telomere length measurement below expected for age

translation:
Identification: male, 62 years old, referred to the pneumology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: shortness of breath and cough.

History of present illness: patient reports experiencing shortness of breath upon climbing stairs and walking longer distances, improving when he stops and rests. He also reports persistent dry cough, without expectoration of sputum.

Physical examination: digital clubbing in the hands. Pulmonary auscultation with velcro rales in the bases on inspiration.

Complementary examinations: pulmonary function test with reduced carbon monoxide diffusion capacity. High-resolution chest CT scan with a pattern of usual interstitial pneumonia; report describes pulmonary fibrosis. Telomere length measurement in leukocytes below expected for age.

findings.text: small and malformed ears with posterior rotation

translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: “she doesn’t grow and is always sick.”

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter always gained little weight and has grown poorly since infancy, being much below other children. She refers to the child frequently catching infections, one after another. She states that she took a long time to start speaking and forming sentences. Denies that the daughter hears poorly. In school she follows the class; previous psychological evaluation without intellectual deficit. The mother noted that the head was becoming small over the years, although at birth it had normal size.

Past medical history: Born premature, small for gestational age. Prenatal ultrasounds without restriction of growth intrauterinely.

Physical examination: Short stature. Microcephaly. Wide-set eyes. Prominent nose. Small jaw. Small and malformed ears with posterior rotation. Clinodactyly.

Complementary examinations: Hemogram with neutropenia. Cranial tomography without calcifications in the basal ganglia and without calcifications in the subcortical white matter.

Identification: Woman, 61 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: “Drooping eyelids and choking”.

History of present illness: The patient reports that her eyelids have been drooping for years, to the point of covering part of her vision. She refers difficulty swallowing food. Her daughter reports that the mother has been losing strength in her arms and legs and that today she can no longer walk, although she used to walk with a walker. Denies vomiting. Denies hearing loss.

Physical examination: Bilateral ptosis. Ophthalmia, with limitation of extraocular eye movement. Upper and lower limb weakness. Preserved strength in cervical and trunk musculature. No amyotrophy.

Complementary examinations: Electroneuromyography with myopathic pattern. Muscle biopsy showing red fibers torn with trichromatic Gomori and COX-negative fibers. Mitochondrial DNA analysis in muscle with multiple deletions. AST within the normal range.

findings.text: menstrual periods were very heavy and lasted more than one week
repeated episodes of bleeding from the mouth
fingers turn white, then purple, and then red in the cold

translation:
Identification: female patient, 70 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Reports that throughout her reproductive life, her menstrual periods were very heavy and lasted more than one week, although they occurred regularly. She also reports repeated episodes of bleeding from the mouth throughout her life. States that in the cold, her fingers turn white, then purple, and then red. Denies gastrointestinal bleeding. Denies prolonged bleeding after dental extractions.

Physical Exam: Skin without livedo reticularis.

Additional Tests: Bleeding time is normal. Platelet count within the normal range.

findings.text: retracted middle third of the face

translation:
Identification: woman, 33 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Reports difficulty feeding for years, with choking and a sensation of food stopping along the way. Has already received a diagnosis of achalasia by a gastroenterologist. Also reports documented neurosensory hearing loss on audiometry. States that her skin is very dry and that she has always had little body fat, from the face down to the limbs. Says that her family comments that she looks older due to very wrinkled skin. Had a previous ocular surgery for cataract. Denies delayed growth in childhood.

Physical Exam: Height appropriate for age and sex, without short stature. Normal cephalic perimeter, without microcephaly. Triangular face, wide forehead, deep-set eyes, retracted middle third of the face. Corneal opacity on inspection. Generalized lipodistrophy. Muscle tone preserved, without hypotonia.

Complementary Examinations: Echocardiogram with thickening of the aortic cusp and aortic insufficiency. Lipid profile with hypercholesterolemia. Ophthalmological evaluation without retinitis pigmentosa.

findings.text: severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction

translation:
Identification: male, 16 years and 5 months, referred to medical genetics by cardiology for evaluation, accompanied by the mother.

Chief complaint: "weak heart".

History of present illness: Patient in cardiology follow-up for congestive heart failure. Mother reports that the son has been followed for dilated cardiomyopathy.

Additional examinations: Echocardiogram with severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, below 30%. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showing myocardial fibrosis. NT-proBNP elevated. 24-hour Holter without episodes of ventricular tachycardia.

findings.text: hyperintensities in the deep white matter

translation:
Identification: woman, 64 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: progressive forgetfulness.

History of present illness: The daughter reports that the patient has been forgetting the names of people and appointments with increasing frequency. She also reports that she is losing mental capacities that she previously had, and that she can no longer organize and plan daily tasks, such as paying bills or preparing meals, without assistance. The patient complains of a constant tinnitus and says that she has become worse at hearing, needing others to repeat what they say. She has had headaches for many years.

Past medical history: Denies hypertension.

Physical examination: Cutaneous plantar reflex is flexed bilaterally, no Babinski sign.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI shows cerebral infarct and hyperintensities in the deep white matter, without reduction in white matter volume. Anticardiolipin IgG negative. Skin biopsy shows no deposits of osmiophilic granular material in the vessels.

Identification: male, 52 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of hematological abnormalities.

Chief complaint: alteration in blood tests.

History of present illness: patient reports that routine tests showed he was “weak” with his blood. He is accompanied by his wife for investigation.

Physical examination: height within the expected range for age and sex. Eyes without increased interpupillary distance. Hands with tenar region of normal volume bilaterally.

Complementary examinations: complete blood count with anemia and MCV increased. Erythrocyte adenosine deaminase level elevated. Hemoglobin electrophoresis without increased HbF. Radiograph of spine without occult spinal bifida.

Identification: female patient, 71 years old, referred to the outpatient immunology clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: recurrent infections.

History of present illness: The patient reports having had repeated episodes of infection that affect both the facial sinuses and the lungs, requiring frequent care. She refers to a previous diagnosis of vascular inflammation, accompanied in another service. Currently, she denies an acute sinus infection. She denies a history of peritonitis. She denies inflamed lymph nodes.

Complementary examinations: Chest CT scan brought by the patient shows bronchiectasis. Serologies: anti-Ro/SSA reactive; anti-La/SSB reactive. Anti-cardiolipin IgG non-reactive. Anti-TSH receptor antibody (TRAb) negative.

Identification: male patient, brought by parents to a medical genetics consultation.

Chief complaint: referred for evaluation of global delay.

History of present illness: parents report that the son is not quiet, is restless all the time, even in places where he should remain seated, such as at appointments and at school. Deny irritability. Does not present with inappropriate laughter. Deny seizures. No episodes of hitting his head against the wall or the bed.

Physical exam: at the consultation, he presents with severe intellectual disability.

Supplemental exams: Family-brought cranial MRI reveals a simplified gyri pattern and small posterior fossa.

findings.text: Serum IgM and IgG without reduction
adequate antibody response to the tetanus vaccine

absent: particular findings to record on this consultation
translation:
Identification: boy, 11 years old, brought by his mother, referred to the immunology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: intermittent fever.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child has repeated episodes of fever over time, which improve and then return. Denies recurrent otitis, recurrent pneumonias, or recurrent bronchitis.

Past medical history: Type 1 diabetes. Hypothyroidism.

Physical exam: No particular findings to record on this consultation.

Additional tests: Elevated serum IL-6; serum IL-10 also increased. Liver biopsy with hemophagocytosis. Serum IgM and IgG without reduction. Antibody response to the tetanus vaccine was adequate, without partial response.

findings.text: absence of single palmar creases bilaterally

absent: generalized seizures with a tonic-clonic phase followed by flailing of the four limbs
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: developmental delay and epileptic seizures.

History of present illness: The parents report that the child is significantly delayed in all acquisitions, both motor and cognitive, well below the expected level for his age. He presents with epileptic seizures that, according to the EEG brought, originate from multiple distinct foci. He has never had generalized seizures with a tonic-clonic phase followed by flailing of the four limbs, and there was no infantile spasm. The mother reports that he has significant difficulty eating, taking a long time to suck, chew, and swallow. She also reports that he frequently has upper airway infections, one after another. The parents perceive that he does not see well, does not fix his gaze, nor does he follow objects.

Physical exam: Head circumference above the p97. Prominent frontal bosses bilaterally. Absence of single palmar creases bilaterally.

Complementary exams: Cranial MRI with polymicrogyria, hypoplastic pons, and slender cerebellar body. Echocardiogram without left ventricular hypoplasia and without pulmonary artery stenosis.

findings.text: all pulmonary veins drain abnormally into the right atrium

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, accompanied by her mother.

Chief complaint: referred to medical genetics for evaluation of complex congenital heart disease.

History of present illness: mother brings pediatric cardiology reports. Denies recurrent otitis. Denies recurrent pneumonias or bronchitis. Denies persistent cough.

Complementary examinations: echocardiogram describes right ventricle with double outlet, with large vessels in transposed position, pulmonary stenosis, mitral atresia and hypoplastic left ventricle. All pulmonary veins drain abnormally into the right atrium. There is no atrioventricular discordance. Abdominal ultrasound shows abdominal organs without defined laterality, in an ambiguous arrangement. There is no complete mirror inversion of the thoracic and abdominal organs.

Identification: female infant, 11 months, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “She still doesn’t sit alone.”

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter is delayed in everything compared to other children of the same age, both in motor development and in interaction and sounds. She refers that to date the child has not been able to stay seated, even with support for a short time. She has also noticed that she seems “floppy” when carried in the arms.

Physical Exam: Small and retracted mandible. Normal height palate, without high palate. Face of fine features, without coarse appearance. Palate with well-defined pillars, of normal length. Superior lip without tent-shaped appearance. Global hypotonia to passive manipulation. Babinski sign present bilaterally to rapid dorsiflexion of the foot.

findings.text: amplitude of movement beyond the normal in several joints
longitudinal arch of the feet touches the ground

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years and 8 months, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred by the pediatrician for evaluation of physical and behavioral characteristics.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the child has always had significant difficulty coping with himself and with relationships with people, with moderate impairment in personality functioning, according to psychological assessment. Despite this, she states that he behaves appropriately when with peers and family members. Denies that he is inattentive or impulsive at school. He began to speak at the expected age, without delay in speech or language. He keeps up with the class well, without intellectual deficit according to school and psychological assessment.

Physical examination: Facial appearance elongated, with pointed chin. Without hypertelorism. Joints with amplitude of movement beyond the normal in several joints. When standing, the longitudinal arch of the feet touches the ground, with flat feet bilaterally.

findings.text: tremors of one side of the body

translation:
Identification: female infant, 11 months old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in pediatric neurology.

Chief complaint: “she is not developing like other children.”

History of present illness: mother reports that the daughter is delayed in everything: she does not sit, does not babble, and interacts little, when compared to other children of the same age. She states that the girl is very intensely startled by any sudden noise or movement near the face, with a whole-body jerk. She also refers to episodes in which the child has a wandering gaze to one side and tremors of one side of the body, interpreted as focal seizures by the team that accompanied her.

Physical exam: infant with global delay in neurodevelopment.

Complementary exams: MRI of the skull brought by the family shows a hypoplastic cerebellar body. EEG during wakefulness with hiparsarhythmia.

findings.text: speaks less than other children his age

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by his mother, referred for evaluation in medical genetics.

Gestational and neonatal history: pregnancy without polyhydramnios. Vaginal delivery, without cesarean section. At birth, a congenital bilateral clubfoot was noted. It was also observed that the testicles were not in the scrotum.

History of present illness: the mother reports that since infancy he had difficulty breastfeeding and, subsequently, with eating. She reports that he took a long time to speak and that he still speaks less than other children his age. He presents with moderate global developmental delay. He was diagnosed with ADHD at school. The mother reports that the bowel is constipated, with spaced-out and difficult evacuations. Pre-sleep polysomnography showed central sleep apnea.

Physical exam: height appropriate for age, without short stature. Deep-set eyes. Wide mouth. Global muscle hypotonia. Male genitalia typical, without genital ambiguity; cryptorchidism. Feet currently without deformity in equinovarus.

Identification: male infant, 1 month and 5 days old, brought in by parents, referred to medical genetics for investigation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that over the last few days the baby has been very floppy and lethargic, feeding weakly and almost not waking up for feedings.

Physical Exam: Anterior fontanelle depressed. Intercostal retractions present.

Complementary Exams: Chest X-ray with increased cardiac area. Echocardiogram with left ventricular dilation and severely reduced ejection fraction, below 30%. Elevated serum lactate. Elevated AST and ALT. Altered coagulogram. Plasma amino acid profile unchanged. Carnitine profile unchanged.

findings.text: bulbous and voluminous nose with prominent nasal root

translation:
Identification: Male, 21 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Always been small and has poor vision."

History of Present Illness: Patient accompanied by his mother. She reports that he was born at a normal size, but after birth he grew little, always remaining smaller than other children of the same age. She also reports that his head became small over the years, although it appeared normal at birth. Since childhood, his eyes have been shaking, moving from side to side continuously. He refers to always having had difficulty seeing, even with glasses. The mother also observes that his hair has always been thin.

Physical Exam: Short stature. Microcephaly. Triangular face, prominent forehead and micrognathia. Bulbous and voluminous nose with prominent nasal root. Small eyes bilaterally (microphthalmia). Nystagmus. Dental crowding. Milk-colored macule on the trunk.

Complementary Examinations: Previous ophthalmological evaluation with high hyperopia and reduced visual acuity.

findings.text: arms and legs became hard and difficult to bend
below -2 SD for age and sex
involuntary movements of a diphasic pattern

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by parents, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "episodes and delay in development".

History of Present Illness: The parents report recurrent seizure episodes. They state that he was delayed in sustaining head control, sitting, speaking, and interacting, lagging behind other children in all areas. They deny loss of skills already acquired. The mother noticed that he was “floppy” in her arms during the first months and that subsequently, the arms and legs became hard and difficult to bend.

Physical exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Axial hypotonia. Hypertonia in limbs. Presence of involuntary movements of a diphasic pattern. Ophthalmic examination without crystalline dislocation or subluxation.

Complementary tests: Low serum uric acid. Urinalysis with elevated xanthine and homocystine elevated.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex (microcephaly)
decreased muscle strength in the upper limbs
decreased muscle strength in the lower limbs
legs are weak, tiring and giving way while walking

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 20 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: Referred for neurological investigation since childhood.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter was delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting as a child, always behind other children of the same age. She also reports that she has had seizures since childhood. The patient has significant learning difficulties and requires assistance with daily activities, having a previous evaluation that concluded intellectual disability. The family noted that one of her eyes “goes out of alignment,” deviating to the side. She also reports having little strength in her arms to hold objects and that her legs are also weak, tiring and giving way while walking.

Complementary examinations: Previous EEG without hypsarrhythmia.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex (microcephaly). Esotropia on ocular examination. Spasticity in the limbs. Decreased muscle strength in the upper limbs and lower limbs. Babinski sign present.

absent: acute and prolonged neurological deficits similar to stroke
difficulty with reasoning in daily life
translation:
Identification: male, 44 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of a finding on an imaging exam.

Chief complaint: “Brain calcifications” seen on CT scan.

History of present illness: Patient reports that he underwent a CT scan of the head and was referred due to the finding. Denies headache. Denies acute and prolonged neurological deficits similar to stroke. He and his wife deny memory loss or difficulty with reasoning in daily life.

Physical exam: Patient without cognitive impairment on evaluation.

Complementary exams: CT scan of the head with cerebellar calcifications, thalamic calcification, and pallid globus calcification. ANA non-reactive. Serum calcium within the normal range.

findings.text: nose without increased projection of the tip

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by parents to the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics for evaluation.

Chief complaint: “He was slow to speak and to walk.”

History of present illness: The parents report that the boy began to speak much later than other children and still speaks little for his age. They also report delay in sitting, crawling, and walking. The mother reports that he sleeps poorly, wakes up several times during the night, and has difficulty falling asleep.

Physical exam: Low hairline at the forehead. Eyebrows join along the midline. No hypertelorism. Upturned nostrils; nose without increased projection of the tip. Normal nasal filter. Small and receded mandible, without prognathism. Teeth of increased size, wider than expected. Abdomen without umbilical hernia.

findings.text: sperm concentration within the reference range
total motility preserved and progressive motility without reduction
tail shows irregular caliber along its course

translation:
Identification: Male, 30 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by the reproductive medicine clinic.

Chief complaint: Unable to have children.

History of present illness: Patient reports that he and his wife have been trying to conceive for some time, without success. The couple’s investigation concluded with male factor infertility. He brings spermograms performed at the reproduction service.

Additional examinations: Spermogram with sperm concentration within the reference range, without oligozoospermia. Total motility preserved and progressive motility also without reduction. In morphology, the sperm cells present rounded heads, without an identifiable acrosome. The tail shows irregular caliber along its course. No curled flagella were observed.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
does not fix or follow objects consistently

translation:
Identification: female patient, 13 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: mother reports that in the first year of life, the daughter presented with sudden contractions in flexion of the trunk and limbs in salvoes, diagnosed as infantile spasms. Since then, she has evolved with severe global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. She walked alone much later than the expected age. Speech has been delayed and remains very limited for her age. She presents with intellectual disability. The mother states that she wakes up several times during the night and takes a long time to return to sleep. Denies chronic constipation. She has not yet presented with any signs of puberty.

Past medical history: pulmonary stenosis and patent foramen ovale identified on echocardiogram.

Physical examination: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Short stature. Weight below the expected age. Generalized decreased muscle tone. Does not fix or follow objects consistently, with cortical visual deficit. Absence of secondary sexual characteristics.

Complementary examinations: altered interictal EEG. Brain MRI without myelination delay and without cortical dysplasia. Ophthalmological evaluation without hyperopia and without myopia.

findings.text: short stature for age and sex
male genitalia with testicular position bilaterally in the scrotum
meatus urethral at the tip of the glans

translation:
Identification: male, 16 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for investigation of developmental delay.

History of present illness: The mother reports that he was delayed in sitting and walking, always behind other children in motor skills. He also started speaking his first words much later than expected and still expresses himself with simple sentences. She refers to his behavior as being different since early childhood, with reactions that the family considers strange for his age. She also reports that his bowels have never functioned properly, with periods of constipation and other periods of disorganized evacuations, being followed by gastroenterology for intestinal motility alterations. In childhood, he had a diagnosis of vesicoureteral reflux. He wears glasses because he has poor vision at a distance. Denies pain.

Past medical history: Ophthalmic follow-up for retinopathy.

Physical exam: Short stature for age and sex. Head circumference below -2 SD (microcephaly). Palpebral fissures without upward slant and of normal length. Male genitalia with testicular position bilaterally in the scrotum; meatus urethral at the tip of the glans, without hypospadias.

findings.text: urinating in large volume during the day
drinking excessive amounts of water throughout the day

translation:
Identification: male, 19 years old, referred to endocrinology/genetics for evaluation of young-onset diabetes.

Chief complaint: "urinating a lot and with a lot of thirst".

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that he has been getting up several times at night to urinate and urinating in large volume during the day. He also reports intense thirst, drinking excessive amounts of water throughout the day. He was attended to in the emergency room, where an elevated blood glucose level and ketones present in the urine were noted, as well as venous acidemia in the gasometry.

Additional Tests: Elevated HbA1c. Low insulinemia. Anti-GAD negative. Clinical picture classified as MODY diabetes.

Treatment: outpatient follow-up.

findings.text: heart positioned in the left hemithorax
Interatrial septum present, without unicuspid atrium
Aortic arch to the left, without right aortic arch
visceral organs in mirror image inverted position

translation:
Identification: female patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Brought by the mother, who brings previous imaging exam reports. The mother denies that the daughter had recurrent pneumonias.

Additional Examinations:
Fetal Ultrasound with Doppler: absence of venous duct formation.
Cranial Magnetic Resonance Imaging: small, underdeveloped vermis cerebelli; dilated fourth ventricle.
Chest X-ray: cardiomegaly. Heart positioned in the left hemithorax, without dextrocardia.
Echocardiogram: Mitral valve perimembranous defect; patent foramen ovale. Interatrial septum present, without unicuspid atrium. Aortic arch to the left, without right aortic arch.
Abdominal Ultrasound: visceral organs in mirror image inverted position; reduced, hypoplastic spleen, without multiple accessory spleens.

findings.text: height above the expected range for age and sex

translation:
Identification: Woman, 26 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: Reports difficulty swallowing food since a long time. States that she sees well up close, but sees blurred at a distance. Uses hearing aid; previous audiometry showed neurosensory hearing loss. In childhood, vesicoureteral reflux was diagnosed. Denies constipation.

Past Medical History: The mother reports that she was born with a cleft lip, surgically corrected. No delay in neurodevelopmental development in early childhood. Previous examinations showed cholestasis and elevated transaminases.

Physical Exam: Height above the expected range for age and sex. Drooping upper eyelids, covering part of the pupils. Large ears, with thin helix. Small jaw. Bifid uvula and submucosal cleft palate observed by oroscopy. Spine without scoliosis.

Complementary Examinations: Ophthalmological evaluation with slit lamp identified posterior embryotoxon.

findings.text: shifts upwards of the umbilical scar
gait without foot support at the heel

absent: stiff joints in multiple parts of the body
needing to support herself with the handrail
being born with stiff joints in multiple parts of the body
translation:
Identification: woman, 50 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of muscle weakness.

Chief complaint: fatigue in the legs and difficulty climbing stairs.

History of present illness: reports difficulty climbing stairs, needing to support herself with the handrail. She also reports that she can no longer run. Denies being born with stiff joints in multiple parts of the body. Family reports that she has never had difficulty with learning or intellectual delay.

Physical exam: weakness of the shoulder girdle and pelvis. Weakness of the cervical and paravertebral musculature. When elevating the head in dorsal decubitus, the umbilical scar shifts upwards. Deep tendon reflexes are globally diminished. Feet with normal plantar arch, without cavus. Gait without foot support at the heel.

Complementary exams: CK slightly elevated. ENMG with myopathic pattern. Muscle RM with fatty replacement of the musculature. Muscle biopsy with increased central nuclei in fibers, without fiber necrosis.

Identification: Female patient, 51 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: Muscle pain.

History of present illness: Patient reports muscle pain and refers that she is unable to keep up with physical activities like other people her age, needing to interrupt walks and efforts before expected. Denies episodes of rhabdomyolysis. Denies muscle weakness.

History: No specific learning difficulties in school life. Does not present with autistic behavior.

Physical examination: Muscle strength preserved in all four limbs.

Complementary examinations: Elevated serum CK. Electroneuromyography with normal nerve conduction velocities.

findings.text: palor of the optic papilla bilateral
rapid and involuntary ‘chorea’ movements throughout the body
periods of repetitive and stereotyped rocking on the same arm
altered gait when attempting to take steps with support

absent: crises with rigidity followed by shaking on both sides of the body
translation:
Identification: girl, 1 year and 1 month, brought by her mother, referred for evaluation in medical genetics.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that the child is delayed in everything for her age, both motor and in interaction and language. She reports that the daughter has a great difficulty breastfeeding and eating, with prolonged feedings. She noticed that she is excessively startled by any noise or movement near the face. She also noticed rapid and involuntary “chorea” movements throughout the body, that appear spontaneously. There are prolonged periods of repetitive and stereotyped rocking on the same arm, that repeat every few seconds for days. Denies crises with rigidity followed by shaking on both sides of the body. When attempting to take steps with support, the gait is very altered.

Physical Exam: eyes misaligned, with esotropia. Upper eyelids droopy, covering part of the pupil. Nystagmus present. No epicanthus. Nasal root without prominence. Trunk hypotonia, with spasticity in the limbs. Cognitive and adaptive performance is much below the expected, with intellectual deficit. Fundoscopy: palor of the optic papilla bilateral.

Complementary Examinations: elevated serum lactate. Muscle biopsy without ragged red fibers; reduced activity of the mitochondrial complex I of the respiratory chain. ENMG without decremental response to repetitive stimulation.

findings.text: absence of a single median superior central incisor
feet with prominent heel and convex plantar surface, resembling a hammerhead
morphological alteration of the vermis cerebelli

translation:
Identification: patient referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: multiple malformations.

History of present illness: the family reports that since birth they noticed that the nose has only one nostril and that the chin is very small and recessed. They also noticed that one of the eyes appears much smaller than normal.

Physical examination: bifid upper lip. Single nostril. Microphthalmia. Micrognathia. Tongue of normal appearance. Absence of a single median superior central incisor. Feet with prominent heel and convex plantar surface, resembling a hammerhead. No increased separation between the hallux and the second toe. Calvaria present, without anencephaly.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI with lobar holoprosencephaly, thalamic fusion, hypothalamic dysplasia, morphological alteration of the vermis cerebelli and abnormally shaped sella turcica; adenohypophysis in normal position, without ectopic tissue. Transthoracic echocardiogram with atrial septal defect (ASD). Abdominal imaging evaluation with hypoplasia of the adrenal glands. Fundoscopy revealing retinal dysplasia.

findings.text: hyperintensities in deep white matter on T2/FLAIR

translation:
Identification: female patient, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for investigation.

Chief complaint: referral due to imaging findings.

History of present illness: patient with a history of lacunar stroke, brought for ambulatory evaluation. Family reports concern regarding the findings of the MRI.

Past medical history: denies diabetes. Does not have hypertension, according to the patient and family.

Additional examinations: Head MRI shows reduction in volumetric parenchymal tissue, widened perivascular spaces, and hyperintensities in deep white matter on T2/FLAIR.

findings.text: low implantation of hair on the forehead

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years old, brought by the mother for evaluation in medical genetics, referred by the pediatrician.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that during gestation she felt the baby move very little. Since infancy, she noticed that he was “mushy,” with the body loose on her lap. She also refers that he cannot fully extend or bend his arms at the level of the elbows and that the feet always remained crooked due to position, without alteration in the bones.

Physical Exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex (microcephaly). Low implantation of hair on the forehead. Triangular shaped face. Micrognathia. Oblique palpebral fissures downward. Palate without elevation. Palate filter of normal length. Columella without shortening. Hands with syndactyly and camptodactyly; fingers without overlap. Contracture in flexion of wrists. Contracture of elbows. Knees with complete passive range of motion, without contractures. Spine with scoliosis and accentuated thoracic kyphosis. Global hypotonia.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
deep tendon reflexes are brisk globally

translation:
Identification: female patient, brought by her mother for evaluation in neurology outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: "she is losing what she already knew how to do."

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter has stopped doing things she previously could do, such as sitting and walking alone. She also noticed that she was losing her understanding, failing to recognize objects and to follow activities she previously performed. She also reports that the child is dribbling excessively, wetting her clothes frequently, and that her speech has become slurred, difficult to understand. She states that the girl walks with great difficulty, stumbling and needing support.

Physical exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Height below the 3rd percentile. Tetraparesis spastic. Deep tendon reflexes are brisk globally. Does not present with dystonic postures.

Complementary exams: Brain MRI shows cerebral atrophy and cerebellar atrophy.

findings.text: no excess of hair on the body

translation:
Identification: boy, 1 year and 1 month, brought in by the parents, referred to medical genetics.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that the child does not yet speak any words or babble like other children of the same age. He cannot sit alone and still, and he has not yet started to walk. He presented with episodes of seizure crises. Severe global delay of neuropsychomotor development.

Physical Exam: Axial hypotonia. Tetraparesis spastic. Lower lip without eversion. Ears without posterior rotation. No excess of hair on the body.

Fundoscopy: Retinal hemorrhages. No tortuosity of the retinal arteries. Absence of vitreous hemorrhage.

Complementary Examinations: Neuroimaging with hydrocephalus, intracranial hemorrhage, hydranencephaly, dilation of the lateral ventricles and sharp corpus callosum.

findings.text: circumlocutions when trying to name objects
hyperintensity in the cerebral white matter on T2/FLAIR weighted sequences

translation:
Identification: Woman, 38 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Forgetfulness and difficulty remembering the names of things."

History of present illness: Patient reports that she frequently cannot say the names of known people and objects of daily life, although she recognizes them and can describe what they are used for. Her husband, who accompanies her, reports that she does not retain new information: she forgets recent conversations, messages, and appointments scheduled just a few days before. She maintains her work and social and domestic activities independently, without a demential syndrome.

Neurological exam: On neurological examination, the difficulty with naming is confirmed, with circumlocutions when trying to name objects presented.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI shows hyperintensity in the cerebral white matter on T2/FLAIR weighted sequences. No cerebral atrophy.

findings.text: evident muscle atrophy in the lower extremities
reduced muscle strength in the distal musculature of the upper extremities
weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles
distal paresis in the lower extremities
strength preserved (grade 5) in the proximal musculature of the upper and lower extremities

translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: weakness in the hands and feet.

History of present illness: The patient reports progressive difficulty buttoning clothes and holding objects firmly, as well as frequently tripping due to inability to lift the toes. He reports being able to climb stairs and rise from a chair without difficulty, as well as comb his hair and lift objects above his head normally. He denies tingling, numbness, or any changes in sensation.

Physical exam: evident muscle atrophy in the lower extremities. Reduced muscle strength in the distal musculature of the upper extremities, with weakness of the wrist extensors and intrinsic hand muscles, and distal paresis in the lower extremities, with a deficit of dorsiflexion and plantar flexion. Strength preserved (grade 5) in the proximal musculature of the upper and lower extremities. Sensation exam without abnormalities.

Identification: female infant, 11 months old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “she is delayed in everything and doesn’t gain weight.”

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter still does not sit without support, does not babble syllables, and interacts little, with delays in all areas of development when compared to other children of the same age. She refers to never losing skills already acquired. She also reports that the suckling is prolonged and laborious, the child gets tired, poorly accepts the puree, and gags easily when eating. Denies vomiting. The mother also noticed that the girl’s eyes “are crossed,” one of them deviating.

Past History: No prior diagnosis of heart failure.

Physical Exam: Weight and length significantly below the expected for age, with significant growth deficit. Global hypotonia on examination, with little resistance to passive movement. Esotropia present.

Complementary Examinations: Echocardiogram without hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy of the Cranium with increased lactate peak. Organic acids in urine without increased dicarboxylic acids.

findings.text: frequent muscle pain in the limbs
weakness of predominance proximal in the four limbs

translation:
Identification: male, 35 years old, referred to neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: progressive muscle weakness.

History of present illness: Patient reports that, over the years, he has begun to walk swaying from side to side, with increasing difficulty walking, until he completely lost the ability to walk, and is now restricted to a wheelchair. He refers frequent muscle pain in the limbs. He has evolved with secondary respiratory failure due to weakness of the respiratory musculature.

Physical examination: Weakness of predominance proximal in the four limbs. Weakness of the axial musculature, with difficulty sustaining the neck and trunk. Diffuse muscle atrophy. Calf muscles increased in volume, hypertrophic. Deep tendon reflexes hypoactive.

Complementary examinations: Echocardiogram without structural cardiac abnormalities.

findings.text: watery stools several times a day

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that the child began walking much later than other children and that he still walks with his toes pointed; she also reports a delay in speech and language. She states that he had many ear infections throughout childhood. He presents with episodes of watery stools several times a day. Mother notes that he gets cold easily, with a low body temperature. Sleeps poorly, with a significantly altered sleep pattern.

Past Medical History: Delivery with shoulder dystocia. Cryptorchidism. Mother denies imperforate lip. Echocardiogram without ventricular septal defect and without atrial septal defect type ostium secundum.

Physical Exam: elongated face, oblique palpebral fissures directed downwards, inverted nostrils, long philtrum. No strabismus. Hands and feet with short fingers; widened hallux. Absence of syndactyly.

findings.text: head circumference within the normal range for age and sex

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years old, accompanied by the mother.

Chief complaint: referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

History of present illness: mother reports that he was significantly delayed in speaking, with the first words and phrases well after the expected time. He has a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder since childhood. In school, the teacher observed that he did not stay quiet, became distracted by anything, and acted impulsively; he was diagnosed with ADHD. He presents with intellectual disability, requiring support with daily activities. The mother reports that he has always been smaller than other children of the same age and has grown slowly. He sat and walked at the appropriate age, without motor delay. Denies seizures. Does not present with aggressive behavior. Sleeps well, without sleep disturbances.

Physical exam: head circumference within the normal range for age and sex, without microcephaly.

findings.text: height below the 3rd percentile for age and sex

absent: different behaviors, such as agitation or isolation
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “He doesn’t grow and he was late to speak.”

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child started speaking much later than other children and still speaks little for his age. He also delayed sitting and walking. She reports that from infancy he grows slowly, always being smaller than his peers. She also reports that feeding has always been a problem: he has difficulty chewing and swallowing, and meals are prolonged. Denies different behaviors, such as agitation or isolation. Previous evaluation did not identify intellectual disability.

Physical Exam: Height below the 3rd percentile for age and sex. Low weight. Head circumference is appropriate, without microcephaly. Facial shape deformity.

findings.text: aortic arch without ventricular septal defect
right lung with only two lobes
no agenesis of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by the parents for evaluation in a medical genetics clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for multiple malformations.

History of present illness: The parents report that at birth he had extra fingers on his hands and feet. He was identified shortly after birth that the baby had no anal opening. An echocardiogram showed the aortic arch, without ventricular septal defect. Chest X-ray showed the right lung with only two lobes. Cranial MRI showed no agenesis of the corpus callosum. Radiograph of lower extremities showed no short femur.

Physical exam: Head circumference without macrocephaly. Forehead without broadening. Eyebrows joined along the midline. Eyes well apart. Ears with low insertion. Small and retracted chin. Palatine cleft. Hands with preaxial polydacty and mesoaxial polydacty. Feet with duplication of the hallux and mesoaxial polydacty.

findings.text: muscle atrophy of the skeletal musculature
tone is preserved in the limbs
lips with vermilion of usual thickness

translation:
Identification: female adolescent, 15 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred by neurology for investigation.

History of present illness: mother reports that since early childhood, the daughter delayed sitting, walking, and interacting, with delays in all areas of development. She never spoke any words. She also reports episodes of seizures. She states that the daughter has moments when she hits people, screams, and breaks objects in the house. She has a previous evaluation with a diagnosis of intellectual disability.

Physical exam: muscle atrophy of the skeletal musculature. Tone is preserved in the limbs, without appendicular hypotonia. Lips with vermilion of usual thickness, without thin lip. Palate without elongation. Ears with normal impaction, not low. Nose without prominence.

Identification: Woman, 40 years old, referred to the neurophthalmology clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "My vision is getting worse."

History of Present Illness: Patient reports seeing well and that, over time, she noticed a loss of vision. She reports a dark spot in the center of her visual field, which interferes when she fixes her gaze on something. She also reports difficulty differentiating colors. She complains of frequent headaches. She further reports that she has been hearing worse, and she has already performed an audiometry, which showed sensorineural hearing loss.

Physical Exam: Visual acuity without reduction on this evaluation. Fundoscopy: optic atrophy; paleness of the temporal disc.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
spine with abnormal curvature in the lateral and anteroposterior planes (scoliosis and kyphosis)
complete absence of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: boy, 4 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: mother reports that the child delayed significantly in supporting his head and sitting, and to date he does not walk independently. He does not speak any words, only emits sounds. He presents with episodes of seizures. He is functionally completely dependent on caregivers, with severe intellectual disability.

History: In the first year of life, he began to be fed via gastrostomy. Currently he needs parenteral nutrition, as he cannot receive enough either orally or via a tube. Prior echocardiogram showed an open oval foramen, without interventricular communication and without pulmonary stenosis.

Physical exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Height below the 3rd percentile. Global hypotonia. Spine with abnormal curvature in the lateral and anteroposterior planes (scoliosis and kyphosis). Hip dislocation. Knee dislocation.

Complementary exams: Brain MRI with complete absence of the corpus callosum, not being just a sharp corpus callosum. Lateral ventricles are enlarged, without signs of hydrocephalus. There is no agenesis.

findings.text: sperm concentration within the expected range
significant reduction in the fraction that moves forward in a straight line
many sperm are observed with short tails
others with the tail coiled around itself
no bent flagella at an angle

translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by andrology.

Chief complaint: unable to have children.

History of present illness: patient reports attempting to conceive his partner for several years without success, and was investigated with a diagnosis of male infertility. He brings spermograms for evaluation.

Additional examinations: spermogram with sperm concentration within the expected range, without oligozoospermia. The sperm exhibit generally low motility, with a significant reduction in the fraction that moves forward in a straight line. In the morphological analysis, many sperm are observed with short tails and others with the tail coiled around itself. No sperm without tails, nor bent flagella at an angle were seen.

findings.text: delayed enhancement demonstrating fibrosis in the left atrium

translation:
Identification: Woman, 48 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology for evaluation.

Chief complaint: Referral for atrial arrhythmia.

History of present illness: Patient reports feeling her heart beating irregularly and out of sync. Electrocardiogram brought by the patient shows atrial fibrillation, without atrial flutter recorded on the available tracings.

Past medical history: Hypertensive for years, under clinical follow-up.

Physical examination: Irregular heart rate on auscultation.

Complementary examinations: Echocardiogram with enlarged left atrium and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging with delayed enhancement demonstrating fibrosis in the left atrium. BNP elevated. NT-proANP below the lower limit of normal.

findings.text: sharp fingers directed towards the tips

translation:
Identification: male patient, 25 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for investigation of developmental delay since childhood.

History of present illness: The mother reports that he was very late to sit, crawl, and walk, and also to pick up small objects with his fingers and hold utensils. She states that his first words came very late and that his speech was always significantly delayed compared to other children. He refers to a global delay in development during the first years of life. He describes episodes of sudden, rapid muscle jerks, like frights, causing his arms to jump. Denies diagnosis of hypothyroidism.

Past medical history: Mother denies excessive amniotic fluid during pregnancy. No astigmatism.

Physical examination: Microcephaly. Permanently open mouth, without a narrow mouth and without downturned labial commissures. Short palate. Micrognathia. Pointed chin. Sharp fingers directed towards the tips. Short feet. Axial hypotonia. Spasticity.

Identification: girl, 3 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: mother reports that the daughter is delayed in all areas of development compared to other children of the same age. She reports that it took a long time for her to sit, crawl, and walk. She also refers to the fact that she speaks very few words and does not form sentences. She also noticed that one of the girl’s eyes “turns inward.”

Past medical history: echocardiogram without persistence of arterial duct. Spinal resonance without syrinomielia.

Physical examination: oblique palpebral fissures upwards. Low nasal bridge. Small mouth with downturned corners. Short chin, without retrognathia. Normal sized uvula, not elongated. Esotropia on eye exam. Global hypotonia. No hypermobility of joints.

Identification: Female patient, 11 years and 6 months old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatric endocrinology.

Chief complaint: Evaluation of ovarian development alteration.

History of present illness: Mother reports that the daughter had her first menstruation later than expected, characterizing delayed menarche. She does not present with primary amenorrhea.

Additional examinations: Pelvic ultrasound demonstrating ovarian aplasia. Hormonal assays with elevated FSH, elevated LH, and reduced Müllerian inhibiting hormone.

findings.text: high anterior implantation of the hair

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by his parents for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for investigation of hair changes and imaging exam.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the patient’s hair breaks very easily, even when combing. She also noted that he has few eyelashes and that his eyebrows are thin.

Physical exam: coarse facies. Full cheeks. Narrow and high forehead, with high anterior implantation of the hair.

Complementary exams: cranial MRI showing cerebellar atrophy and a pointed corpus callosum.

findings.text: without any particular findings to record on this consultation

translation:
Identification: woman, 34 years old, referred by the assisted reproductive clinic for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: "I can't get pregnant."

History of present illness: Patient reports attempting to conceive for several years without success, with an infertility diagnosis made by the human reproductive team. She has undergone several IVF cycles in which the transferred embryos, described as of good quality, never implanted. According to the clinic reports, in the IVF/ICSI cycles, the oocytes retrieved did not complete maturation, remaining blocked in an immature stage, which rendered attempts with these oocytes unsuccessful.

Physical exam: without any particular findings to record on this consultation.

findings.text: limitation of the passive range of motion of the hips
limitation of the passive range of motion of the shoulders
increased space between the hallux and the second toe

translation:
Identification: girl, 13 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter was delayed in sitting, walking, and interacting when young, lagging behind other children in everything. She began to speak her first words and phrases much later than expected. Today she attends school with great difficulty, with an intellectual disability diagnosed in a neuropsychological evaluation. The mother states that her speech is slurred and difficult to understand by those who do not live with her. Denies rapid, involuntary muscle jerks. She wears glasses for astigmatism.

Physical Exam: Head circumference above the 97th percentile. Ears of normal impaction. Palpebral fissures without downward slant. Nose tip without prominence. Global muscle hypotonia. Limitation of the passive range of motion of the hips and shoulders. On the feet, increased space between the hallux and the second toe.

Complementary Examinations: EEG with abnormal tracing. Brain MRI without hypomyelination.

findings.text: palor of the temporal sector of the optic disc bilaterally
area of macular atrophy in both eyes

translation:
Identification: female patient, 39 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by ophthalmology for evaluation.

Chief complaint: referred due to finding in the fundus examination.

History of present illness: patient reports seeing well, without noticing worsening of vision distance or near. Denies spots or defects in the center of vision when fixing gaze on objects.

Physical examination: visual acuity preserved in both eyes. Fundoscopy: palor of the temporal sector of the optic disc bilaterally; area of macular atrophy in both eyes.

Complementary examinations: autofluorescence of the fundus shows hypoautofluorescent lesions in the retina. Previous ophthalmological evaluation describes macular dystrophy.

findings.text: nose of normal length, with bulbous nose
enlarged tongue, occupying the entire oral cavity

translation:
Identification: male, 15 years and 11 months, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for investigation of developmental abnormalities.

History of present illness: The mother reports that he was very slow to say his first words and form sentences. She also reports that he had difficulty holding small objects, buttoning clothes, and using utensils, achieving this much later than his siblings. He has a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder. The mother denies episodes of esophagitis.

Past medical history: During the neonatal period, patent arterial duct persistence was identified.

Physical examination: Head circumference without macrocephaly. Wide forehead. Midface hypoplasia. Nose of normal length, with bulbous nose. Superior lip with thin vermillion. Normal width mouth. Enlarged tongue, occupying the entire oral cavity. Large earlobes; without pre-auricular appendages. Excessive hairiness throughout the body. Digital clubbing. Bunion valgus.

findings.text: sperm concentration within the reference range
spermatozoa with more than one flagellum inserted into the head

translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by urology.

Chief complaint: difficulty in having children.

History of present illness: patient reports that, together with his partner, he has been trying to conceive for some time, without success; he was evaluated by urology and received a diagnosis of male infertility. He brings a spermogram for evaluation.

Complementary examinations: spermogram with sperm concentration within the reference range, without oligozoospermia. Asthenozoospermia, with decreased progressive motility. On morphological analysis, spermatozoa with absent flagella, short flagella, flagella coiled around themselves, and spermatozoa with more than one flagellum inserted into the head are observed.

findings.text: alteration in the morphology of the corpus callosum

translation:
Identification: woman, 34 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of changes in cranial magnetic resonance imaging.

Chief complaint: recurrent headache.

History of present illness: patient reports long-standing, episodic migraine headaches. Denies seizure crises. Denies episodes of loss of consciousness. Attendant reports no change in behavior. Denies difficulty walking.

Physical exam: gait without alterations.

Complementary examinations: Cranial MRI shows cerebral atrophy, alteration in the morphology of the corpus callosum, alteration of the pallidum and alteration of the cerebellar peduncles. Diffusion sequence without changes.

findings.text: episodes in salvos of sudden contractions, with trunk flexion and arm elevation
focal seizures with impairment of consciousness

absent: generalized shaking of the four limbs
translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by the parents, referred to the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of epileptic seizures.

Chief complaint: seizures and developmental delay.

History of present illness: The parents report that, still in the first year of life, the child began to present with episodes in salvos of sudden contractions, with trunk flexion and arm elevation, repeated several times in succession. Subsequently, episodes emerged in which the boy stands still, with a fixed gaze, unresponsive when called and without remembering the occurrence afterward, described as focal seizures with impairment of consciousness. The parents deny that these seizures evolve into generalized shaking of the four limbs. They deny seizures triggered by fever. There has never been a prolonged episode of non-motor seizure, without non-convulsive status epilepticus.

Past medical history: The mother noticed that he delayed in supporting his head, sitting, babbling, and interacting with people, lagging behind other children of the same age in all areas.

Physical exam: Child in good general condition, without other abnormalities to record on this consultation.

findings.text: increased absolute number of B lymphocytes
reduced proportion of memory B cells
reduced number of memory effector CD4+ T cells
reduced number of memory effector CD8+ T cells
absence of antibody response to tetanus vaccine
persistently positive PCR for EBV in blood

translation:
Identification: girl, 8 years old, brought by her mother, referred to the immunology/genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: fever and recurrent infections.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter has frequent episodes of sore throat, ear pain, and sinusitis since childhood, requiring multiple consultations per year. She has had fever for weeks.

Physical examination: Liver and spleen were enlarged upon palpation of the abdomen.

Complementary examinations: Complete blood count with anemia, leukocytosis, and lymphopenia; no lymphocytosis; platelet count normal. Elevated LDH. Bilirubin within the normal range. Immunophenotyping: increased absolute number of B lymphocytes, reduced proportion of memory B cells, reduced number of memory effector CD4+ T cells, and reduced number of memory effector CD8+ T cells. Absence of antibody response to tetanus vaccine. PCR for EBV in blood persistently positive in serial measurements.

findings.text: atrophy of the distal musculature of the upper extremities
atrophy of the distal musculature of the lower extremities

absent: tremor when performing movements or holding objects
translation:
Identification: woman, 45 years old, referred to the neurology genetics clinic.

Chief complaint: difficulty walking since childhood.

History of present illness: The patient reports that she started walking later than her siblings and that she has always walked on the tips of her feet. She reports that over the years her legs have become increasingly rigid and that today she stumbles because she cannot raise her feet. She has also noticed that her hands have become thinner and weaker, with difficulty buttoning clothes. Denies urgency to urinate. Denies tremor when performing movements or holding objects.

Past medical history: Educational level and professional life without learning difficulties; without intellectual disability.

Physical examination: Spastic gait. Spasticity in the lower extremities. Hyperreflexia, with ankle reflexes abolished bilaterally. Babinski sign present. Atrophy of the distal musculature of the upper extremities and the lower extremities. Reduced strength in the distal musculature of the upper extremities and the lower extremities, with dorsiflexor paresis of the feet. Flat feet, without cavus foot, and hammer toes. Spine without hyperlordosis.

Complementary examinations: Electroneuromyography showing axonal motor neuropathy.

findings.text: structural alterations of the head of the spermatozoa
reduced progressive motility of the spermatozoa

translation:
Identification: male patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by urology.

Chief complaint: the couple is unable to conceive.

History of present illness: patient reports attempts at conception with his partner, without success, which is why he was investigated and received the diagnosis of male infertility. He brings a spermogram for evaluation.

Complementary examinations: spermogram showing sperm concentration below 20 million/mL, head of the spermatozoa with structural alterations and reduced progressive motility.

Management: continues in outpatient follow-up.

findings.text: reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes

translation:
Identification: girl, 12 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: fevers that come and go.

History of present illness: mother reports repeated episodes of fever over the years. She also reports episodic vomiting crises, with periods without symptoms between them, and on some of these occasions the girl became dehydrated. She states that the girl becomes very sleepy, with difficulty staying awake. She has already presented with seizure crises.

Past medical history: surgical correction of inguinal hernia. Mother reports hepatic alteration already identified in previous follow-up. No global delay in development in the first years of life.

Physical exam: intact palate, without cleft palate.

Complementary tests: anemia. Elevated PCR. Low serum IgG. Immunophenotyping with a reduced percentage of CD4+ T lymphocytes and an inverted CD4/CD8 ratio. Brain MRI with pineal cyst.

Identification: male, 52 years old, referred to the pneumology/genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

Chief complaint: long-standing respiratory problems.

History of present illness: patient reports that for many years he has lived with a stuffy nose, nasal secretion, and a feeling of facial pressure that never completely resolves, with periodic worsening. He reports having been operated on in the past for removal of “growing flesh” inside the nose.

Physical examination: anterior rhinoscopy reveals bilateral nasal polyposis.

Complementary examinations: Chest CT with bronchiectasis. Facial sinus CT with findings of chronic sinusitis. Nasal nitric oxide dosage is reduced. Echocardiogram without alteration in the spatial arrangement of the cardiac segments.

findings.text: increased variability of muscle fiber caliber

translation:
Identification: girl, 11 years and 6 months, brought by her mother, referred to the pediatric neurology clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter gets very tired quickly during playtime and physical education, needing to stop before her peers. Denies muscle pain. No difficulty with feeding, chewing, or swallowing.

Physical Exam: Percussion of the muscles with a reflex hammer, no persistent localized bulging of the muscle is observed, nor rolling contractions along the muscle belly.

Complementary Examinations: Elevated serum CK. AST within the normal range. Muscle biopsy brought by the family: increased variability of muscle fiber caliber.

findings.text: diffuse scaling of ichthyotic appearance in the limbs and trunk
telangiectasias in the malar and nasal regions

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "dry skin and itching since always".

History of present illness: Patient reports that since childhood he has had red and very itchy plaques in the folds of his arms and behind his knees, which worsen and improve throughout the year. He also reports that his skin all over his body is very flaky, with dry scales, mainly in his legs. He states that he has lived with a stuffy nose and running, for years, without lasting improvement. He has noticed that he hears poorly, needing to increase the volume of the television.

Past medical history: Asthma since childhood. Hyperthyroidism on follow-up with endocrinology.

Physical examination: Good general condition. Skin with diffuse scaling of ichthyotic appearance in the limbs and trunk; eczema in antecubital fossae and popliteal fossae. Telangiectasias in the malar and nasal regions.

Complementary examinations: Audiometry brought by the patient shows sensorineural hearing loss.

findings.text: cutaneous crease covering the inner canthus bilaterally

translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “developmental delay”.

History of present illness: mother reports that the child has always been slower than other children in all developmental stages. She states that he took a very long time to start walking alone. She also refers that he struggled to speak and still uses few words to ask for what he wants, although he appears to understand what is said to him. Since childhood, the family has noticed that one of the eyes “goes out of alignment”.

Complementary exams: Brain MRI brought by the family shows delayed myelination, without vermis cerebellar atrophy. Echocardiogram without patent foramen ovale.

Physical exam: Cutaneous crease covering the inner canthus bilaterally. Low implantation of ears. Palpebral fissures without upward slant. Eyebrows without accentuated arch. Nostrils not anteverted. Esotropia. Hypotonia. Deep reflexes exaggerated.

findings.text: triangular face, wider in the temples and tapering towards the chin
fingers of the hands long and thin

translation:
Identification: boy, 5 years old, brought by the mother, referred by the pediatrician for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: developmental delay.

History of present illness: mother reports that the child has always been slower than other children to sit, walk, and play, presenting with global neuropsychomotor developmental delay. She refers that he started to speak very late and still speaks few words, much less than his peers the same age. She also reports that he frequently swings his hands repeatedly, mainly when he is excited.

Physical exam: height appropriate for age, without short stature. Triangular face, wider in the temples and tapering towards the chin. Deep-set eyes. Lips with thin vermillion. No retrognathia. Ears without posterior rotation. Fingers of the hands long and thin. Feet flat on orthostatism.

Complementary exams: Cranial MRI without septum pellucid cavum and without schizencephaly.

findings.text: tremor in his hands when they are at rest
decreases when he picks up objects
difficulty with reasoning and problem-solving in daily life
involuntary twisting movements of the body
push test with retraction, requiring support by the examiner

translation:
Identification: Male, 74 years old, referred to neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation of movement disorder. Comes accompanied by his wife.

History of Present Illness: The wife reports that he presents with tremor in his hands when they are at rest, supported on his lap, which decreases when he picks up objects. He reports frequent falls at home. She notes that his handwriting has been getting smaller and smaller when he writes. The family has noticed that he is more forgetful and has difficulty with reasoning and problem-solving in daily life. Parkinsonian syndrome with good response to dopamine therapy, according to report from the originating service. The wife also describes involuntary twisting movements of the body throughout the day.

Past Medical History: Gastric ulcer. Neoplasm under follow-up.

Physical Exam: Push test with retraction, requiring support by the examiner.

findings.text: spastic hypertonia in the lower extremities
misses the target on the index-nose test
slowness and irregularity when alternating pronation and supination of the hands rapidly

translation:
Identification: woman, 32 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: difficulty walking.

History of present illness: patient reports that she has been walking worse and worse, stumbling and needing support. She also reports difficulty standing upright for long periods and feeling weak legs. She complains of problems controlling her bladder. Denies memory loss or cognitive decline; family confirms that she continues to work and organize normally. Denies weakness in the arms.

Past medical history: denies chronic liver disease, with report of prior evaluation without cirrhosis.

Physical examination: nystagmus with lateral gaze. Picture of spastic ataxia. Spastic hypertonia in the lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are brisk globally. Babinski sign is present. Lower extremity paresis, with preserved strength in the upper extremities. On the index-nose test, misses the target, passing beyond the point. Slowness and irregularity when alternating pronation and supination of the hands rapidly. Muscle wasting is preserved, without amyotrophy.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI brought by the patient without cerebellar atrophy.

Identification: Female patient, 22 years old, accompanied by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that in early childhood the daughter was delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting, lagging behind other children in everything. She also reports that after acquiring some skills, the daughter lost abilities she had already acquired. Currently, she presents with intellectual disability. During adolescence, she began to present with a psychotic picture, accompanied by psychiatry. The family reports that she has episodes in which she screams, curses, and hits people and breaks objects, and that she often bites and scratches herself until she hurts herself. The mother denies that she is excessively nervous or worried. They also note that she hears poorly and does not respond when called from a distance.

Past Medical History: Gastroesophageal reflux disease. The mother reports that for years she has had few bowel movements per week, with hard stools and a lot of effort. Hyperopia under ophthalmological follow-up. Denies cardiovascular disease, without interventricular communication.

Physical Exam: Obesity. Esotropia on ocular examination. Muscle tone preserved, without hypotonia. Spine without kyphosis. Feet with plantar arch preserved, without flatfoot.

findings.text: extensive, wide, violaceous striae in the abdomen and flanks
