primary micronodular pigmented nodular adrenal disease

translation:
Identification: male, 23 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "shortness of breath and fatigue".

History of present illness: Patient reports shortness of breath and is unable to keep up with his peers in physical activities, becoming very tired before expected. The mother noticed that his face became quite round and swollen, that his abdomen grew quite a bit, and that there was an accumulation of fat in his neck. She also noted dark spots on his lips.

Physical examination: Thin, translucent skin with visible veins through transparency. Extensive, wide, violaceous striae in the abdomen and flanks.

Complementary examinations: Elevated serum cortisol. Increased free cortisol in urine. Suppressed plasma ACTH. Echocardiogram with cardiac myxoma. Anatomopathological examination of the adrenal glands revealed primary micronodular pigmented nodular adrenal disease.

Identification: woman, 33 years old, referred by hematology to the outpatient genetics clinic.

Chief complaint: evaluation of hematological abnormalities.

History of present illness: patient reports follow-up for pancytopenia in serial hemograms, with thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and macrocytic anemia. Bone marrow aspiration and bone marrow biopsy revealed hypocellular bone marrow and dyserythropoiesis. Denies hearing loss. Denies any diagnosed tumor to date.

Physical examination: height within the expected range for age and sex. Face with malar hypoplasia, short chin, and small mandible. Palate with submucosal cleft observed and palpated. Hands with short fifth finger bilaterally and clinodactyly of the fifth finger. Nipples without increased webbing. Perineal region without fistula.

findings.text: visual acuity with mild reduction, between 20/40 and 20/70
perception that he sees well only what is directly in front of him, ‘as if he were looking through a tube’

absent: diagnosis of autism or suggestive behaviors
translation:
Identification: male patient, referred by ophthalmology for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: difficulty seeing at night.

History of present illness: The patient reports poor vision in dark environments or with low light, frequently stumbling in the evening. He also reports bumping into objects located nearby, perceiving that he sees well only what is directly in front of him, “as if he were looking through a tube.” Previous ophthalmological evaluation concluded with rod and cone dystrophy.

History: Denies seizures. Family denies diagnosis of autism or suggestive behaviors.

Physical exam: No obesity. No hemiplegia on the right.

Complementary exams: Visual acuity with mild reduction, between 20/40 and 20/70.

Identification: Female patient, 29 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by the assisted reproductive technology clinic.

Chief complaint: "I can't get pregnant."

History of Present Illness: Patient reports infertility, for which she has undergone in vitro fertilization cycles. According to the assisted reproductive technology clinic report, in some of the cycles the embryos stopped dividing before reaching the appropriate stage for transfer. In the cycles in which good quality embryos were transferred, implantation did not occur, a situation repeated after several attempts.

Management: Follow-up in the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

findings.text: muscle strength diminished in all four limbs

translation:
Identification: woman, 34 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: fatigue and weakness.

History of present illness: reports persistent fatigue for years, with lack of energy that does not improve with rest. Reports difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair, as well as weakness in the arms and legs. Reports recurrent infections, having been previously followed for immunodeficiency. Denies seizures.

History: Previous cardiology evaluation without cardiomiopathy.

Physical examination: high palate. Drooping eyelids bilaterally. Ophthalmic neuropathy. Muscle strength diminished in all four limbs, with predominant proximal weakness. Deep tendon reflexes abolished globally.

Complementary examinations: CK elevated. Triglycerides normal. Transaminases normal. Electroneuromyography without peripheral neuropathy. Muscle biopsy with ragged red fibers on trichrome Gomori stain, increased fiber diameter variation and COX-negative fibers; biochemical study showed deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes. Mitochondrial DNA analysis revealed multiple deletions.

findings.text: height above the 97th percentile for age and sex

translation:
Identification: boy, 8 years and 9 months, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

History of Present Illness: Mother reports that the child was a little later than other children to sit, walk, and acquire the other developmental stages, with a mild delay. He started speaking late and still has vocabulary and sentences below the expected level for his age. At school, he follows along with difficulty; neuropsychological evaluation concluded mild intellectual disability. He has a diagnosis of ADHD made by neuropediatria. The mother reports that he sleeps poorly, wakes up several times during the night, and has restless sleep. Denies hearing loss; the family refers that he hears well.

Physical Exam: Height above the 97th percentile for age and sex. No hypertelorism. Ear pavilions of normal size, without macrotia. Does not present esotropia. Feet with preserved plantar arch, without flat foot.

Complementary Examinations: Ophthalmological evaluation with hyperopia. Altered EEG.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex
instability when attempting to reach objects

translation:
Identification: boy, 1 year of age, brought by the mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Presenting Illness: The mother reports that the child is slightly delayed compared to other children of the same age in sitting, crawling, and interacting, although she considers the delay to be subtle. She also reports that he has not yet said any words and almost does not babble. She has also noted that his eyes “shake” from side to side, continuously.

Physical Exam: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Low-set ears and enlarged ears. Prominent nose, without increased nasal length. Oblique palpebral fissures upwards. Absence of bi-temporal depression. Nystagmus present; no exotropia. Voluntary movements are uncoordinated, with instability when attempting to reach objects, characterizing ataxia. Presence of bulbous signs. Muscle tone preserved, without hypotonia.

Complementary Examinations: Hepatic transaminases without elevation.

findings.text: inability to bend and stretch some joints
reduced range of motion in the joints

translation:
Identification: Male, 39 years and 6 months, presents alone, referred from orthopedics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: Joint pain.

History of present illness: Patient reports joint pain for several years, primarily in the evenings. He refers to having swollen joints sometimes. He also notes that he is unable to bend and stretch some joints as before. He states that family members comment that he is “rebolando,” swaying the hips from side to side.

Past medical history: Always the shortest among his peers. Denies having had a slipped capital femoral epiphysis beyond the expected in childhood.

Physical exam: Short stature. Anserine gait. Reduced range of motion in the joints. Spine without kyphosis. Lower extremities without genu varum and without genu valgum.

Complementary exams: Bone densitometry demonstrating decreased bone mineral density.

findings.text: diminished vibratory sensation in distal extremities

translation:
Identification: male, 47 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: difficulty with walking.

History of present illness: Patient reports difficulty with walking. Denies weakness in the legs.

Physical exam: Spastic paraplegia. Patellar reflexes are brisk bilaterally. Achilles reflexes are brisk. No ankle clonus. No patellar clonus. Babinski sign is present. Hoffmann sign is present. Vibratory sensation diminished in distal extremities.

Complementary exams: Electroneuromyography shows reduced motor conduction velocity, reduced sensory conduction velocity, and motor conduction block.

findings.text: dry skin with red plaques and intense itching in the axillary and knee folds
reactions after ingesting certain foods, such as milk and egg
diarrheal complaint with mucus and blood

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought in by parents, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “delay in development and many allergies”.

History of Present Illness: The parents report that he was delayed in sitting, walking, speaking, and interacting with other children. From an early age, he has dry skin with red plaques and intense itching in the axillary and knee folds, which thicken over time. He presents with reactions after ingesting certain foods, such as milk and egg. He reports recurrent episodes of pneumonia and bronchitis over the years, as well as recurrent mycoses. He has a diarrheal complaint with mucus and blood, having undergone a colonoscopy that revealed colitis, and the biopsy showed an eosinophilic infiltrate in the colon. The parents deny seizure crises. He denies recurrent skin infections.

Past Medical History: Pregnancy with intrauterine growth restriction. At birth, head circumference below -2 SD. Followed by ophthalmology for high myopia.

Physical Exam: Microcephaly. Marked thoracic kyphosis. Anoperineal fistula. Uvula without bifidity.

Complementary Examinations: Complete blood count with eosinophilia. Elevated serum IgE with a monoclonal band on electrophoresis. Serum IgA without reduction. Echocardiogram without structural cardiac abnormalities.

findings.text: multiple cutaneous warts in the neck
multiple cutaneous warts in the trunk
multiple cutaneous warts in the arms
multiple cutaneous warts in the legs
extensive and atypical molluscum contagiosum with hundreds of umbilicated papules
reduced absolute number of CD3+ T lymphocytes
decreased percentage of CD8+ among the T cells
proportional reduction of naive CD4+ and naive CD8+

translation:
Identification: male, 24 years old, referred to the outpatient immunology clinic for investigation.

Chief complaint: recurrent skin lesions.

History of present illness: patient reports erythematous, scaling plaques with intense itching in the folds of elbows and knees for a long time. He also reports warts scattered over the neck, trunk, arms, and legs. Denies decreased sweating. Brought in with a previous diagnosis of combined immunodeficiency, previously followed with autoimmune thrombocytopenia.

Physical exam: erythematodescalative plaques in flexural regions. Multiple cutaneous warts in the neck, trunk, and limbs. Extensive and atypical molluscum contagiosum with hundreds of umbilicated papules. Hair of normal thickness and texture, not thin.

Complementary tests: lymphopenia. Reduced absolute number of CD3+ T lymphocytes. Decreased percentage of CD8+ among the T cells. Proportional reduction of naive CD4+ and naive CD8+. Reduced proliferative response to phytohemagglutinin. Oligoclonal TCR repertoire. Low TRECs. Eosinophils within the normal range. Normal IgA and IgG serum levels.

findings.text: thin hair, very curly, in tightly closed curls, with a woolly appearance
right testicle not palpable in the scrotum

translation:
Identification: boy, 7 years and 11 months, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: delay in development and school difficulties.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that since infancy, he delayed in reaching developmental milestones in all areas. He walked alone much later than his siblings. He began to speak late and to this day his speech is poor for his age. He reports frequent episodes in which the child is very distressed, restless, and struggles, reaching to hit people and himself. School psychological evaluation indicated mild intellectual disability. Mother denies episodes with loss of contact or staring and automatisms. He interacts well with other children, maintains eye contact, and does not present with repetitive behaviors or restricted interests.

Physical Exam: Head circumference appropriate for age, without microcephaly. Height within the expected range, without short stature. Thin hair, very curly, in tightly closed curls, with a woolly appearance. Cardiac auscultation without murmurs; prior echocardiogram without ventricular septal defect. Genitalia: right testicle not palpable in the scrotum, left testicle atopic.

Complementary Examinations: Brain MRI revealed absence of the olfactory bulb.

findings.text: no intention tremor on the finger-nose test

translation:
Identification: male, 19 years old, accompanied by the mother, referred to medical genetics for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that since birth the head was small, with a head circumference below the expected value at birth. In the first years there was a global delay in development; it took a long time to sit and walk, and speech also came very late. He has always been a “floppy” baby. He presents with episodes in which he is still, with a vacant stare, without responding to what happens around him. He has significant difficulty thinking, reasoning, and remembering things, and depends on others for daily activities, with severe intellectual disability. The mother also noted from an early age that the eyes “do not align”.

Physical Exam: Face with atypical shape. Small jaw. Esotropia. Nystagmus horizontal. Dysmetric saccadic movements. Axial hypotonia. Spasticity in the lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are exaggerated. No intention tremor on the finger-nose test. Speech without dysarthria. There is no hypermobility of the joints. Nails without dysplasia.

Complementary Examinations: Fundoscopy without optic nerve hypoplasia.

findings.text: angular deviation of fingers at the level of the interphalangeal joint

translation:
Identification: male patient, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred by pediatric cardiology for investigation.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the child frequently “catches a cold that goes down to the chest,” with several episodes of respiratory infection throughout the year. He has a diagnosis of asthma under follow-up. Prior bronchoscopy described bronchomalacia. He is being followed for hypertension, already confirmed in multiple consultations.

Past medical history: echocardiogram and angiography show an inter ventricular communication, abnormal pulmonary venous drainage, and double superior caval vein (right and left). Heart in normal position in the left hemithorax, without dextrocardia. There is no transposition of the great arteries, the left ventricle has preserved dimensions, without hypoplasia, the pulmonary valve is patent, without atresia, and the coronary sinus is not dilated. Abdominal imaging showed abdominal organs without defined laterality, with multiple small spleens, in addition to significant dilation of the pelvis and renal calyces.

Physical exam: ears with posterior rotation. Chest with sternal depression. Angular deviation of fingers at the level of the interphalangeal joint.

Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by the mother, referred by pediatrics for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: cognitive delay and difficulty with speech.

History of present illness: Mother reports that the child has intellectual disability, accompanied in school with pedagogical support. She refers that he presents seizures since childhood. He states that he knows what he wants to say, but he cannot coordinate his mouth to form the words, making more errors the longer the word or phrase. She also observes that he bites his lips and hits his head against the wall when frustrated. Denies sudden fits of laughter without reason. Denies that he has difficulty hearing.

Physical exam: Head of disproportionately large appearance in relation to the body, with head circumference within 2 standard deviations. Slow and uncoordinated voluntary movements. Muscle tone without hypotonia and without hypertonia. No convergent eye deviation.

findings.text: muscles of the lower extremities without increased volume

translation:
Identification: Woman, 45 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

Chief complaint: Previous episode of muscle destruction.

History of Present Illness: Patient reports that during a viral infection, she presented with rhabdomyolysis triggered by the viral infection, with intense muscle pain throughout her body. She reports that during this period she noticed dark urine, cola-colored, and the team that attended her documented myoglobinuria. The hospitalization recorded acute rhabdomyolysis complicated by acute renal injury.

Physical exam: Muscles of the lower extremities without increased volume. Upper extremities without muscular hypertrophy.

Identification: girl, 7 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred by the pediatrician for investigation of development.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the daughter took longer than other children to start walking independently. She refers that, in general, the girl has always been a little slower to acquire the expected skills for her age, with mild global developmental delay. The mother also noticed that “one of the eyes sometimes drifts”. She denies that the child acts without thinking or in a disinhibited manner; she describes her as capable of waiting and following instructions. She denies heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding. She denies any tumors diagnosed to date.

Physical examination: strabismus on eye examination. Deep-set eyes, convergent in the face. Forehead of normal size, without a prominent brow. Eyebrows without elongated lashes.

findings.text: atrophy of the pigment epithelium of the retina
pigmentation in bone spicules in the peripheral retina
concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field

translation:
Identification: male patient, 69 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for ophthalmological evaluation.

Chief complaint: difficulty seeing at night.

History of present illness: the patient reports that he cannot see well at night or in poorly lit environments. He also reports bumping into objects next to him, perceiving that his visual field has been narrowing at the edges.

History: denies high myopia.

Physical examination: slightly reduced visual acuity, approximately 20/50 in both eyes. Fundoscopy: pale optic disc, atrophy of the pigment epithelium of the retina, and pigmentation in bone spicules in the peripheral retina.

Complementary examinations: perimetry with concentric constriction of the peripheral visual field, without annular scotoma.

findings.text: testicles of reduced volume on palpation
IGF-1 below the lower limit of normal

translation:
Identification: male, 32 years and 8 months, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that during gestation, she was informed that the baby was small for gestational age with restricted growth in utero. After birth, she noticed that he grew slowly, always smaller than other children. She also reports that the head was becoming small over the years, although at birth it appeared of adequate size. The patient presents with seizure crises. He completed his studies without specific difficulties of reading, writing, or attention; there is no intellectual deficit.

Physical Exam: Short stature. Microcephaly. Scrotum in bag of retention. Testicles of reduced volume on palpation. No café-au-lait spots. Columella without low insertion.

Complementary Exams: Anemia. Elevated TSH, with free T4 not reduced. IGF-1 below the lower limit of normal.

findings.text: short stature for age and sex
absence of signs of pubertal development

translation:
Identification: boy, 15 years old, brought by his mother to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

History of Present Illness: Mother reports significant delay in all developmental stages since the first year of life. Only began walking alone well after her siblings. Never spoke any words. Always had difficulty feeding, taking very long meals and having difficulty chewing and swallowing. Does not interact with other people, does not seek contact and remains fixed in the same activities and routines. He swings his hands and trunk repeatedly, apparently without purpose. Presents with generalized onset epileptic crises and also focal onset crises, with an episode of status epilepticus. Mother denies episodes of epileptic spasms. Has a previously diagnosed intellectual disability.

Physical Exam: Short stature for age and sex. Absence of signs of pubertal development, characterizing delayed puberty for age. Global hypotonia. Gait with widened base.

Complementary Examinations: Brain MRI reveals a septum pellucidum cavum. No cerebral atrophy, adequate myelination, subarachnoid space without widening and cerebellar body of normal thickness.

Identification: female patient, brought in by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter always took longer than other children to sit, walk, speak, and use her hands. She also reports that at one point, the girl stopped doing things she had already known, losing acquired skills. She presents with episodes of seizures. In the neuropsychological evaluation, intellectual disability was identified. Mother denies food intolerance.

Past Medical History: Followed for hypothyroidism. No renal insufficiency. Echocardiogram without inter ventricular communication.

Physical Exam: Global hypotonia. Palate of normal width, without narrowing. Well-formed, without microtia.

findings.text: fifth digits straight, without deviation towards the hallux
right lung with only two lobes

translation:
Identification: female patient, brought by her parents for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: referred for investigation of malformation findings.

History of present illness: The parents report that from an early age they noticed that the daughter’s chin is small and receding. They bring previous imaging studies.

Physical exam: micrognathia. Feet with fifth digits straight, without deviation towards the hallux.

Complementary exams: Abdominal ultrasound with kidney in ectopic position. Cranial MRI showing enlarged ventricles; cerebellum of preserved volume, without hypoplasia; corpus callosum with normal thickness, without tapering. Chest CT showing right lung with only two lobes; ribs without fusion. Echocardiogram without tetralogy of Fallot.

findings.text: narrow thorax in the lateral-lateral direction

translation:
Identification: male patient, 20 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that shortly after birth he had significant difficulty breathing, requiring care in the neonatal intensive care unit. He was operated on for pyloric stenosis hypertrophy in the first few weeks of life. He reports that to this day he gets tired and has difficulty breathing, straining to get air.

Physical Exam: Narrow thorax in the lateral-lateral direction, without a bell shape. Spine without lumbar scoliosis.

Complementary Examinations: Chest X-ray shows short ribs and only 11 pairs of ribs, without thoracic dysplasia. Previous imaging describes pulmonary hypoplasia. Echocardiogram without structural cardiac abnormalities.

findings.text: small, rhythmic, upward movements of his arms

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by his mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child has always been delayed in everything compared to other children in the first years of life. He walked much later than expected. He started speaking very late and his speech is still quite poor to this day. He presents with severe intellectual disability, dependent on daily activities. The mother noticed that he shakes his hands and trunk repeatedly, without apparent purpose. She also noticed that his head became small with growth, although it was normal at birth. He has epilepsy with various types of seizures: episodes in which he stops what he is doing, with a fixed stare and small, rhythmic, upward movements of his arms; repetitive rhythmic shaking seizures; and bilateral generalized tonic-clonic seizures with generalized onset.

Physical Exam: Short stature. Microcephaly. Wide-set eyes. Esotropia. Hands have normal length and thickness, without arachnodactyly. Tendon reflexes are not brisk. Gait without instability.

Complementary Examinations: Abdominal ultrasound without dilation of intra-hepatic bile ducts. Liver elastography without fibrosis.

findings.text: increased range of motion in joints

translation:
Identification: girl, 9 years old, brought by her mother, referred by the pediatrician for evaluation in medical genetics.

History of Present Illness: mother reports that the daughter delayed reaching all developmental milestones as a child. She began speaking words and phrases much later than other children. She also had difficulty holding a pencil, buttoning clothes, and picking up small objects with her fingers. She has a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder and ADHD made by a neuropediatrist. Psychological assessment concluded intellectual deficit.

Past History: Prior renal ultrasound showed duplication of the renal pelvocal system. Echocardiogram without inter ventricular communication. Brain MRI without cerebellar atrophy and with normal olfactory bulbs.

Physical Exam: elongated face, deep-set eyes, large ears. Normal forehead width. Normal pupil shape. High palate. Increased range of motion in joints. Flat feet bilaterally.

Identification: male patient, age not specified, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic by cardiology.

Chief complaint: "heart racing".

History of present illness: Patient reports episodes in which he feels his heart beating fast and accelerated in the chest. Denies a history of myocarditis.

Physical examination: No muscular dystrophy found on neuromuscular examination.

Complementary examinations: The echocardiogram brought by the patient shows hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, with hypertrophy of the interventricular septum. A 24-hour Holter monitor shows sinus bradycardia, first-degree AV block, and periods of second-degree AV block. No atrial flutter, ventricular tachycardia, or ventricular extrasystoles were recorded.

findings.text: loose, wrinkled, and drooping skin with little elasticity
scoliosis on examination of the spine

translation:
Identification: female patient, 19 years old, accompanied by her mother, referred for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that in childhood the daughter delayed achieving all developmental milestones. She only managed to sit alone much later than other children and began walking late. She also delayed saying her first words and forming sentences. In school age, neuropsychological evaluation revealed moderate intellectual disability, without criteria for severe degree. Several years ago she stopped walking, although previously she used to walk. She presents with episodes in which she remains stationary, disengaged from the environment and does not respond when called; denies episodes with rigidity and generalized convulsions. She refers to episodes in which she has difficulty breathing and feels tired. She has had many ear infections throughout her life. Denies difficulty with feeding. Mother denies that the daughter is overly agitated or restless. Denies fever.

Physical Exam: Loose, wrinkled, and drooping skin with little elasticity. Global hypotonia. Hypermobility of joints. Scoliosis on examination of the spine.

Complementary Examinations: Pelvic radiographs with hip dislocation.

findings.text: does not present unilateral cleft lip

translation:
Identification: female patient, brought by her mother for the first consultation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by pediatrics.

Chief complaint: "delay in learning things."

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the daughter took longer than other children to sit, crawl, and walk. She also refers to significant learning difficulties and lack of autonomy in daily activities, with a previous assessment indicating intellectual disability. In developmental assessment, there is a global moderate delay of development, without a severe global delay.

Past Medical History: No prior interatrial communication. No aortic root aneurysm.

Physical Exam: Head circumference without mild microcephaly. Does not present unilateral cleft lip.

findings.text: increased spacing between the hallux and second toe bilaterally
brain MRI with reduction of the volume of white matter

translation:
Identification: boy, 13 years old, brought by his mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for investigation of developmental delay.

History of Present Illness: Mother reports that he took a very long time to sit alone and also started walking much later than his siblings. The first words and phrases came late. In the overall assessment, he presents with moderate developmental delay neuropsicomotor. He has a diagnosis of ADHD made by the school and health team and of mental health. He still needs help with bathing, dressing, and feeding. Mother denies that he has fallen below the expected weight gain and growth. She reports that he walks with firmness, without imbalance.

Physical Exam: Narrow forehead, prominent nasal root, short philtrum, retropositioned jaw and wide chin. Long fingers. Increased spacing between the hallux and second toe bilaterally. Eyes aligned, without esotropia. No dystonic postures. Normal tendon reflexes, without hyperreflexia.

Complementary Examinations: EEG with interictal changes. Brain MRI with reduction of the volume of white matter.

Identification: female patient, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: visual alterations and difficulty hearing.

History of present illness: the family reports that the patient does not hear well, needing them to speak louder and repeat the phrases. They also noted from an early age that the girl with the eyes has a different shape, resembling a lock mechanism hole.

Past medical history: prior renal and urinary tract ultrasound shows both kidneys present, without unilateral renal agenesis.

Physical exam: on the ophthalmic examination, iris coloboma. Fundoscopy reveals choroidoretinal coloboma and optic disc coloboma. At biomicroscopy, posterior subcapsular cataract.

findings.text: decreased muscle strength in the distal portions of the four limbs
atrophy of the distal musculature of the limbs
reduced amplitude of compound muscle action potentials

translation:
Identification: male, 50 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: difficulty with walking.

History of present illness: patient reports having progressive difficulty walking. He also reports fatigue and weakness throughout the body, a generalized sensation of lack of strength. Denies generalized seizures.

History: According to the family, there was no delay in neurodevelopmental development in childhood. No intellectual disability.

Physical exam: altered gait. Decreased muscle strength in the distal portions of the four limbs. Atrophy of the distal musculature of the limbs. Deep tendon reflexes abolished globally. Tone without spasticity. Coordination tests without ataxia.

Complementary exams: electromyography with reduced amplitude of compound muscle action potentials.

translation:
Identification: male, 35 years old, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: weakness in the hands and feet.

History of present illness: patient reports progressive difficulty buttoning clothes and holding small objects, as well as tripping frequently due to inability to raise the toes. Reports that hands tremble when holding a cup or keeping arms extended. Noticed that the hands and legs are thinner. Noticed that the foot has a very arched sole, even when standing.

Physical examination: gait without spastic pattern. Cavus feet bilaterally. Atrophy of the intrinsic muscles of the hands and distal atrophy of the legs. Strength grade 4 in distal musculature of the upper extremities and distal paresis in the lower extremities. Postural tremor in the upper extremities. Achilles tendon reflexes abolished (not just hypoactive). Biceps and triceps reflexes without exaggeration. No Babinski sign. Hypoesthesia and diminished tactile sensation in the lower extremities.

Complementary examinations: electromyography with reduced amplitude of sensitive action potentials and reduced amplitude of compound muscle action potentials.

findings.text: head circumference within the normal range

translation:
Identification: woman, 26 years old, accompanied by her mother.

Chief complaint: referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation of global developmental delay.

History of present illness: the mother reports that the daughter was very delayed in sitting and walking, significantly behind other children. She also started speaking her first words and forming sentences much later than expected. In childhood, she was extremely restless, impulsive, and unable to maintain attention on school tasks, having received a diagnosis of ADHD. She has intellectual disability, with the need for support in daily activities. The mother denies repetitive behaviors, social isolation, or restricted interests. She also denies nervousness, excessive worry, or panic attacks.

Physical examination: height appropriate for age and sex. Head circumference within the normal range, without microcephaly. On neurological examination, spasticity.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI with corpus callosum thickening. Interictal EEG without abnormalities.

findings.text: episodes of stiffness followed by rhythmic thrashing
short stature for age and sex

translation:
Identification: Female patient, 17 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: Referred by neurology for investigation.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the daughter was born with a small head, already measured below the expected at birth. Since the first few months, she noticed that she took a very long time to hold her head, sit, and speak, with significant delays in all acquisitions. She reports episodes in which the daughter becomes stiff and then begins to thrash with both sides of her body, in a rhythmic manner. Previous neuropsychological evaluation revealed intellectual disability.

Physical exam: Short stature for age and sex; does not present elevated stature. Wide mouth. Spastic tetraparesis.

Complementary examinations: Cranial MRI shows areas of hypodensity and areas of hyperdensity. Arborized body present, without agenesis.

findings.text: scoliosis on inspection of the spine

translation:
Identification: Male, 27 years old, referred to the neurology genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Imbalance while walking."

History of present illness: Patient reports that he is stumbling, with his legs apart, and has a tendency to fall. His mother, who accompanies him, reports that he has always been very clumsy, frequently dropping objects and bumping into furniture. He also reports that his speech is slurred and difficult to understand. The family has noticed that his head is swaying forward and backward.

Physical examination: Esotropia on ocular examination. Speech is dysarthric. Gait is ataxic. Scoliosis is noted on inspection of the spine.

Complementary examinations: Patient-brought cranial MRI reveals cerebellar hypoplasia.

findings.text: head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex

translation:
Identification: girl, 6 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics for genetic evaluation.

Chief complaint: “very sensitive skin to the sun”.

History of present illness: The mother reports that since early childhood, the child has an exaggerated reaction to the sun, with redness in exposed areas even after short periods outdoors. She also reports that the daughter is uncomfortable with brightness, closing her eyes and avoiding illuminated environments. She states that she falls down frequently while playing. At school, the teacher observes difficulty in learning; a previous psychological assessment indicated mild intellectual disability.

Past medical history: Born small for gestational age. Mild global delay in neurodevelopment: walked independently late and the first words and phrases took a long time to emerge, persisting delay in speech and language.

Physical examination: Head circumference below -2 SD for age and sex. Height appropriate for age. Erythema on face and dorsum of hands. Multiple lentigines in sun-exposed areas. Scars on face and forearms. Skin without dryness, without ichthyotic scaling. Nails of normal appearance.

Complementary examinations: Complete blood count without leukopenia.

findings.text: cortical thickening of the diaphyses of the long bones

translation:
Identification: male, 17 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: short stature.

History of present illness: The mother reports that the son has always been smaller than his peers of the same age, with a small body in a harmonious manner. She also reports that since childhood he was “soft,” with a loose body when picked up in the arms. She noticed that one of his eyelids droops more than the other. Denies glaucoma.

Physical examination: Short stature proportionate, without shortening of the lower limbs. Oval face, not triangular. Wide forehead. Prominent nose. Thick and dense eyebrows, without sinofris. Generalized muscle hypotonia. Hands with short middle phalanges, without syndactyly.

Complementary examinations: Brain MRI with enlarged magna cistern. Skeletal radiographs showing cortical thickening of the diaphyses of the long bones and cone epiphyses in the hands.

findings.text: bilateral crystalline opacity on ocular inspection
elastic hypertonia with hyperreflexia in the limbs
abnormal postures sustained with limb and trunk torsion

translation:
Identification: male, 16 years old, accompanied by the mother, referred to medical genetics.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the son used to walk, but several years ago he stopped being able to walk and today he depends on a wheelchair. He reports seizures of two types: some start with tremors in one side of the body and others already begin with loss of consciousness and tremors in the four limbs. He frequently complains of headaches. The mother notes that he has difficulty coordinating movements when performing tasks such as dressing. Denies tinnitus in the ears. No episodes of alternating between euphoria and depression.

findings.text: muscle strength is grade V globally
deep tendon reflexes are exaggerated in all four limbs
reduction in volume of white matter in the brain

translation:
Identification: Female adolescent, 16 years old, brought by her mother for evaluation in the medical genetics outpatient clinic, referred by neurology.

The mother denies repetitive behaviors, rituals, or restricted interests. According to the mother, the daughter is not shy, approaches others naturally.

findings.text: generalized tonic-clonic epileptic seizures with bilateral involvement

translation:
Identification: girl, 10 years and 6 months, brought in by her mother, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

She also reports that she sat and walked much later than other children. To date, the daughter has never spoken any words. She presents with generalized tonic-clonic epileptic seizures since the beginning, with bilateral involvement. The mother denies that the child is excessively agitated or restless. findings.text: one extra digit on the side of the fifth finger, bilaterally

translation:
Identification: Male neonate, 5 days of life, evaluated in the neonatal ICU at the request of the team for genetic evaluation.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that shortly after birth, the infant “became stiff,” with arms and legs difficult to bend. It evolved with convulsive crises and with respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. It is being used with a nasogastric tube for feeding, as he cannot suck. The team refers prolonged neonatal jaundice. The parents report that the skin never became cyanotic.

Complementary Exams: Hyperbilirubinemia. EEG with interictal epileptiform activity.

findings.text: seeing people and animals inside the house

absent: diminished reflexes in the upper extremities
translation:
Identification: Female patient, 76 years old, brought by her daughter, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: "Stopped walking."

History of present illness: The daughter reports that the mother began to walk unsteadily, swaying, and over time was unable to walk, currently restricted to a wheelchair. She also noted that the patient’s speech became slurred, drawn-out. She reports that the patient is more nervous, easily irritated by anything, and sometimes says she sees people and animals inside the house that no one else sees. The family noticed that her head is swaying unintentionally. Denies tremor in the hands, arms, or legs.

Deep tendon reflexes in the upper extremities not diminished. In the lower extremities, reflexes without hyperreflexia or hyporeflexia.

Identification: girl, 4 years old, brought by her mother, referred by pediatrics to the medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: “she is losing what she already knew how to do.”

History of Present Illness: Mother reports that the daughter was developing and began to lose previously acquired skills. She also reports that the child turns her entire head instead of moving her eyes to look at something to the side. She also noted small, rapid, involuntary movements in the arms and body, sometimes at rest, sometimes when trying to pick up objects. She presented with generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

Physical exam: Unstable gait, with widened base and dysmetria to grasp objects. Oculomotor apraxia. Palpable enlarged spleen.

Complementary exams: Hemogram with leukopenia and anemia; platelet count within the normal range. Myleogram brought by the family describes Gaucher cells.

Identification: Male, 31 years old, referred to the medical genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: Referred due to alterations in laboratory tests.

History of present illness: Patient presented for investigation after routine tests showed elevated serum CK above the upper limit of normal on repeated dosages.

Additional examinations: Manovacuometria with reduced PImáx and reduced PEmáx. Echocardiogram without evidence of cardiomyopathy. Chest X-ray in PA with normal cardiac index, without cardiomegaly.

findings.text: areas of skin without color on the face
areas of skin without color on the trunk
areas of skin without color on the limbs
membranous skin crease in both axillae

contracture in flexion of both wrists

translation:
Identification: male infant, 3 months, brought by parents for evaluation in medical genetics.

Chief complaint: “white patches on the skin and white hair”.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that since birth, the baby has areas of skin without color, on the face, trunk, and limbs, which have not changed. She also noticed that the eyebrows and eyelashes are completely white and that there are already several gray hairs, which she found strange for the age. translation:
Identification: female patient, referred to the endocrinology/genetics outpatient clinic for evaluation.

Chief complaint: absence of menstruation and excessive hair growth.

History of present illness: patient reports that she has not had a menstrual period for more than six months. She also reports the growth of coarse hairs in the chin, jaw, nipple area, and abdominal line, which greatly bother her. She has also noticed dark, velvety patches on her neck and axillae.

Physical examination: hirsutism in the face, thorax, and abdomen. Hyperpigmented, thickened, and velvety plaques in the posterior cervical region and axillae, suggestive of acanthosis nigricans.

Complementary examinations: pelvic ultrasound with bilateral polycystic ovaries. Elevated fasting insulinemia. Oral glucose tolerance test with glucose intolerance. Laboratory evaluation indicative of insulin resistance. Serum androgen levels with elevated serum androgens. Skin biopsy of the lesion in the cervical region showing acanthosis of the epidermis.

translation:
Identification: boy, 10 years old, brought by his mother for evaluation in a medical genetics outpatient clinic.

Chief complaint: skin and hair changes since birth.

History of Present Illness: The mother reports that the child was born with red, scaly skin all over the body, a condition that has persisted to this day. She also reports that after sun exposure, the skin becomes red and irritated easily. She states that the hair has always been rough to the touch. She has also noted that two teeth are missing in the front, next to the central incisors of the upper teeth. Good school performance, without intellectual disability.

Physical exam: Non-bullous congenital ichthyosis with erythrodermia. Absence of upper lateral incisors. Height appropriate for age, without short stature. Fundoscopy: pigment epithelial detachment of the retina.

Additional tests: Elevated serum IgE. Polarized light microscopy of hair strand with tiger stripe pattern.
